issues.title: VM parity follow-up: trace-aware compilation (16.3) and interp-arena ownership for full cross-interp alias parity (16.2)
issues.body:
Follow-up to the M16 VM-parity work on the #923 name-resolution plan (`docs/design/name-resolution-fix-plan.md`, M16). Both stages are **done per their plan definitions** — alias-loop prevention, child→parent/parent→child aliases, command + execution traces, all tclsh8.6/9.0-pinned — but each carries a deliberate, tested architecture boundary where full C-Tcl parity needs a deeper rearchitecture than the stages called for. This ticket tracks those two projects.

## 1. Step traces on compiled-inline commands (16.3)

**Today:** `enterstep`/`leavestep` fire for every *dispatched* command (procs, non-inlined builtins) with C-faithful `{cmd-string code result op}` shapes. Commands the compiler lowers to inline opcodes (`set`, `incr`, `return`, …) never reach the dispatcher, so they do not step.

**C Tcl:** attaching an execution trace forces the traced proc out of bytecode entirely; every inner command — transitively, including nested proc bodies — steps. tclsh8.6-verified:

```
proc st args { puts "S:[join $args |]" }
proc stepped2 {} { helperp }
proc helperp {} { return H }
trace add execution stepped2 {enterstep leavestep} st
stepped2
→ S:helperp|enterstep
  S:return H|enterstep
  S:return H|2|H|leavestep
  S:helperp|0|H|leavestep
```

The VM prints only the `helperp` pair (its `return H` is an inline opcode).

**Pinned by:** `rust/tcl-vm/tests/command_traces_e2e.rs::step_traces_observe_dispatched_commands_only_vm_divergence` — any engine change here shows up as a conscious test update, not silent drift.

**What closing it takes:** trace-aware compilation — when a step trace attaches to a proc, recompile (or re-enter) its body in a no-inline mode so every inner command routes through `dispatch_words`, and invalidate on trace removal (C's compile-epoch bump). Touches the `CompileService` seam, per-proc body caching, and the step-scope stack already in place (`Vm::exec_step_scopes`).

## 2. Cross-interp aliases beyond the one-level ownership tree (16.2)

**Today:** parent→child aliases dispatch directly; child→parent aliases suspend the child's whole activation stack (`YieldReq::ParentCall` under `DriveMode::ChildHosted`) and the parent's pump loop executes the target at its current frame from its global namespace — `info level` stacking, `uplevel 1` visibility, and catchable error propagation all tclsh-pinned (`rust/tcl-vm/tests/cross_interp_alias_e2e.rs`), with loop prevention walking across the boundary in both directions.

Three tested boundaries remain, all consequences of children being **owned** by their parent (`Vm.children: HashMap<String, Vm>`) rather than living in a shared arena like C's per-thread interp registry:

- a parent-target alias reached across a **native re-entry** (coroutine resume, `lsort -command`, an `invoke_command` re-entry) cannot suspend across the Rust stack and errors `cannot invoke parent-interp alias: C stack busy` — the same boundary `yield` has;
- the interp tree is **not re-entrant**: a parent-side target that re-enters the currently-suspended child gets a clean could-not-find error (C interps are freely re-entrant);
- **sibling↔sibling** child aliases (and deeper `interp` paths generally — C addresses arbitrary `{a b c}` paths) are rejected.

**What closing it takes:** move interp ownership into a shared arena (e.g. `Rc<RefCell<VmInner>>` with the root wrapped too, or an id-keyed slab with a per-"process" registry) so any interp can evaluate into any other without `&mut` exclusivity, then generalise `interp` path resolution to multi-level paths. The suspension trampoline can stay as the fast path; the arena removes the re-entrancy and topology limits.

## Context

- Plan: `docs/design/name-resolution-fix-plan.md` § M16 (stages 16.2/16.3 record these limits inline).
- Implementation: the M16 commit on the #923 follow-up branch (`claude/nifty-pasteur-2bq56k`).
- All current behaviour — including the divergences — is executable-pinned against real tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4.

issues.title: Follow-up to #933/#937/#938: resolution model is unsound across control flow, source views, interpreters, and TclOO
issues.body:
## Scope

Holistic review of merged PRs #933, #937, and #938 at their combined tip `6f9caba8d5f14fca68af739a69166d0d006c60f0` (base before the series: `14e19cfc2`). The review treated C Tcl 9 as the default truth oracle and explicitly used the Homebrew Tcl 9 executable on this Mac:

```text
/opt/homebrew/opt/tcl-tk/bin/tclsh9.0
info patchlevel = 9.0.3
```

The three PRs are interdependent and should be fixed as one analyser/compiler/LSP resolution-model follow-up. The master plan currently says “COMPLETE. All 16 milestones (every stage) are landed with tests”, but M14 is itself marked “MOSTLY DONE”, and the confirmed faults below show that the analyser/compiler/LSP completeness claim is not supportable. Backend/codegen/runtime findings were split into #946.

## Executive summary

The shared literal command-resolution vectors are good, and the explicitly pinned Tcl 9 oracle suites pass. The failures occur around identity, control flow, interpreter domains, source views, and TclOO dispatch—surfaces that cannot be represented faithfully by a flat qualified-name map or a flow-insensitive lexical walk.

Confirmed faults:

1. Rename of a constant command stored in a scalar deliberately leaves the command-name literal stale and produces broken Tcl.
2. Constant indirect dispatch is flow-insensitive and selects the lexically last branch assignment as if it were unconditional.
3. A file sourced into multiple namespaces is one physical declaration with multiple runtime identities, but declaration-side navigation arbitrarily chooses the first namespace.
4. Cross-file TclOO go-to-definition resolves externally unexported methods that C Tcl rejects.
5. Per-object methods are keyed only by the receiver variable’s simple tail, so unrelated objects in different scopes collide.
6. Cross-file TclOO go-to-definition returns an entire override family instead of resolving the actual call-chain entry.
7. Safe/sub-interpreter command visibility is not modelled; hidden commands are analysed as callable.
8. The new `interp eval` model is a synthetic namespace approximation, not an interpreter model, and misses multi-word scripts, interpreter existence, safe state, aliases, hidden commands, and interpreter-relative identity.
9. Command probes such as `namespace which -command` intentionally have no navigation reference because the reference role conflates “reference” with “must exist”.

## Oracle and project tests run

The canonical resolver was checked against Homebrew Tcl 9 explicitly:

```sh
TCL_LSP_TCLSH=/opt/homebrew/opt/tcl-tk/bin/tclsh9.0 \
  cargo test -p tcl-syntax --test command_resolution_conformance -- --nocapture
```

Both canonical resolver tests passed. Additional analyser/LSP review regressions and Tcl oracle programs are documented under each finding. Relevant logs:

- `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-command-resolution.log`
- `/tmp/pr933-938-vm-resolution.log`
- `/tmp/pr933-937-938-workspace.log`

A workspace run reached the server e2e suite with 881 passing tests. Its sole failure was the expected version-string `.dirty` mismatch caused by temporary review-only regression tests in the detached worktree; it is not a product finding.

## 1. P0: constant-command rename knowingly emits broken Tcl

The existing test `rename_never_rewrites_the_const_cmd_dispatch_span_m7` expects edits only on the proc declaration and direct call:

```tcl
proc target {} { return hi }
set cmd target
$cmd
target
```

Renaming `target` to `renamed` leaves `set cmd target` unchanged. The test comment even acknowledges that the variable value still names the old proc. The correct non-corrupting edit is to rewrite the literal value token, not the `$cmd` head.

Actual result of the currently expected edit under Homebrew Tcl 9:

```tcl
proc renamed {} {return hi}
set cmd target
$cmd
```

```text
broken-edit=1 msg=invalid command name "target"
```

Changing the value to `set cmd renamed` returns `hi`.

Root cause: `ConstDispatchSite` carries the indirect head span but discards the defining constant’s source span already available in `const_strings`. The design treats “do not replace `$cmd`” as equivalent to “do not preserve the dispatch”.

Required fix: command identity facts must retain provenance. A proven constant command value should produce:

- a read-only indirect invocation at `$cmd`;
- a writable command-name reference at each contributing literal definition;
- no writable reference when the value has no exact source representation.

Do not special-case `set` in consumers. Add a registry-level/value-provenance descriptor and carry it through the compiler fact model.

Required tests:

- TP: scalar literal assignment is rewritten and the renamed script executes under Tcl 9.
- FP: `$cmd` itself is never replaced.
- TN: dynamic/computed value without an exact source span abstains.
- FN: namespace-qualified and list-prefix command values retain their exact writable component.
- LSP e2e and VS Code rename tests must apply the workspace edit and execute the resulting Tcl with Tcl 9.

Review oracle log: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-const-dispatch-rename.txt`.

## 2. P0: indirect command constants are not control-flow sound

Reproducer:

```tcl
proc foo {} {return foo}
proc bar {} {return bar}
set cmd foo
if {$runtime} {
    set cmd bar
}
$cmd
```

C Tcl 9:

```text
runtime=0 target=foo
runtime=1 target=bar
```

A temporary regression against `Analyser` fails because the analyser records only `::bar`:

```text
runtime-dependent dispatch must abstain:
SignatureCommandInvocation {
  name: "bar",
  resolved_qualified_name: Some("::bar"),
  indirect: true,
  ...
}
```

The plan says the compiler’s SSA/SCCP result is already available, but Stage 7.2 uses the lexical `const_strings` map instead. That map is path-insensitive and mutates while recursively walking conditional bodies, so the last visited assignment wins regardless of runtime control flow. The same class of error applies to loops, `catch`, `try`, callbacks, `uplevel`, traces, and conditional command-environment mutations.

Required redesign: query the compiler’s program-point value lattice for the command head. Use exact `Const`, finite `ConstSet`, and Unknown/Overdefined:

- `Const(foo)`: one possible target;
- `ConstSet(foo, bar)`: both may-targets, with provenance for each source literal;
- Unknown/Overdefined: abstain;
- never collapse a branch join to the lexically last write.

The fact must be attached at the command’s program point and flow through SSA/MemorySSA as appropriate. Do not add command-name string checks.

Required TP/FP/TN/FN tests must cover `if`, `switch`, loops, `catch`/`try`, proc arguments, array/dict dispatch, and writes reachable through `upvar`/traces.

Project regression log: `/tmp/pr933-938-review-conditional-dispatch.log`.
Tcl oracle log: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-conditional-dispatch.txt`.

## 3. P0: multi-seed `source` arbitrarily loses runtime identities

Reproducer shape:

```tcl
# b.tcl
proc helper {} {namespace current}

# a.tcl
namespace eval ::x {source b.tcl}
namespace eval ::y {source b.tcl}
::x::helper
::y::helper
```

Homebrew Tcl 9 proves that the one physical declaration creates both commands:

```text
x=::x y=::y commands=::x::helper ::y::helper
```

The workspace index correctly creates multiple seeded views, but `seed_mapped_symbol` returns the first seed for a declaration-side query. A temporary regression expected both callers and received only line 2 (`::x::helper`), losing line 3 (`::y::helper`):

```text
left: {2}
right: {2, 3}
```

This also makes rename unsafe. Editing the one physical declaration changes every sourced runtime identity, even if the query was arbitrarily mapped to only one seed. References, rename, definition, call hierarchy, and diagnostics need a one-source-to-many-runtime-symbol model.

Required redesign:

- represent a source document as physical syntax plus a set of execution views;
- map a declaration cursor to a set of symbol identities, never the first sorted seed;
- references may union all exact views;
- rename must either update the physical token with an explicit multi-symbol result or abstain when the requested operation purports to rename only one runtime identity;
- include repeated sourcing, global + namespaced sourcing, transitive sourcing, conditional sourcing, cycles, `source -encoding`, computed paths, and safe-interpreter hidden `source`.

Project regression: `/tmp/pr933-938-review-multi-seed-source.log`.
Tcl oracle: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-multi-seed-source.txt`.

## 4. P1: cross-file TclOO ignores export visibility

Reproducer:

```tcl
oo::class create Vault {
    method _secret {} {return hidden}
}
set v [Vault new]
$v _secret
```

C Tcl 9:

```text
methods=destroy
call=1 msg=unknown method "_secret": must be destroy
```

The LSP’s cross-file go-to-definition returns `Vault::_secret` anyway. Temporary regression:

```text
an externally unexported TclOO method is not callable:
[Location { uri: file:///vault.tcl, line: 1, ... }]
```

The workspace index reduces methods to `Vec<String>`, losing instance/class-object kind, export state, definition order, and MRO contribution. TclOO visibility is mutable via `export`/`unexport`, and per-object visibility also matters.

Required redesign: registry-described TclOO member effects should feed a typed method table carrying owner, receiver kind, export state, declaration span, definition order, and MRO role. External `$obj m`, internal `my m`, class-object calls, forwards, filters, mixins, per-object methods, and `next`/`nextto` must use different access contexts.

Required TP/FP/TN/FN tests:

- lowercase/default-exported external call;
- underscore/uppercase default-unexported external call;
- explicit `export` and `unexport`;
- internal `my` call to unexported method;
- inherited/mixin/per-object visibility;
- cross-file LSP e2e + VS Code definition/references/rename.

Project regression: `/tmp/pr933-938-review-unexported-method.log`.
Tcl oracle: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-unexported-method.txt`.

## 5. P1: per-object methods collide by variable tail across scopes

Reproducer:

```tcl
oo::class create C {}

proc a {} {
    set o [C new]
    oo::objdefine $o {method m {} {return a}}
    $o m
}
proc b {} {
    set o [C new]
    oo::objdefine $o {method m {} {return b}}
    $o m
}
```

C Tcl 9 returns:

```text
a=a b=b
```

The analyser stores `object_methods: HashMap<String, Vec<MethodDef>>` keyed only by the receiver’s simple name. Both unrelated locals are `o`; `lookup_object_method` takes the first matching method. Go-to-definition for `b` therefore jumps to `a`’s method:

```text
b's distinct object override:
left target line 3
expected line 8
```

Required redesign: use binding/object identity, not textual variable tail. Carry the compiler’s resolved variable/place identity and an object-value lattice to objdefine and call sites. Alias propagation (`set p $o`, proc parameters, returns, containers, `upvar`) should preserve a finite object set where provable and abstain otherwise. Per-object method state belongs to the abstract object identity and interpreter domain.

Required tests: same tail in different scopes (FP), alias of same object (TP), two possible objects after a branch (finite-set FN), object recreated/reassigned (TN), namespace variables, `upvar`, and cross-file consumers. Add core, native LSP e2e, and VS Code coverage.

Project regression: `/tmp/pr933-938-review-objdefine-scope.log`.
Tcl oracle: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-objdefine-scope.txt`.

## 6. P1: go-to-definition returns the override component, not the dispatch entry

With `Animal::speak` overridden by `Dog::speak`, a `Dog` instance enters `Dog::speak`. C Tcl 9:

```text
result=dog
Dog.call={method speak ::Dog method} {method speak ::Animal method}
```

`cross_file_method_definition` calls `method_override_family` and returns every definer. A consumer-file query returned both Animal and Dog, while a definition request should identify the runtime entry (and optionally expose the remaining call chain through a separate hierarchy UI):

```text
go-to-definition must select Dog::speak only:
[animal.tcl, dog.tcl]
```

The current “weakly-connected component of definers” is not a TclOO method resolution order. It also unions superclass and mixin edges and does not model filters, per-object mixins, class-object methods, visibility, or definition order.

Required redesign: compute a C-Tcl-faithful call chain for a receiver context. Go-to-definition selects the first applicable implementation. References/rename need an explicit policy and must not reuse a connectivity component merely because names match. `next` and `nextto` should navigate within the computed chain.

Project regression: `/tmp/pr933-938-review-override-definition.log`.
Tcl oracle: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-tcloo-override.txt`.

## 7. P1: safe interpreter command visibility is absent

C Tcl 9 safe interpreter proof:

```tcl
interp create -safe s
interp eval s {source nowhere.tcl}
```

```text
safe=1
source visible=0 hidden=1
load visible=0 hidden=1
file visible=0 hidden=1
socket visible=0 hidden=1
exec visible=0 hidden=1
cd visible=0 hidden=1
pwd visible=0 hidden=1
glob visible=0 hidden=1
open visible=0 hidden=1
source-call=1 msg=invalid command name "source"
```

`interp invokehidden s source ...` reaches the hidden command instead.

The analyser gives every `interp eval` body the parent document profile/registry, so it treats hidden unsafe commands as normally callable and can even build invalid source/package edges from them.

Required redesign: introduce an interpreter-domain graph with an `InterpreterProfile` derived from the dialect profile plus safe/hidden/exposed command state. Registry specs should carry safe-interpreter availability/capability metadata. `interp hide`, `expose`, `invokehidden`, aliases, child creation/deletion, and safe initialization mutate that domain at program points.

Tests must cover safe vs normal interpreters, hide/expose, invokehidden, aliases crossing domains, packages, source, IO/process/network commands, and dynamic interpreter paths. Add diagnostics, navigation, native LSP e2e, VS Code, and VM differential tests.

Oracle log: `/tmp/pr933-938-homebrew-tcl9-safe-interp.txt`.

## 8. P1: `interp eval` isolation is not an interpreter model

`handle_interp_eval_command` represents a child interpreter as `ScopeKind::Namespace` named from the path and homes child `::foo` as synthetic `::<path>::foo`. This prevents one parent collision but loses Tcl semantics:

- interpreter path is relative to the current interpreter, not a Tcl namespace;
- a non-existent literal child is still analysed as if execution succeeds;
- dynamic paths are converted into synthetic names;
- only exactly one script word is handled, although Tcl accepts `arg ?arg ...?` and concatenates them;
- safe state and hidden/exposed commands are ignored;
- separate evals, deletion/recreation, nested interpreters, and aliases require temporal identity;
- child global namespace `::` is not parent namespace `::child`;
- parent↔child aliases deliberately cross interpreter domains while definitions do not;
- `uplevel`/frame identity inside alias callbacks cannot be represented by a namespace scope.

The existing analyser test for isolation uses `interp eval child {...}` without creating `child`, which is not runnable Tcl and therefore cannot prove C fidelity.

Required redesign: use explicit `InterpreterId`, `NamespaceId`, and `FrameId` in resolution facts. Registry hooks should describe evaluation semantics generically (target interpreter operand, script-word concatenation, target namespace/frame, safe capability), rather than a command-name branch in compiler code.

## 9. P2: command probes cannot navigate

M14 admits that `namespace which -command NAME` is intentionally not a reference because `ArgRole::CommandName` also feeds W123. This is a model fault: reference identity and existence assertion are orthogonal.

Add a registry-level descriptor such as a typed command-reference role with:

- resolution context;
- required vs probe existence policy;
- invocation/callback arity policy;
- writable-on-rename policy;
- command-prefix provenance.

Use it for `namespace which -command`, `info commands` where statically exact, introspection, traces, ensemble maps, aliases, and future command-valued APIs. Consumers should not infer diagnostic semantics from a broad role.

Tests: existing target navigates; missing target produces no W123; dynamic/pattern probe abstains; rename rewrites only exact writable references.

## Cross-cutting architecture required

Do not patch these with command-name string checks. The general model should have:

1. **Typed execution domains:** interpreter, namespace, frame, safe capabilities, and lifecycle identity.
2. **Program-point environments:** command table, rename/alias/import links, namespace path/unknown handler, trace state, source/package state, and TclOO method state represented as lattices over CFG/SSA.
3. **Value provenance:** exact literals, finite constant sets, and unknown values with writable source spans distinct from invocation spans.
4. **Typed callable identity:** proc/alias/import/rename target, TclOO receiver kind, object identity, visibility, MRO call chain, and interpreter domain.
5. **One-to-many source views:** physical syntax separated from runtime symbol identities.
6. **Registry-owned semantics:** extend command/member/interpreter descriptors and typed hooks; generic consumers dispatch on descriptors, never command strings.
7. **Sound abstention:** when a finite exact set cannot be proved, avoid destructive rename and false single-target definition.

Use plain, idiomatic modern Rust. No new clippy allows.

## Required validation before closing

For every confirmed fault, add TP/FP/TN/FN at the deepest fact layer, provider tests, native `tcl-lsp-server/tests/*_e2e.rs`, and VS Code integration tests. Execute transformed rename outputs under Homebrew Tcl 9, not merely inspect edit ranges.

Also run the repository-mandated final gates on the exact fixed tree:

```sh
make prep-pr
make check-rust
make test-ext
make test-emacs
```

The issue should not be closed by weakening the “COMPLETE” wording alone; the confirmed corrupting/false-resolution analyser/compiler/LSP behaviours above require code fixes. Backend/codegen/runtime parity is tracked separately in #946.

issues.title: Backend/runtime follow-up to #933/#937/#938: cross-interpreter re-entry and step-trace parity
preview version :  The ::tcl::mathfunc namespace cannot find any references when functions are added in expr.
W123 doesn't fire for a call through a proc/class/alias/rename target deleted earlier in the file
Add dedicated hover/completion/call-hierarchy/minify/graph test coverage for expr math-function resolution
issues.body:
## Context

The `expr` math-function invocation-resolution fix (closing #968 and its follow-ups) corrected `resolved_qualified_name`/`resolution_candidates` for `sin(...)`/`max(...)`-style calls inside `expr`: namespace-local TIP 232 overrides, `namespace path`, and a collision bug where an unrelated same-named ordinary proc/class/alias/rename target could hijack a math-function call's resolved name. See `docs/design/tricky-name-resolution-surfaces.md` §1.6 for the full writeup.

Three consumers of those fields got dedicated end-to-end coverage as part of that work, each proving the fix reaches a real LSP feature and not just the underlying data:

- go-to-definition (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/definition.rs`: `no_definition_for_mathfunc_call_despite_unrelated_same_named_proc`, `mathfunc_call_jumps_to_namespace_local_override`)
- find-references (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/references.rs`: `references_do_not_cross_between_unrelated_proc_and_mathfunc_override`)
- rename (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/rename.rs`: `rename_mathfunc_override_updates_call_site_and_skips_unrelated_proc`)

## Gap

The same `resolved_qualified_name`/`resolution_candidates` fields on `SignatureCommandInvocation` also feed:

- hover (signature/documentation lookup for the call target)
- completion (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/completion.rs`)
- call hierarchy (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/call_hierarchy.rs`)
- minify (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/minify.rs`)
- the dependency graphs (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/graphs.rs`)
- linked editing ranges (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/linked_editing_range.rs`)

None of these has a dedicated test exercising a math-function call through the specific scenarios the fix addresses (namespace-local override, `namespace path`, or the unrelated-same-named-command collision). Their existing suites (1017+ tests across `tcl-lsp-core`/`tcl-lsp-db`) passed unmodified throughout the fix, which rules out a regression in the paths those suites already cover, but that's not the same as a test that specifically watches one of these features do the right thing with a math-function call in the tricky cases above.

## Suggested test shape

Mirror the pattern already used for the go-to-definition/references/rename tests: a namespace-local `proc ::ns::tcl::mathfunc::f` override alongside an unrelated ordinary `proc f` sharing the bare tail name, then assert the feature under test resolves/links to the override (not the unrelated proc) from inside the override's namespace, and to the unrelated proc's own definition when queried on *that* declaration directly. For hover specifically, also worth covering the "no override, real builtin" case — the hover text should come from the registry's math-function documentation, not silently show nothing or the wrong signature.

## Non-goals

This is a test-coverage gap, not a known defect — nothing above is reported as currently broken, only unverified by a dedicated test for this specific call shape.

issues.title: Interprocedural call-site literal seeding is unsound across dynamic dispatch (`$cmd args`)
issues.body:
## Background

Issue #969 ("I230 false positive") was caused by an unsound interprocedural constant-propagation seed in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs`: `collect_call_site_constants` / `params_constants_from_call_sites` treats a proc parameter as a compile-time literal whenever every call site the scan can *resolve* agrees on a value. The fix (PR #970) closed several concrete ways a real, varying call site could go unresolved and silently vanish from that evidence (namespace-blind resolution, `catch`/`uplevel` bodies, `TclOO` method bodies, `namespace import` aliasing).

## The gap

A call site dispatched through a variable — `set cmd helper; $cmd args` — is currently just skipped by the scan: it neither counts as evidence for nor against any proc's parameters, because its target can't be statically resolved. But `$cmd` could hold the exact name of a proc the scan has *already* (otherwise soundly) seeded from other, literal-looking call sites, making that seed silently unsound. Example shape:

```tcl
proc helper {mode} {
    if {$mode eq "prod"} { ... } else { ... }
}
helper prod
helper prod

set cmd helper
$cmd dev   ;# this call is invisible to the scan
```

Today, `helper`'s two literal `prod` calls seed `mode` as the constant `"prod"`, folding the condition — even though `$cmd dev` may also reach `helper` at runtime with a different value.

## Why this isn't fixed yet

A blanket fix was attempted during the #969 work ("any dynamic dispatch call site anywhere in the module disqualifies every seed in the module") and reverted: it broke a legitimate, already-covered true-positive test, `fp_var_as_cmd_param_flow_non_command_fires` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/fp/obj.rs` — a dispatch-table proc whose own body legitimately uses `$cmd` lost its own, unrelated, otherwise-sound seed as collateral damage.

## What to investigate

- Can a more targeted fix track which string literals are ever assigned to a variable that later reaches a dynamic command position, and disqualify only a proc whose name appears in that literal set — without a circular dependency on the SCCP result this seed itself feeds?
- If no precise per-proc fix is achievable without disproportionate complexity, what's the least-collateral-damage conservative alternative (if any is worth it)?

## Verification bar

Any fix here should include: a regression test that fails on the current code and passes after, and confirmation that `fp_var_as_cmd_param_flow_non_command_fires` (and the rest of `cargo test -p tcl-compiler --lib` plus `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`) still passes with no new clippy allows.

## References

- Root issue: #969
- Fix PR: #970 (see `docs/design/compiler/fp-audit-todo.md`, entry `FP-IPCP-01`, for the full history of this class of bug and what's already fixed)
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs` (`collect_call_site_constants`, `params_constants_from_call_sites`, `record_call_site_evidence`)

issues.title: Calls made only through a `CommandPrefix`-role argument (e.g. `trace add variable ... command`) are invisible to interprocedural call-site analysis
issues.body:
## Background

Issue #969 ("I230 false positive") traced to an unsound interprocedural constant-propagation seed in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs`. The fix (PR #970) made `collect_call_site_constants` recurse into `ArgRole::Body` arguments (registry-driven via `CommandRegistry::arg_indices_for_role`, re-segmented with `crate::segmenter`) so calls hidden inside `catch { ... }` / literal `uplevel { ... }` bodies are no longer invisible to the scan.

## The gap

The same scan does **not** follow `ArgRole::CommandPrefix` arguments — e.g. `trace add variable v write cb` or a `-command cb` option, where `cb` names a command to be invoked with extra trailing arguments at runtime, not a literal script to re-segment. A proc invoked only this way is a real caller whose (necessarily non-literal, since trailing args are appended at fire time) argument never gets counted as evidence, letting a coincidentally-uniform set of *other*, directly-resolved call sites wrongly seed the proc's parameters.

This is not a regression from #969/#970: the codebase's own general call-graph builder, `interprocedural::scan_source_for_calls` (used for taint/purity summaries), has the identical gap — it also only recurses into `ArgRole::Body`, never `ArgRole::CommandPrefix`. So this is a shared, pre-existing limitation across (at least) two consumers.

## What to investigate

What it would take to make both `collect_call_site_constants` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs`) and `interprocedural::scan_source_for_calls` recognise a `CommandPrefix` argument as a call site to the named command — resolved the same way a `Statement::Call`'s command word already is, via `crate::interprocedural::resolve_internal_call` — so a proc invoked only via `trace add variable ... command myProc` (or another `CommandPrefix`-tagged callback registration) is counted as a real caller. Use `CommandRegistry::arg_indices_for_role` / `CommandRegistry::command_prefixes` (already used elsewhere for this exact role) rather than hardcoding command names. Since this affects two consumers, decide whether to share one primitive between them or fix each independently, and record the reasoning either way.

## Related but distinct

#239 ("False W214 triggering in case of usage `[trace add variable]`") is about the W214 unused-parameter diagnostic's signature checking for `trace` callbacks — a different diagnostic and mechanism from the call-graph/interprocedural-seeding gap described here. Worth knowing about since it touches the same command shape, but not a duplicate.

## Verification bar

A reproduction (a proc whose only literal-looking external call disagrees with a value passed through a `CommandPrefix`-registered callback) and regression tests for both fixed consumers, with full-suite verification and no new clippy allows.

## References

- Root issue: #969
- Fix PR: #970 (see `docs/design/compiler/fp-audit-todo.md`, entry `FP-IPCP-01`)
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs` (`collect_call_site_constants`, `record_call_site_evidence`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/interprocedural.rs` (`scan_source_for_calls`)

issues.title: Investigate: does `namespace ensemble configure -map` redirection break interprocedural call-site resolution?
issues.body:
## Background

Issue #969 ("I230 false positive") traced to an unsound interprocedural constant-propagation seed in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs`. The fix (PR #970) made `collect_call_site_constants` / `params_constants_from_call_sites` resolve every call site via `crate::interprocedural::resolve_internal_call`, which now correctly handles plain namespace-relative resolution, `namespace import` aliasing (`resolve_via_namespace_import`), and forces the right namespace context for `TclOO` method bodies and `namespace eval` bodies.

## The potential gap

None of that resolution path has any knowledge of `namespace ensemble configure -map {subcmd targetProc ...}` — an ensemble command that redirects `mycmd subcmd args...` to an arbitrary target command, which can be a plain user proc. If a proc is invoked only via such a mapped ensemble subcommand, its call site would be invisible to the scan, potentially reproducing the same false-positive shape as #969.

## Important: this is unconfirmed, not a known bug

Unlike the other follow-ups from this investigation (see #976, #977, #978), this one has **not** been verified with a failing reproduction — it's a plausible gap based on reading the resolution code, not a confirmed defect. Please investigate before fixing:

1. Does the codebase already parse/track `namespace ensemble configure -map` anywhere (check the analyser, optimiser, and `interprocedural.rs`) — is there an existing fact this scan could reuse, the same way `resolve_via_namespace_import` reuses `ir::Module::namespace_imports`?
2. Write a minimal reproduction: a proc whose only "literal-looking" external call site is via an ensemble's mapped subcommand with a differing argument, and confirm whether `collect_call_site_constants` actually misses it today — don't assume; the other four follow-up issues from this investigation were each confirmed with a real `tclsh`-verified repro and a Rust test that fails before any fix, before writing a line of fix code.
3. If confirmed, fix analogously to `resolve_via_namespace_import`: a resolution fallback consulting whatever ensemble-map fact is available (existing or newly added at lowering time), with regression tests. If not confirmed as reachable in practice (e.g. because ensemble maps to plain procs are rare enough, or already excluded some other way), please report that finding plainly rather than fix a non-issue.

## References

- Root issue: #969
- Fix PR: #970 (see `docs/design/compiler/fp-audit-todo.md`, entry `FP-IPCP-01`)
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs` (`collect_call_site_constants`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/interprocedural.rs` (`resolve_internal_call`)

issues.title: `uplevel #0 { ... }` body resolves against the wrong namespace in interprocedural call-site analysis (confirmed, root cause identified)
Bare classmethod/object-command dispatch matching is namespace-blind (can cross-link the wrong class)
11 private ::tcl:: ensemble-backing sub-namespaces are undocumented and unmodeled
issues.body:
## Summary

Real Tcl uses a set of private, undocumented sub-namespaces under `::tcl::` to back built-in ensemble commands: `::tcl::dict`, `::tcl::string`, `::tcl::array`, `::tcl::file`, `::tcl::info`, `::tcl::clock`, `::tcl::binary`, `::tcl::namespace`, `::tcl::encoding`, `::tcl::zlib`, `::tcl::chan` (11 total).

Checked directly against real Tcl C source for all five releases this repo tracks (8.4.20, 8.5.19, 8.6.16, 9.0.4, 9.1b0):

- These namespaces are **100% undocumented** in Tcl's own documentation — one incidental, non-normative mention only, nothing that constitutes a documented public contract.
- Membership and even existence churn significantly across version boundaries: 6 of the 11 don't exist at all in 8.5.19; more appear by 8.6; the set is frozen between 9.0 and 9.1.
- They exist purely to back the corresponding ensemble command's ordinary public subcommands (e.g. `::tcl::dict::create` backs `dict create`) — calling into them directly is not a documented or supported usage pattern in any Tcl release.

This repo's registry/dialect model doesn't currently represent these namespaces at all — they're neither known-good nor flagged as suspicious if a script directly calls e.g. `::tcl::dict::create` instead of `dict create`.

## Why this probably isn't worth per-command modeling

Given how much the membership churns release-to-release, and that these are private implementation details rather than a documented surface, modeling each of the ~11 namespaces' individual subcommands with per-version dialect data (the way ordinary commands are modeled) would mean tracking undocumented internals across version boundaries indefinitely, for a usage pattern that isn't a supported or recommended way to write Tcl in the first place.

## Suggested direction

A lighter-weight, namespace-prefix-level diagnostic: flag direct calls into `::tcl::<any of the 11>::*` as "this is a private Tcl implementation namespace — use the public ensemble command instead" (e.g. suggest `dict create` in place of `::tcl::dict::create`), without needing to model each subcommand's individual dialect availability. This gives useful signal without taking on the maintenance burden of tracking internals that aren't part of Tcl's actual contract and that are already known to shift under version upgrades.

issues.title: Find References / Rename don't follow [incr Tcl]'s `Factory::make` class-proc dispatch at all
issues.body:
## Summary

[incr Tcl] (`itcl::class`) supports a class-scoped `proc` — its equivalent of TclOO's `classmethod` / snit's `typemethod` — but it's dispatched as a single `::`-qualified identifier (`Factory::make`), not the two-word `Factory make` shape TclOO/snit use. The object-method call-site scanner (`find_obj_method_call_sites` / `scan_obj_method_region` in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs`) only ever looks for the two-word shape, so an itcl class-proc's real dispatch site is never found by Find References, and never rewritten by Rename.

```tcl
itcl::class Factory {
    proc make {} {
        return 1
    }
}
Factory::make
```

Find All References on `make`'s declaration returns only the declaration itself — `Factory::make` is invisible. Renaming `make` leaves `Factory::make` pointing at the old, now-nonexistent name.

## Root cause

`Factory::make` is a single, `::`-namespace-qualified command-head token — structurally identical to a qualified proc call (`::ns::proc`), not an object-method dispatch. The object-method scanner (`scan_obj_method_region`) never considers this shape; it only recognizes a bare receiver word immediately followed by a separate method-name word. Meanwhile the *ordinary* proc-reference path (`proc_references` / `proc_reference_spans` in the same file) resolves qualified command names generically, but has no way to know that `Factory::make` should resolve to the itcl `ClassDef`'s `class_methods["make"]` entry rather than a plain `proc`.

## Current mitigation

The two-word scanner is explicitly guarded against *misfiring* on this shape (verified with a regression test, `fp_itcl_class_proc_colon_dispatch_not_confused_with_bare_dispatch` in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/tests/name_resolution.rs`), so `Factory::make` is at least never wrongly counted as a reference to something else. It's simply never resolved as a reference to the itcl proc it actually is.

## Suggested fix direction

Teach the qualified-name proc-reference resolution path (or a new small resolver alongside it) to recognize a `::`-qualified call whose immediate parent namespace matches a known itcl class's qualified name, and whose tail matches one of that class's `class_methods` entries — routing it to the same declaration/rename-family machinery `classmethod`/`typemethod` two-word dispatch already uses, rather than treating it as an ordinary unqualified proc.

## Related

- #981 (bare classmethod/object-command dispatch is namespace-blind) — a different itcl-adjacent gap in the same dispatch-matching area, but about the two-word shape's namespace precision, not this missing colon-qualified shape entirely.

issues.title: Method/classmethod code-lens click shows fewer references than Find All References on the same symbol (missing cross-file resolution)
Rename of a TclOO method/classmethod doesn't update call sites in pure-consumer documents (cross-file)
issues.body:
## Summary

Renaming a TclOO method or classmethod propagates to every document that *defines* the method (the override family) or *inherits* it (a subclass that doesn't override it), but not to a document that only *calls* it — a "pure consumer" that never declares or extends the class at all. That consumer document's call site is silently left pointing at the old, now-renamed name.

This is the rename analogue of a gap that Find References already closed: `cross_file_consumer_method_references` (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs`) exists specifically to find `$obj method` / bare classmethod-dispatch sites in a pure-consumer document via the workspace index's `documents_invoking_classes`, and reference-finding *does* correctly reach those sites. Rename has no equivalent.

## Root cause

`rename()`'s handler calls `cross_file_method_rename`, which computes its target document set from `index.method_override_family(...)` and `index.method_inheritor_classes(...)` only — the same two sets `cross_file_method_references` uses. There is no third call analogous to `cross_file_consumer_method_references`; `documents_invoking_classes` (the mechanism that finds pure-consumer documents) is used exactly once in the whole file, inside `cross_file_consumer_method_references`, and nowhere near the rename path.

## Repro

```tcl
// factory.tcl
oo::class create Factory {
    method make {} { return 1 }
}
```
```tcl
// consumer.tcl (sibling document, never declares/extends Factory)
set f [Factory new]
$f make
```

Renaming `make` from its declaration in `factory.tcl` produces an edit for `factory.tcl` only. `consumer.tcl`'s `$f make` call site is left unchanged, now calling a method that no longer exists under that name — a real, silent correctness break, not just an incomplete-but-safe omission (unlike most of the gaps in this area, which under-count references; this one actively leaves broken code behind).

## Suggested fix direction

Add a `cross_file_consumer_method_rename` (or fold the consumer document set into the existing `cross_file_method_rename`), mirroring `cross_file_consumer_method_references`'s approach: resolve the override family + inheritor set, use `documents_invoking_classes` to find consumer documents that construct/hold an instance of a family member, and for each one compute rewrite spans via the same `find_obj_method_call_sites_with_extra_cmd_names` (or equivalent) call the references path already uses — but producing `TextEdit`s instead of read-only locations.

issues.title: Find References / Rename / Code Lens use a weaker object-type map than the compiler's own interprocedural lattice
issues.body:
## Summary

The compiler already has a proper interprocedural object-type lattice — `object_handle_classes` / `object_collection_classes` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/object_types.rs` — that does real fixpoint propagation across aliasing, proc-return edges, proc-parameter edges, and constructor-parameter edges. It's consumed by `compilation_unit.rs`, `interprocedural.rs`, and `type_infer.rs` for compiler-internal analysis, and by `semantic_tokens.rs` for editor highlighting.

Find References, Rename, and Code Lens for TclOO object dispatch don't use it at all. They instead key off `analysis.instance_classes` — a much simpler single-pass map (visible directly in `find_obj_method_call_sites` / `method_target_with_access` / `classmethod_dispatch_class`, all in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/{references,rename,definition}.rs`), populated without the lattice's interprocedural propagation.

## Impact

Any object-typed variable whose class the *semantic-highlighting* pass can already infer via the richer lattice — because it flows through a proc return, a proc parameter, a constructor parameter, or a plain alias — but which the simpler `instance_classes` pass can't (because it's a strictly single-pass, non-fixpoint map) is invisible to Find References, Rename, and the code lens count for that class's methods, even though the same file's semantic tokens correctly color the variable's method calls as belonging to that class. The two features can visibly disagree on the same document: a method call token is highlighted as a TclOO dispatch, but right-clicking it and choosing "Find All References" doesn't recognize it as one.

## Suggested fix direction

Two possible directions, in increasing order of invasiveness:

1. Have the LSP-facing analysis populate (or replace) `instance_classes` from `object_handle_classes`'s output directly, so the two consumers agree by construction rather than by coincidence.
2. Have `find_obj_method_call_sites` and friends consult `object_handle_classes` themselves for cases `instance_classes` doesn't cover, as a fallback layer.

Either way, this is a proper unification, not a quick patch — `object_handle_classes` operates on `CompilationUnit`/CFG-level data the LSP's single-document `AnalysisResult` doesn't currently carry, so wiring it in means deciding how (or whether) to run the heavier interprocedural pass for LSP requests without regressing latency on large files.

## Related

- #927 (track widget-path variables to their widget type so `$w instate ...` resolves) is a different, narrower instance of the same underlying theme — extending object/instance-type inference precision for dispatch resolution — worth considering together when either is picked up.

issues.title: Call Hierarchy incoming/outgoing calls can't see `my method` dispatch or bare classmethod dispatch
issues.body:
## Summary

Call Hierarchy's Incoming Calls and Outgoing Calls (`method_incoming_calls` / `method_outgoing_calls` in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/call_hierarchy.rs`) resolve call sites inside a method/classmethod body by comparing a segmented command's own head word against the target member's bare name. This structurally cannot recognize the two dispatch shapes TclOO methods and classmethods actually use in practice — `my method` and bare `ClassName method` — because in both shapes the head word is never the member's own name.

Confirmed empirically for all four combinations (instance method × incoming/outgoing, classmethod × incoming/outgoing) with throwaway unit tests exercising `incoming_calls`/`outgoing_calls` directly; all four returned an empty result where a real call site existed.

## Root cause

`segment_body_calls` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/call_hierarchy.rs:224-263`) segments a method body into top-level commands and returns `cmd.argv.first()` — the command's own head word — for each one (`:252`, `:260`).

`method_incoming_calls` (`:642-677`) then matches with `if head != target_method.name { continue; }` (`:656`) — i.e. "does this command's head word literally equal the target method's name."

`method_outgoing_calls` (`:682-736`) matches the opposite direction with `class_def.methods.get(&head).or_else(|| class_def.class_methods.get(&head))` (`:697-700`) — i.e. "does this command's head word name some method/classmethod of the class."

Both only work when the command's head word *is* the member's own name — a bare, unqualified command literally spelled like the method (`greet`, `twice`). That shape is exercised by the only existing tests (`outgoing_calls_from_method_to_sibling_method`, `incoming_calls_for_method_grouped_by_caller_method`), both of which call a sibling method as a bare word with no receiver at all.

That bare-word-with-no-receiver shape is not how TclOO method/classmethod dispatch actually works, though. From inside a method body, calling a sibling method requires `my methodName` (head word is `my`, not the method name); a classmethod dispatch from outside — or a classmethod calling another classmethod of the same class — is `ClassName methodName` (head word is the class name, not the method name). A bare `greet` command in a method body only resolves at all in real Tcl if a same-named ordinary command/proc happens to exist in scope; it is not a `my`-less spelling of self-dispatch. So the one shape the existing tests cover is not TclOO's real dispatch syntax, while the two shapes that are real dispatch syntax are both unhandled.

Confirmed with `grep` that there is no handling of `"my"` anywhere in `call_hierarchy.rs`, and no classmethod-aware bare-dispatch resolution either (contrast with `references.rs`'s `find_obj_method_call_sites`, which explicitly scans for both `my method` sites via `scan_my_method_sites` and bare classmethod/object-command dispatch via `scan_obj_method_region`/`find_class_member_references` — none of that machinery is reused here).

## Repro

```tcl
oo::class create Bar {
    method getOptions {key} { return $key }
    method get {key} { return [my getOptions $key] }
}
```

- Incoming Calls on `getOptions`'s declaration: expected one caller (`get`, via `my getOptions $key`) — actually returns none.
- Outgoing Calls on `get`: expected one callee (`getOptions`) — actually returns none.

```tcl
oo::class create Factory {
    classmethod make {} { return 1 }
    classmethod build {} { Factory make }
}
Factory make
```

- Incoming Calls on `make`'s declaration: expected callers at both the top-level `Factory make` and inside `build`'s `Factory make` — actually returns none.
- Outgoing Calls on `build`: expected one callee (`make`, via `Factory make`) — actually returns none.

## Impact

Call Hierarchy is effectively non-functional for the two dispatch shapes that make up the overwhelming majority of real-world TclOO method/classmethod call sites. A method that only ever calls its siblings via `my` — which is the idiomatic, and in most cases the *only* correct, way to do it — shows "no callers"/"no callees" for edges that are actually present, silently under-reporting rather than erroring.

## Suggested fix direction

Reuse the dispatch-recognition logic `references.rs` already has instead of re-deriving a weaker version of it here:

- For incoming calls: instead of comparing `segment_body_calls`'s head word directly against the target name, recognize a `my <method>` shape (head word literally `my`, with the method name as the next argument) in addition to the bare-name shape, and for classmethods, recognize a bare `ClassName <method>` shape analogous to what `find_obj_method_call_sites`/`scan_obj_method_region` in `references.rs` already scan for.
- For outgoing calls, the same two shapes need recognizing on the producing side: `my <head2>` should resolve `head2` (not `my`) against `class_def.methods`, and `ClassName <head2>` should resolve `head2` against `class_def.class_methods` when `ClassName` matches the enclosing class (or a related class in its hierarchy).
- Given `references.rs` already solves call-site recognition for both shapes (including the namespace/inheritance-aware variants), the more maintainable direction may be for `call_hierarchy.rs` to call into (or share a common helper with) that module's scanners rather than re-implementing head-word matching independently in `segment_body_calls`'s consumers.

## Related

- #981 (bare classmethod/object-command dispatch matching is namespace-blind) and #990 (itcl `Factory::make` class-proc dispatch invisible to Find References/Rename) are the same general theme — a dispatch-shape recognizer missing a real call-site form — in `references.rs`/`rename.rs` rather than `call_hierarchy.rs`. This issue is call hierarchy's version of the same class of gap, for the two most common TclOO dispatch shapes rather than a namespace-precision or itcl-specific one.

issues.title: folding/formatting/minify/declaration/interprocedural/param_traits/tcl-irules-walker only implement the direct-apply half of the BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX fix from 2cf3725 (#954)
issues.body:
## Background

Commit `2cf3725` ("fix(lsp): apply lambda body highlighting through `[list ...]` indirection (issue #954)") was supposed to make every consumer that walks an `apply {argList body} …` lambda literal also see through the list-quoted spelling of the same call, `[list apply {argList body} …]`, since that's the shape issue #954 was actually reported against (a `pkgIndex.tcl`-style `package ifneeded name ver [list apply {dir {...}} $dir]` entry).

The correct two-shape resolution already exists in the tree and is the pattern every consumer should mirror:

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/command_prefix.rs::extract_list_quoted_prefix_head` (lines 252–283) — strips the token's `[`/`]`, re-segments the inner script, requires it to be exactly one call to a `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` command (`list`, resolved via `registry.get`, command_prefix.rs:264–267), and only then treats the *second* word (`apply`) as the real head.
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs::insert_lambda_literal_overrides` (~2811–2883, trait check at 2841) implements the analogous second branch for semantic tokens and is the one consumer in this commit that got both shapes right — it's cited here as the in-repo template the other consumers should copy, not as something needing a fix itself.

Every other consumer the commit touched only added the *first* branch — a direct `registry.arg_indices_for_role(cmd.name(), …, ArgRole::LambdaLiteral)` lookup keyed off the literal, immediately-segmented head word. None of them added the second branch that checks `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` on that head and re-resolves through `list`'s first argument. Since `list`'s own `CommandSpec` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/list_.rs`) carries `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` but declares no `arg_roles`, and `CommandRegistry::arg_indices_for_role` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs:1090–1154`) does no BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX unwrapping for any role except `ArgRole::CommandPrefix`, every one of these consumers silently no-ops on the list-quoted shape.

## The gap

All seven consumers below were independently audited (static read + a temporary, reverted unit/integration test per consumer) and each confirmed to implement only the direct-apply branch, never the list-quoted branch:

| Consumer | Direct `apply {...} $x` | List-quoted `[list apply {...} $x]` | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/folding.rs` (`collect_body_folds`, 353–482) | Works — `apply_lambda_body_folds_and_recurses_into_nested_blocks` passes | No fold anywhere — probe returned `regions = []` | Editor-UX only (cosmetic). Folding gutter never offers a collapse for the lambda body in a `package ifneeded … [list apply {...} $dir]` entry, though the same code now highlights correctly via semantic tokens. |
| `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/formatting/engine.rs` (`identify_body_args`, 358–373) | Works — `apply_lambda_body_indents_and_params_normalise`, `apply_lambda_namespace_element_preserved` pass | No-op — probe input formatted byte-for-byte unchanged (no reindent, no `dir`→`{dir}` normalisation) | Editor-UX only (cosmetic, non-destructive). Format-on-save "fixes" the direct spelling of a lambda callback but silently skips the list-quoted spelling. |
| `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/minify.rs` (`render_command`, 2428–2453; `reconstruct_raw` Str arm, 2546) | Works — `apply_lambda_body_minifies` passes | No-op — probe: comments/extra whitespace inside the lambda body pass through byte-for-byte | Editor-UX only (cosmetic). Output stays valid Tcl; only the size-reduction purpose of the tool is defeated for this idiom. |
| `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/declaration.rs` (LambdaLiteral branch, 205–228) | Works — `global_declared_inside_apply_lambda_body_is_found` passes | Fails — probe test returned `locs.len() == 0`, expected `1` | Backs `textDocument/declaration` (go-to-declaration: jump from a `global`/`variable`/`upvar` reference to its declaration site, falling back to go-to-definition). Ctrl-click on a variable used inside a list-quoted lambda body silently returns no navigation result, with no error and no fallback — a real feature gap, though not destructive. |
| `rust/tcl-compiler/src/interprocedural.rs` (`scan_source_for_calls`, 1686–1707) | Works — `call_inside_apply_lambda_body_is_a_direct_call` passes | Fails — probe: `direct_calls` for the caller proc is `[]` instead of containing the callee | **Real correctness/safety risk.** The missing call-graph edge propagates through `compute_transitive_calls` (interprocedural.rs:465, 788–794, 866–893) into `ProcSummary.calls`, which `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/unused_procs.rs`'s O124 pass (`reachable_procs`, 84, 101–105, 142–161) walks from `::when::*` event roots. End-to-end repro: a proc reachable from a `when HTTP_REQUEST { … }` handler only through `[list apply {p {helper $p}} …]` gets O124-flagged and auto-commented-out by the optimiser as dead code, even though it is live. |
| `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/param_traits.rs` (`scan_deep` LambdaLiteral loop, ~432–462) | Works — `eval_param_inside_apply_lambda_body_records_eval_trait` passes | Fails — probe test panicked `no traits for body` | Feeds `ProcArgTrait::Eval` metadata, surfaced only via `rust/tcl-mcp/src/tools.rs:1035–1042` (MCP proc-introspection tool). Currently **latent, not live-impacting**: the containing pass is gated behind `Analyser::deep_param_traits`, which defaults to `false` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs:401–409, 709`) and is set `true` nowhere outside unit tests today. Will bite the first time a future consumer wires that flag on. |
| `rust/tcl-irules/src/walker.rs` (LambdaLiteral loop, 191–214) | Works — `a_pool_used_only_inside_an_apply_lambda_body_is_referenced` passes | Fails — probe: reference list is `[]` for the list-quoted form vs `["/Common/some_pool"]` for the direct form | **Real correctness/safety risk.** `extract_irules_object_references`'s output feeds `rust/tcl-bigip/src/graph.rs::EdgeBuilder::irule_pass` (577–595, wired into `build_forward_edges`/`build_bigip_object_graph` at 614/646), which `rust/tcl-bigip/src/cleanup.rs::compute_cleanup` (90–125) BFS-walks from root nodes to decide what's unreachable. A pool referenced only inside a list-quoted lambda body in an iRule looks unreachable and gets a `delete ltm pool …` cleanup command generated for it — the "safe to run this generated tmsh script" bigip-cleanup workflow would delete a pool that's actually still in use. |

**Bottom line on severity:**
- **Real correctness/safety consequences, beyond cosmetics:** `interprocedural.rs` (O124 can auto-comment-out a live, reachable-only-via-list-quoting proc) and `tcl-irules/src/walker.rs` (bigip-cleanup can emit a delete command for a pool still referenced only through list-quoted indirection).
- **Editor-UX-only / cosmetic:** `folding.rs`, `formatting/engine.rs`, `minify.rs` — all three fail closed (no fold / no reformat / no minification) rather than corrupting anything; annoying and inconsistent with the direct-call form, not destructive.
- **Feature gap, not cosmetic but not destructive either:** `declaration.rs` backs `textDocument/declaration` (go-to-declaration for `global`/`variable`/`upvar` sites) and silently returns zero results for the list-quoted shape.
- **Latent/dormant today:** `param_traits.rs`'s gap is real but currently unreachable through any wired feature (`deep_param_traits` defaults off); flagged so it isn't reintroduced once a live consumer turns that flag on.

None of these are regressions — in every case the LambdaLiteral-aware branch itself is new code added by `2cf3725`, and the list-quoted shape was equally unhandled (in a more diffuse way) before the commit. The gap is that the commit's own stated scope ("wired into every consumer that previously re-segmented the whole lambda literal as a script") oversells these seven consumers' coverage relative to what `command_prefix.rs` and `semantic_tokens.rs` actually received in the same commit.

## Verification bar

For each consumer in the table above, "fixed" means:

1. Add a `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` check on the segmented command's head, mirroring `extract_list_quoted_prefix_head` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/command_prefix.rs:252–283`) — when the head (e.g. `list`) carries the trait, re-resolve the effective head from its own first argument and re-query `ArgRole::LambdaLiteral` (or the relevant role) against *that* head, exactly as `insert_lambda_literal_overrides` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs:2811–2883`) already does for semantic tokens.
2. A new test per consumer using the canonical repro shape (`package ifneeded foo 1.0 [list apply {dir {...}} $dir]` or the closer-to-source-file variant already used in each consumer's probe, e.g. `set y [list apply {p {helper $p}} 1]` for `interprocedural.rs`, `[list apply {dir { pool /Common/some_pool }} /Common]` for `tcl-irules/src/walker.rs`) produces output matching the already-passing direct-call sibling test in the same file.
3. For `interprocedural.rs` specifically: an end-to-end optimiser test (mirroring the one used to confirm this gap) showing O124 no longer fires on a proc reachable only through `[list apply ...]` from a `when` handler.
4. For `tcl-irules/src/walker.rs` specifically: an end-to-end `tcl-bigip` cleanup test showing a pool referenced only through `[list apply ...]` inside an iRule is no longer proposed for deletion.
5. `docs/kcs/kcs-issue-apply-lambda-body-not-highlighted-via-list-quoting.md`'s "Test anchors" section updated to list the new list-quoted test for each of these seven files (it currently lists only the direct-call test for each, which is what let this gap ship unnoticed).

## References

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/command_prefix.rs:252-283` — `extract_list_quoted_prefix_head`, the reference two-shape implementation; trait check at `264-267`.
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs:2811-2883` (trait check at `2841`) — `insert_lambda_literal_overrides`, the one consumer in `2cf3725` that implements both shapes correctly; used above only as the pattern to mirror.
- `rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs:1090-1154` — `CommandRegistry::arg_indices_for_role`; does BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX unwrapping only for `ArgRole::CommandPrefix`, never for `Body`/`LambdaLiteral`.
- `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/list_.rs` — `list`'s spec: carries `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX`, declares no `arg_roles`.
- `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/apply.rs:50` — `apply`'s `arg_roles: &[(0, ArgRole::LambdaLiteral)]`.
- `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/package_.rs:59-60` — `package ifneeded`'s script argument as `ArgRole::Body`/`BodyKind::Structural`, the motivating pkgIndex.tcl shape.
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/folding.rs:353-482` (guard at `395`, LambdaLiteral loop `446-480`).
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/formatting/engine.rs:358-373` (`identify_body_args`; `is_braced` gate at `364`, `370`; `reconstruct_raw` Cmd-token passthrough `228-328`).

issues.title: Document that rename/interp-alias of apply (or any registry-special command) defeats ArgRole-driven handling (e.g. LambdaLiteral)
issues.body:
## Background

Commit 2cf3725 fixed `apply`'s own `CommandSpec` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/apply.rs`) so its first argument is tagged `ArgRole::LambdaLiteral` instead of `ArgRole::Body`, giving eight consumers (semantic tokens/highlighting, folding, formatting, minify, declaration scanning, interprocedural call-graph, param-trait inference, and the iRules object-reference walker) lambda-body-aware handling: the body script inside `{x {puts $x}}` gets real tokenisation (`puts` as `TokenKind::Function`, `x` as `TokenKind::Parameter`, etc.) instead of being painted as one opaque string.

All eight consumers reach that handling the same way: resolve the segmented command's literal head text and look it up by exact string in `CommandRegistry` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs`, `CommandRegistry::get` at lines 432-440 and `arg_indices_for_role` at 1090-1103 — both a plain `HashMap` lookup keyed on the literal spelling baked into the static spec built in `CommandRegistry::build_default`). That lookup mechanism itself is not new to this commit; it's the pre-existing architecture the whole registry-driven resolution system is built on.

## The gap / bug

Because resolution is purely by literal command name against the registry, renaming or aliasing `apply` silently and completely defeats every one of the eight lambda-literal-aware consumers, even though real Tcl treats the rename/alias as fully behaviourally transparent:

```tcl
rename apply myapply
myapply {x {puts $x}} hi
;# tclsh: prints "hi" -- identical to calling apply directly

interp alias {} myapply2 {} apply
myapply2 {x {puts $x}} hi
;# tclsh: prints "hi" -- identical to calling apply directly
```

Verified against real Tcl (tclsh 8.6.14) that both forms behave exactly like a direct `apply` call. Verified in the LSP (via a temporary, since-reverted `cargo test` in `semantic_tokens.rs`, working tree confirmed clean afterward) that after either `rename` or `interp alias`, the entire `{x {puts $x}}` word is left as a single opaque string token — `puts` is not `TokenKind::Function`, `x` is not `TokenKind::Parameter`. This is exactly the "parameter word misread as script" failure mode 2cf3725 fixed for `apply`'s literal spelling, reachable again through any rename or alias.

This is **not a regression introduced by 2cf3725**: `git show 2cf3725 -- rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/apply.rs` shows the only change was the `arg_roles` tag on the same statically-named `"apply"` `CommandSpec`, inserted into the same literal-keyed `by_name` map the same way before and after. Every `registry.insert(spec)` call sits inside the static `build_default`/`build` constructor, never on a rename/alias event, so the name-keyed architecture predates this commit and is orthogonal to what it changed. The gap is general: *any* registry-special command (not just `apply`) loses its special handling once renamed or aliased.

Worth noting precisely, since a shallower look could conclude otherwise: the codebase does have real rename/alias tracking — `signature_scan::handlers::handle_rename` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/handlers.rs:360-377`) populates `SignatureScanResult.renames`, and `analyser::handlers::resolve_alias` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:2656-2673`) resolves `interp alias`-recorded `command_aliases`. But `renames` only widens the W123 "known command" recovery set (`analyser/utils.rs:221-242`, no `ArgRole`/`Traits` attached), and `command_aliases` only feeds the separate find-references/rename/call-hierarchy link graph described in `docs/design/cross-file-command-resolution-lattice.md`. Neither is consulted by any of the eight `ArgRole`/`LambdaLiteral`-driven walkers, nor by the reference `BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` implementation in `command_prefix.rs:264` (which gates on `registry.get(&seg.texts[0])` the same way).

This is currently undocumented: `docs/kcs/kcs-issue-apply-lambda-body-not-highlighted-via-list-quoting.md`'s Failure modes / Triage checklist sections (lines 158-196) list several known gaps but say nothing about rename/`interp alias` defeating detection, and the command-registry.md design doc's 2cf3725 diff doesn't mention it either.

## What to fix / investigate

At minimum, document this as a known, accepted limitation:

- Add a line to `docs/kcs/kcs-issue-apply-lambda-body-not-highlighted-via-list-quoting.md`'s Failure modes/Triage checklist (or a dedicated section in `docs/design/compiler/command-registry.md`) stating that `CommandRegistry` resolution is purely literal-name-based, so `rename`/`interp alias` on any registry-special command (not limited to `apply`) silently loses that command's special `ArgRole`/`Traits`-driven handling across all consumers.
- Make clear in that note that this is a pre-existing property of the registry architecture shared by every registry-driven consumer, not something specific to `apply` or introduced by 2cf3725.

A real fix (teaching the eight `ArgRole`/`LambdaLiteral` consumers, plus `command_prefix.rs`'s `BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` gate, to consult the existing `renames`/`command_aliases` fact tables before falling back to a literal `registry.get`) is a substantially larger undertaking — it would mean threading whole-file alias/rename resolution into every role-lookup call site, several of which (e.g. `semantic_tokens.rs`, `minify.rs`) are hot paths. Given how rare renaming or aliasing `apply` (or other registry-special commands) is in real Tcl/iRules code, this is likely not worth doing unless it turns up in practice (e.g. a user's `pkgIndex.tcl`-style wrapper or logging/instrumentation alias around `apply`). This issue is to track the gap and get it documented, not to mandate the larger fix.

## Verification bar

- Documentation-only: confirm the added note accurately states (a) the limitation is general to the registry architecture, not `apply`-specific, and (b) it predates and is orthogonal to 2cf3725.
- If anyone later attempts the "real fix": the bar is that `rename apply myapply; myapply {x {puts $x}} hi` and `interp alias {} myapply2 {} apply; myapply2 {x {puts $x}} hi` produce the same semantic-token output (`puts` as `TokenKind::Function`, `x` as `TokenKind::Parameter`) as calling `apply {x {puts $x}} hi` directly, across all eight consumers listed above plus `command_prefix.rs`'s `BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` gate — not just semantic tokens.

## References

- `rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs` (`CommandRegistry::get` 432-440, `arg_indices_for_role` 1090-1103, `by_name` construction in `build_default`)
- `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/apply.rs` (2cf3725's only change: `arg_roles` tag)
- Eight consumers: `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs` (1811, 2830, 2839), `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/folding.rs` (191), `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/formatting/engine.rs` (361), `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/minify.rs` (2421-2429), `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/declaration.rs` (216), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/interprocedural.rs` (1669, 1692), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/param_traits.rs` (395, 438-440), `rust/tcl-irules/src/walker.rs` (191)
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/command_prefix.rs` (264, `BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` reference gate)
- Existing (unconsulted-by-these-paths) rename/alias tracking: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/signature_scan/handlers.rs` (`handle_rename`, 360-377), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs` (`resolve_alias`, 2656-2673), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/utils.rs` (`recovery_known_commands`, 221-242)
- `docs/kcs/kcs-issue-apply-lambda-body-not-highlighted-via-list-quoting.md` (Failure modes/Triage checklist, 158-196)
- `docs/design/compiler/command-registry.md`
- `docs/design/cross-file-command-resolution-lattice.md`

issues.title: Cross-file autoload (tclIndex) rename/go-to-definition races the workspace scan, fails deterministically in isolation
issues.body:
Fixed in bitwisecook/tcl-lsp#997 (commits `b90549c` and `eda64f2`):

- Added a `workspace_scan_gate` mutex in `tcl-lsp-server`'s `Backend`, held for the full duration of `scan_workspace_folders`. `ensure_autoload_indexed` now waits it out before consulting `package_resolver`, so a rename/go-to-definition request landing during an in-flight scan blocks until the scan completes instead of reading a possibly-still-empty resolver. Also added a `[timing] workspace_folders_scan` log line mirroring the existing `[timing] workspace_state.update` convention.
- Verified directly against the running server: a rename request fired with zero synchronization wait (the worst case) now correctly blocks for the scan's duration (~650ms in the test fixture) and returns the full cross-file edit, instead of racing it and returning null.
- Added a unit regression test (`autoload_indexed_query_waits_out_an_in_flight_workspace_scan`) that holds the gate directly and asserts a concurrent `ensure_autoload_indexed` call blocks until it's released, rather than relying on incidental timing.
- Separately, fixed the M8 VS Code test itself: it waited on the wrong signal (the consumer document's own per-document diagnostics commit, not the workspace-wide scan) and was additionally unreliable in a full suite run (`diagnostics.test.ts`'s issue-832 test opens the same fixture earlier, so no *new* log line for it ever fires within this test's `since` window). Removed that wait entirely — the rename request is now correct regardless of timing, so no synchronization is needed before firing it.

Confirmed: the previously-failing VS Code test passes 3/3 in isolation and the full `test-ext` suite (692 tests) passes cleanly.

issues.title: W123 alias/rename-target checks use file-end-only deletion gating, not call-site/conditional-aware (follow-up to #973)
issues.body:
## Background

#973 fixed W123 ("unknown command") never firing for a proc/class/rename target/`interp alias` target that was renamed or deleted away with no later re-establishment. For procs and classes, the fix (`fact_live_for_call` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/unresolved.rs`) is call-site- and conditional-body-aware: it checks whether the call is textually before an unconditional top-level deletion, and whether the deletion itself sits inside a proc/class/method body that might never execute — matching the sophistication `qualified_name_deleted_before` already gives registry builtins.

The alias (`alias_names`) and rename-target (`rename_target_names`) sets in `build_w123_known_names` still use the older, cruder `fact_live_at_file_end` check — file-end granularity only, no call-site or conditional-body awareness. This predates #973 (it's the mechanism #973's fix was modeled after) and was left untouched deliberately, since #973 was scoped to procs/classes. It carries two false positives that the proc/class path no longer has.

## The gaps (confirmed against tclsh 8.6.14)

**1. A call to an alias/rename-target textually *before* its later deletion still fires W123**, even though the call resolves fine at the time it runs:

```tcl
proc target {} { return 1 }
interp alias {} short {} target
short                            ;# tclsh: succeeds
interp alias {} short {}
```

tclsh: `short` succeeds. The analyser: W123 fires on `short` anyway, because `alias_names` only asks "is this alias's most recent action in the whole file a live definition or a deletion", ignoring where the call sits relative to the deletion.

**2. A deletion recorded inside a proc body that's never called still poisons the whole-file set**, even though the deletion never actually executes:

```tcl
proc target {} { return 1 }
interp alias {} short {} target
proc maybeDelete {} { interp alias {} short {} }
proc caller {} { short }
```

tclsh: calling `caller` (without ever calling `maybeDelete`) succeeds. The analyser: W123 fires on `short` inside `caller`, because the conditional deletion inside `maybeDelete` is treated as unconditional.

## What the fix looks like

Same shape as #973's proc/class fix: replace `alias_names: HashSet<String>` / `rename_target_names: HashSet<String>` with per-tail (or per-name) `(qualified_name, establishing_offset)` maps — mirroring `proc_defs_by_tail` / `class_defs_by_tail` — and check each candidate's liveness per call site via `fact_live_for_call` instead of `fact_live_at_file_end`, inside `w123_invocation_resolves`.

## Verification bar

- Repro tests for both gaps above (expect no W123).
- Regression tests for the cases `fact_live_at_file_end` already gets right today (alias/rename-target deleted with no re-establishment still fires W123; re-established after deletion still resolves) — don't regress these.
- All confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available in the environment, 9.0) before/after.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo xtask resolution-drift`.

## References

- Root issue: #973
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/unresolved.rs` (`build_w123_known_names`, `fact_live_at_file_end`, `fact_live_for_call`, `w123_invocation_resolves`)

issues.title: Arity checker (E002/E003) silently abstains when a rename/alias deletion sits inside a never-triggered proc body
issues.body:
## Background

While fixing #973 (W123 false negative on a deleted proc/class/alias/rename target), I found the same root-cause class of bug in the same-file arity resolver (E002/E003, `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs`), which uses a related but distinct mechanism: `fact_in_effect` / `fact_superseded_by_deletion`, consulted by `resolve_indirect_call_target`.

`fact_in_effect` treats a call inside a proc/method body as unconditionally seeing every top-level fact (`!cand.enforce_order || established_off < cand.call_off`) — correct for call-site order-gating. `fact_superseded_by_deletion` then reuses the *same* `fact_in_effect` check to decide whether a recorded deletion is "in effect" by the time of the call:

```rust
fn fact_superseded_by_deletion(&self, name: &str, fact_off: u32, cand: &PendingUserCallArity) -> bool {
    self.deleted_commands
        .get(name)
        .is_some_and(|&del_off| del_off > fact_off && Self::fact_in_effect(cand, del_off))
}
```

This reuse is the bug: `fact_in_effect(cand, del_off)` only asks "is the call order-gated against the *call's own* body/top-level status", not "did the deletion itself actually execute" — it has no way to know that `del_off` names a statement sitting inside a *different*, possibly-never-invoked proc body. So any `rename`/`interp alias` deletion recorded anywhere in the file — even one nested inside a proc nobody calls — permanently disqualifies the fact for every later proc-body call, causing the arity check to abstain (silently, no diagnostic) instead of checking against the still-live definition.

The W123 fix in #973 addresses the equivalent question for `unresolved.rs` via `fact_live_for_call`, which adds `self.offset_is_inside_definition_body(del_off)` — checking whether the *deletion itself* is conditional — before treating the deletion as in effect. `fact_in_effect`/`fact_superseded_by_deletion` in `validity.rs` has no equivalent check.

## Repro (confirmed against tclsh 8.6.14)

```tcl
proc target {a b} {}
proc maybeDelete {} { rename target {} }
target 1 2 3
```

tclsh: `maybeDelete` is never called, so the `rename` never executes — `target 1 2 3` fails `wrong # args: should be "target a b"`.

The analyser (`arity_codes` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/tests.rs`'s test harness): reports **nothing** — no E002/E003 at all. It has silently treated `target` as permanently deleted (superseded), because `maybeDelete`'s `rename target {}` disqualifies it, and abstains rather than checking the still-live 2-arg signature.

For contrast, the call-site-order half of this already works correctly — a top-level call *before* a later, unconditional (non-body) deletion still gets checked:

```tcl
proc target {a b} {}
target 1 2 3
rename target {}
```

tclsh and the analyser agree: `E003` fires. Only the "is the deletion itself conditional" half is missing.
