This affects procs, `rename` targets, and `interp alias` targets alike, since they all flow through the same `fact_superseded_by_deletion` helper via `resolve_indirect_call_target`.

## What the fix looks like

Add a check to `fact_superseded_by_deletion` (or a new helper it delegates to) mirroring `fact_live_for_call`'s `self.offset_is_inside_definition_body(del_off)` guard — a deletion recorded inside a proc/method/class body should not supersede a fact unless that body is known to run unconditionally (which it isn't, by the same "no CFG dominator model" limitation already documented elsewhere in this file for conditionally-*defined* procs).

## Verification bar

- The repro above must fire `E003` after the fix.
- The existing conditional-deletion-adjacent tests in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/tests.rs` (`same_file_rename_reestablished_after_deletion_checks_new_arity`, `same_file_alias_reestablished_after_deletion_checks_new_target_arity`, etc.) must not regress.
- Confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available, 9.0) for both the fixed case and its existing-passing counterparts.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## References

- Discovered while fixing #973 (same root-cause class, different diagnostic pass).
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs` (`fact_in_effect`, `fact_superseded_by_deletion`, `resolve_indirect_call_target`)

issues.title: Constant-$cmd dispatch settlement resolves through a renamed/deleted-away proc, class, alias, or rename target with no deletion gate
issues.body:
## Background

Same root-cause class as #973/#1006/#1007: a "is this name a known/live command" predicate that consults `all_procs`/`all_classes`/`command_aliases`/`renamed_commands` via `.contains_key(...)` with no awareness that the name may have been renamed away or deleted (`rename NAME {}` / `interp alias {} NAME {}`, tracked in `deleted_commands`) with no later re-establishment.

Found in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/const_dispatch.rs`, `settle_one_site`'s `known` (lines ~111-118) and `user_defined` (lines ~119-124) closures — used to settle a `set cmd target; $cmd` (or `{*}$cmd`) style indirect dispatch site against the compiler's flow-sensitive constant-value model (M7). Neither closure checks `deleted_commands` at all (only the registry-builtin clause of `known` gates on a `renamed_away` set) — the exact shape the `known` predicate in `scope.rs`'s `finalise_invocation_resolutions` had before #973.

## Confirmed (via the analyser's own test harness, not just reasoning)

```tcl
proc target {} {}
rename target {}
set cmd target
$cmd
```

tclsh 8.6.14: `$cmd` fails `invalid command name "target"` (confirmed in earlier investigation for #973/#1006).

The analyser: the indirect invocation created for `$cmd` still resolves `resolved_qualified_name: Some("::target")`, as if `target` is still live — because `user_defined("::target")` returns `true` (no deletion check) so `settle_one_site` doesn't abstain.

## Why this does NOT cause a W123 false negative (scoped correctly)

`settle_const_dispatches` (which calls `settle_one_site`) runs from `emit_cfg_ssa_diagnostics`, which `run_diagnostic_emitters` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs`) calls **after** `emit_unresolved_command_diagnostics` (W123) — confirmed by the code's own comment at `canonicalize_result_order` ("W123 already emitted"). So the invocations this module creates are never re-checked by W123's own (already deletion-aware, per #973/#1006) resolution logic.

**The actual impact is narrower but still real:** stale/incorrect `resolved_qualified_name` on the `SignatureCommandInvocation`s this module pushes into `result.command_invocations`, which feed hover, go-to-definition, find-references, and rename-tracking (per the module's own doc comment) for `$cmd`-style indirect dispatch sites. A `$cmd` dispatch whose value resolves to a renamed-away/deleted-with-no-reestablishment command will still show that command as its "live" target in these features, even though calling it fails at runtime.

## What the fix looks like

Extend `known`/`user_defined` in `settle_one_site` with the same offset-comparison approach `fact_live_for_call` (`unresolved.rs`) or `fact_superseded_by_deletion` (`validity.rs`) already use — checking each qualified candidate's own establishing offset against `deleted_commands`, with re-establishment and conditional-body awareness. The call-site offset available here is `site.span.start()` (the `$cmd`/`{*}$cmd` token's position).

## Verification bar

- The repro above must resolve to no target (or at least not falsely resolve as `::target`) after the fix — confirm via `command_invocations` in a unit test (see `const_cmd_head_records_a_reference_to_the_dispatched_proc_m7` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/tests.rs` for the existing test shape/pattern).
- Regression guard: the same shape *with* a later re-establishment (a fresh `proc target {} {}` after the deletion) must still resolve correctly.
- Confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available, 9.0).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## References

- Discovered while auditing for more instances of #973's root cause after fixing #1006/#1007.
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/const_dispatch.rs` (`settle_one_site`, `known`, `user_defined`)

issues.title: var_command.rs has four more ungated "is this command known" checks — one actively deletes a correct W123 diagnostic
issues.body:
## Background

Same root-cause class as #973/#1006/#1007/(const_dispatch.rs sibling issue): an "is this name known" check against `all_procs`/`all_classes`/`command_aliases`/`renamed_commands` with no `deleted_commands` gate. `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs` has **zero** references to `deleted_commands`, `fact_live_for_call`, `fact_superseded_by_deletion`, or `offset_is_inside_any_definition_body` anywhere in the file (confirmed by grep) — every "known" check in it predates the #973 fix pattern entirely. Audited every `.contains_key(...)` site in the file against real Tcl semantics; four are genuine bugs, two are not (see below).

## Confirmed bugs, in priority order

### 1. `resolve_interpolated_w123_diagnostics` (~line 1478-1479) — highest priority: actively deletes a correct diagnostic

This closure retroactively **removes an already-emitted W123** for an interpolated command head (`do${suffix}`) once SCCP folds `$suffix` to a constant, checking the folded name against `all_procs.contains_key` with no deletion gate.

Repro (same shape confirmed working for #973/#1006):
```tcl
proc doThing {} {}
rename doThing {}
set suffix Thing
do${suffix}
```
tclsh 8.6.14: fails `invalid command name "doThing"`. The analyser: W123 is emitted initially for the unresolved interpolated head, then this closure sees the SCCP-folded name `doThing`, finds it in `all_procs` (deleted-but-not-pruned), and **deletes the W123 diagnostic outright** — a duplicate, independently-implemented "is this proc known" that never got the #973 fix, and the only one of these four that regresses an already-correct diagnostic rather than just failing to add one.

### 2. `is_known_command` (~line 578), used by `w307_site_suppressed`

Gates suppression of W307 ("non-literal command name — cannot statically analyze") once SCCP resolves a `$var` dispatch head to a constant. No deletion gate, and no call-site offset is even threaded into the closure today, so a `fact_live_for_call`-style fix needs that plumbed through `w307_site_suppressed` first. Not redundantly covered elsewhere — this is `var_command.rs`'s own territory (dynamic `$var` dispatch), so a dead-but-still-`all_procs`-resident name here genuinely suppresses a warning real Tcl's runtime would reject.

### 3. `emit_dispatch_table_command_references`'s `known` (~line 1266-1269)

Synthesizes a `SignatureCommandInvocation` reference for a dispatch-table literal (`array set`/`dict` proc-name string) when its value is a known proc/class — feeding rename-tracking, references, and (via `command_invocations`) call-graph/dead-code consumers. Confirmed by code-flow (not just reasoning): this runs from `emit_cfg_ssa_diagnostics` → `emit_var_command_diagnostics`, which — like the sibling `const_dispatch.rs` issue — executes *after* `finalise_invocation_resolutions` (`scope.rs`, the #973-fixed, deletion-aware settling pass) already ran, so entries this closure pushes are never re-settled and permanently keep whatever the ungated `known` decided. Lower urgency than #1/#2 (feeds navigation/rename-tracking, not a diagnostic code directly), but same fix shape.

### 4. `harvest_constructor_object_types` (~line 144-147) / `emit_cmd_command_diagnostics` (~line 1070-1071) — same check, two call shapes

Checks whether `head`/`class_qn` is a known `all_classes` entry to attribute `set x [Cls new]` (or `[Cls new] method`) as producing an `Object(Cls)`, driving W308 method-name validation. Lowest priority: if `Cls` was renamed away with no re-establishment, real Tcl fails the constructor call itself with "invalid command name" — which the already-fixed, deletion-aware class path in `unresolved.rs`'s W123 very likely already catches as the primary diagnostic. This gap mostly produces a redundant/misleading secondary W308-family diagnostic rather than the sole miss, and the trigger (renaming a TclOO class command) is rare. Worth fixing for consistency if the area is being touched anyway, not urgent standalone.

## Confirmed NOT bugs (different questions, no gate needed)

- **`compute_factory_object_ranges`'s `is_user_proc`** (~line 706-709, used at ~723) — this only *routes* factory-object classification (name-shape heuristic vs. the separate proc-return-value fixpoint); it doesn't itself answer the terminal "is this class currently live" question, so gating it changes nothing about correctness.
- **`has_external_super_or_mixin`** (~line 1368-1373) — asks "do I have structural knowledge of this class's method table" (an inheritance-edge/MRO fact established once, at `superclass`/`mixin` declaration time), not "is this class's command currently callable." TclOO's real semantics: renaming or deleting a class command after a subclass link is established does not invalidate that subclass's inherited method table (the well-known "rename the class away after subclassing, existing subclasses/instances keep working" idiom) — so the ungated check matches real behavior here.

## Verification bar

- Repro tests for each of the four bugs above (using the same tclsh-confirmed pattern already established for #973/#1006/#1007), expecting the corrected behavior after fixing.
- Regression guards for the re-established-after-deletion case for each.
- Confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available, 9.0).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## References

- Discovered while auditing for more instances of #973's root cause after fixing #1006/#1007.
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs`

issues.title: type_infer.rs's constructor_object_type has no deletion gate, independently re-introducing a fixed var_command.rs false positive
issues.body:
## Background

Same root-cause class as #973/#1006/#1007/#1009/#1010: an "is this a known class" check with no `deleted_commands` gate. Found while fixing #1010's `var_command.rs::harvest_constructor_object_types` (the `set x [Cls new]` variable-assignment constructor-typing site).

`rust/tcl-compiler/src/type_infer.rs`'s `constructor_object_type` (~line 190-221) types a `[Cls new]` / `[Cls create x]` call as `TypeLattice::object_of(Cls)` purely from `known_classes.contains(command)` — a plain `HashSet<String>` with no offset or deletion awareness:

```rust
fn constructor_object_type<S: std::hash::BuildHasher>(
    command: &str,
    args: &[&str],
    known_classes: &HashSet<String, S>,
    namespace: &str,
) -> TypeLattice {
    let is_ctor_spelling = args.first().is_some_and(|a| matches!(*a, "new" | "create") ...);
    if is_ctor_spelling && !known_classes.is_empty() {
        if known_classes.contains(command) {
            return TypeLattice::object_of(command);
        }
        ...
```

This feeds `fu.types` (the per-symbol SSA type lattice), which `var_command.rs::aggregate_object_types`'s `collect_object_types` reads directly to drive W308 method-resolution. #1010 fixed the *other* independent source that feeds the same map (`harvest_constructor_object_types`, a syntactic mirror of this same recognition for the var-assignment shape) — but since `aggregate_object_types` unions **both** sources, this one alone is enough to keep reproducing the bug for the `set x [Cls new]` shape, even with #1010's fix applied.

## Confirmed (via the analyser's own test harness)

```tcl
oo::class create Dog { method bark {} { return woof } }
rename Dog {}
proc foo {} { set x [Dog new]
$x fly }
```

tclsh 8.6.14: `Dog` is gone after the rename — `[Dog new]` itself fails `invalid command name "Dog"`, so `x` is never assigned an object at all.

The analyser (after #1010's fix to `harvest_constructor_object_types`): still emits `W308` ("unknown method 'fly'") on `$x fly`, because `type_infer.rs`'s independent, ungated `constructor_object_type` still types `x` as `Object(::Dog)` via the SSA type lattice — the exact same misleading-secondary-diagnostic problem #1010 fixed for the *direct*-call shape (`[Dog new] fly`, handled by `var_command.rs::emit_cmd_command_diagnostics`), which does **not** recur there since that site's `class_live_for_call` fix is sufficient (it's the sole source for that shape).

## Why this is a separate, harder fix (not folded into #1010)

- `constructor_object_type` (and its caller `return_type_for_command`) is a bare, `&self`-less free function deep in the flow-insensitive-per-symbol SSA type-inference pass (`type_infer.rs`), called from at least 3 internal sites during CFG/SSA construction (lines ~921, ~1060, ~1601) — nothing like `Analyser`'s `deleted_commands` map or `fact_live_for_call`/`fact_live_at_file_end` is threaded into this module today.
- Unlike every other site fixed so far (which reused an existing helper with a one-line call-site or file-end check), this needs either (a) plumbing a `&HashMap<String, u32>` (deleted_commands) plus a per-statement offset through `type_infer.rs`'s call chain into a module that doesn't currently take either, or (b) a different design (e.g., pre-filtering `known_classes` to only live-at-file-end classes before it's passed in, which would need its own scoping analysis for the "conditional deletion inside a never-triggered body" case #973/#1010 already handle correctly elsewhere).
- `type_infer.rs` is foundational — used far beyond just W308 — so a rushed change here risks collateral regressions disproportionate to this bug's severity (a redundant/misleading *secondary* diagnostic; the actual root cause, `Dog`'s own W123, already fires correctly per #973's fix).

## What the fix likely looks like

Most likely: pass `known_classes` into `constructor_object_type`/`return_type_for_command` already pre-filtered to file-end-live classes only (`fact_live_at_file_end`-equivalent, computed once by the caller in `var_command.rs` or wherever `known_classes` is first assembled for this module), rather than threading offsets through `type_infer.rs`'s internals. Needs a look at all 3 call sites to confirm none needs finer, per-call-site (vs. file-end) precision.

## Verification bar

- The repro above must not draw W308 after the fix (or, if a design constraint makes file-end-only precision correct here, confirm that boundary is documented and tested — same TP/FP/TN discipline as #1010).
- Regression guard: re-establishment after deletion (a fresh `oo::class create Dog` later in the file) must still type `x` as `Object(Dog)` correctly.
- The already-fixed direct-call shape (`[Dog new] fly`, `emit_cmd_command_diagnostics`) and #1010's other 3 fixed sites must not regress.
- Confirmed against a real tclsh (8.6 and, if available, 9.0).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` (no new allows), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## References

- Discovered while fixing #1010 (same root-cause class, deeper subsystem).
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/type_infer.rs` (`constructor_object_type`, `return_type_for_command`); consumed by `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs` (`aggregate_object_types`, `collect_object_types`).

issues.title: hover() has no cross-document/autoload fallback that definition()/references() already use (issue #923 idx 24)
issues.body:
## Summary

Go-to-definition, find-references, and diagnostics all correctly resolve a tcllib-style command that is exported from a package-provide file but physically defined only in a sibling file reachable via `auto_path`/`tclIndex` (or even a plain `source`) — but **hover silently returns nothing at the exact same call-site location**, even though the same information is trivially available: the definition provider already found it, and hovering the definition itself, or a same-file call, renders it fine.

## Repro

Workspace (mirroring tcllib's `modules/math/math.tcl:17-44`):

`main.tcl`:
```tcl
lappend auto_path [file join [file dirname [info script]] mathlib]
package require math
math::zzqfrobnicate 1 2 3 4
```

`mathlib/math.tcl` — only `namespace export`s `zzqfrobnicate`/`wibblenum` and extends `::auto_path`; the real proc bodies live in a sibling file.

`mathlib/misc.tcl`:
```tcl
proc ::math::zzqfrobnicate {val args} { ... }
proc ::math::wibblenum {n} { ... }
```

`mathlib/tclIndex`:
```tcl
set auto_index(::math::zzqfrobnicate) [list source [file join $dir misc.tcl]]
```

`tclsh9.0` and `tclsh8.6` both run this cleanly and print the expected output — ground truth confirms `::math::zzqfrobnicate`/`::math::wibblenum` in `misc.tcl` are the real, unambiguous targets.

- `lsp_client.py definition main.tcl 3 15` (cursor on `zzqfrobnicate` in the call) → correctly returns `misc.tcl 4:5-4:26` (the exact proc declaration).
- `lsp_client.py references mathlib/misc.tcl 4 17` → correctly returns both `misc.tcl 4:5-4:26` and `main.tcl 3:12-3:31`.
- `lsp_client.py diagnostics main.tcl` → `0 items` (no false unknown-command warning).
- `lsp_client.py hover main.tcl 3 15` (and every column across the same token) → **`(no hover)`** — wrong. Hovering the identical symbol at its own definition site (`hover mathlib/misc.tcl 4 10`), or at a same-file call site, both render the full `proc ::math::zzqfrobnicate {val args} {...}` signature correctly.

A minimal control with a literal `source` instead of `auto_path`/`tclIndex` reproduces the identical hover-vs-definition split, showing the gap is a general cross-file hover limitation, not specific to the `tclIndex` mechanic — but it does affect exactly the assigned tcllib pattern.

## Root cause / suggested fix direction

`rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs`: `compute_definition` (~line 3633-3706) has four resolution tiers — in-document (`core_definition::definition`), cross-file TclOO method (`resolve_method_target`/`cross_file_method_definition`), cross-document workspace-index fallback (`cross_document_definition`), and an explicit "Autoload tier (M8)" (`autoload_definition`, ~line 3717) that resolves via `tclIndex`/`pkgIndex` specifically for this kind of pattern. The `references` handler (~line 8065) likewise merges local + cross-document hits.

By contrast, `hover()` (~line 9939-9984) calls only `core_hover::hover_with_profile(&doc.text, ..., &analysis, ...)` against the single-document `analysis_for(&uri, ...)` result and never calls `self.cross_document_definition(...)` or `self.autoload_definition(...)` when the in-document lookup misses. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs`'s `resolve_called_proc` call (~line 268, reusing `crate::definition::resolve_called_proc`) is likewise only ever given the single-file `AnalysisResult` — there is no cross-file/workspace-index parameter threaded into hover at all, and no test in `hover.rs` exercises a second file.

Suggested fix: in the `hover` handler, when `core_hover::hover_with_profile` returns `None` and the cursor is on a command head, fall back to the same workspace-index / autoload lookup `compute_definition` uses, then format the resulting `ProcDef`/`ClassDef` with the same `proc_hover_text`-style renderer already used for in-document hits.

## Provenance

Found during the issue #923 differential-audit campaign (real corpus: tcllib 2.0). Full detail (additional repro variants isolating the `tclIndex` mechanism from the general cross-file gap, oracle transcripts) is in `docs/design/issue-923-differential-audit/data/07-remaining-tcllib-findings-14.json` (idx 24) on the `claude/tcl-lsp-issue-923-qzkfqz` branch, along with `STATUS.md` in the same directory for the broader campaign context.

issues.title: W210 false-fires inside a dynamically-resolved -safe interp eval body on a plain set-then-read (pre-existing, predates PR #1020's rebase)
issues.body:
## Summary

`tcl-compiler::analyser interp_value_flow::builtins_only_dynamic_interp_eval_body_stays_silent` fails on `claude/tcl-lsp-issue-923-qzkfqz` (PR #1020), both locally and in CI (`rust-tests` check, e.g. run [30035264703](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/actions/runs/30035264703/job/89301669000)).

**Confirmed pre-existing**: this is NOT caused by PR #1020's rebase onto `origin/rust`. The test already fails identically on the branch's pre-rebase tip (`4f9eb58`), so it's a latent bug in this branch's own prior work — specifically the idx=9 fix that introduced tracking `set VAR [interp create ...]` as an interpreter-domain binding (commits `d43393d`/`edd0119`, "track set VAR [interp create ...] as an interpreter-domain binding (issue #923 idx 9)"). The test doesn't exist on `origin/rust` at all.

## Repro

```tcl
set s [interp create -safe]
interp eval $s {
    set x 1
    expr {$x + 1}
    puts "hi"
}
```

Expected: no diagnostics (a plain `set`-then-read of a local var inside the eval body, using only builtins, should never fire anything).

Actual: `W210` (read-before-set) fires.

```
thread 'interp_value_flow::builtins_only_dynamic_interp_eval_body_stays_silent' panicked at rust/tcl-compiler/tests/analyser.rs:1813:9:
["W210"]
```

## Root cause hint

This body is only reachable through a *dynamically*-targeted `interp eval $s {...}` (the interpreter handle `$s` was assigned from `interp create -safe`, tracked via the idx=9 interpreter-domain-binding mechanism) rather than a statically-named interp. The isolated/deferred analysis pass for such a body appears to lose or mis-order the write-before-read fact for `x`, even though `set x 1` textually precedes `expr {$x + 1}` in the same body — most likely because this body is analysed through the same kind of isolated/deferred pass used for proc/method bodies (see `DeferredBody`, `safe_interp_ctx`, and the `-safe` interp tracking added around the same area), and something in how that isolated pass seeds or walks the body's local scope treats `x` as read before its own `set`.

Not yet root-caused down to the exact function; worth checking `handle_interp_eval` / wherever a dynamically-resolved `interp eval $var {...}` body gets queued for analysis, and how it differs from the statically-named case (which the neighbouring test `synthetic_autoname_key_used_for_pathless_interp_create` shows still passes).

## Suggested next step

Self-contained `tcl-compiler` analyser bug, no dependency on the other tracked issues. Fix with the usual tclsh oracle + regression-test discipline once picked up.

issues.title: `link` modelled as an unconditional global CommandSpec — bareword TclOO sibling calls resolve without an actual `link` (regression introduced by PR #1020's rebase)
issues.body:
## Summary

Codex PR review on #1020 (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/oo_link.rs:30`, [comment](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/pull/1020#discussion_r3640051719)):

> This registers bare `link` as an unconditional core Tcl 8.6+ command, but stock Tcl does not provide such a global command; the audited implementation is the Tcllib/ooutil proc `::oo::Helpers::link`, made bare-callable only through a TclOO method's namespace path after that helper has been loaded. As a result, top-level `link ...` and method calls without ooutil are now accepted by registry-based diagnostics, hover, and completion even though they fail at runtime. Model the qualified, package-provided helper and its method-context resolution instead of adding a global `CommandSpec`.

## This is a live, currently-failing regression, not just a modelling nit

`tcl-lsp-server::preview_tickets_e2e::class_member_bareword_call_requires_link_e2e` fails in CI (`lsp-e2e` check, run [30035264703](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/actions/runs/30035264703/job/89301669067)) and locally on PR #1020's current tip.

**Confirmed to be a rebase-introduced regression**: this exact test PASSES on PR #1020's pre-rebase tip (`4f9eb58`) and FAILS on the post-rebase tip (`4cc9989`), after rebasing onto `origin/rust`'s current head. The test itself (and the underlying idx=113 fix it guards — "require `oo::Helpers::link` before resolving bareword TclOO member calls") predates the rebase and was passing; something `origin/rust` changed in the interim, combined with `oo_link.rs`'s unconditional global `CommandSpec`, now lets the gate through.

### Repro

```tcl
oo::class create Widget {
    method foo {x} { return "foo-called:$x" }
    method bar {} { return [foo 42] }
}
```

No `link foo` anywhere in the class body. Go-to-definition on `foo` inside `bar`'s `[foo 42]` call must abstain (empty/null result) — real Tcl raises `invalid command name "foo"` at runtime here, since `foo` was never linked. Instead, the LSP now returns a real definition location:

```
thread 'class_member_bareword_call_requires_link_e2e' panicked at rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/preview_tickets_e2e.rs:902:5:
un-linked bareword sibling call must abstain from definition: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":[{"range":{"end":{"character":14,"line":1},"start":{"character":11,"line":1}},"uri":"file:///link.tcl"}],"id":2}
```

The second half of the same test (same class, but with `constructor {} { link foo }` present) still correctly resolves — so the specific regression is the *abstain* side: the gate that should require a genuine `link` call is no longer effective, in a way that lines up with the Codex finding above.

## Suggested next step

Model `link` as the qualified, package-provided `::oo::Helpers::link` helper (method-context resolution, gated on ooutil being loaded) rather than a global `CommandSpec`, per the Codex review, and use `class_member_bareword_call_requires_link_e2e` as the regression test to confirm the fix. Worth checking whether the interaction is with `oo_link.rs` alone or also with whatever else changed in bareword TclOO-member resolution during the `origin/rust` rebase.

issues.title: interp create value-flow path uses split_whitespace, mis-splitting a braced/nested interpreter path
issues.body:
## Summary

Codex PR review on #1020 (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:123`, [comment](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/pull/1020#discussion_r3640051717)):

> For `set i [interp create {child}]` or a nested path such as `{parent child}`, `split_whitespace` retains braces and even splits one Tcl word into multiple fragments. The direct `interp create` handler records the real domain key, while this value-flow path binds `$i` to a different key such as `{child}` or `{parent`, so later `$i eval`/`interp alias $i ...` operations are associated with a bogus interpreter and no longer connect to equivalent literal-path operations. Reuse the Tcl segmenter/list parser here rather than whitespace splitting.

## Repro (not yet verified against a live oracle — flagging as reported, verify before fixing)

```tcl
set i [interp create {child}]
$i eval { ... }
```
or a nested path:
```tcl
set i [interp create {parent child}]
```

Expected: the value-flow path (which binds `$i` to the interpreter domain key for hover/definition/rename tracking of the dynamic handle) should bind to the same key the *direct* `interp create {child}` handler already records — real Tcl treats `{child}` as one word naming the interpreter `child`.

Actual (per the Codex finding): `split_whitespace` on the raw argument text retains the braces and can split a single braced word into multiple fragments (e.g. `{parent child}` → `"{parent"` + `"child}"`), so `$i` gets bound to a key like `"{child}"` or `"{parent"` instead of the real interpreter name — diverging from the direct handler's own key and breaking later `$i eval` / `interp alias $i ...` tracking for anyone using the `set i [interp create ...]` idiom with a braced or nested path.

## Suggested next step

Per the Codex review: replace the `split_whitespace` call in this value-flow path (`handlers.rs` around line 123) with the Tcl segmenter/list parser already used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. `tcl_syntax::list::find_element` / `list_word_elements`, used by the ensemble `-map`/`-subcommands` extraction after the same class of Codex finding was fixed there in the #1001 follow-up) so a braced interpreter-path word is parsed the same way the direct `interp create` handler already does. Add a regression test with both a single-braced and a nested `{parent child}` path, verified against the direct-handler key.

issues.title: Model `link` (oo::Helpers::link) qualified + method-context, not as a global command spec (Codex review, PR #1020)
issues.body:
## Summary

Owner/Codex review on PR #1020 (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/oo_link.rs:55`):

> The version gate fixes the 8.6 availability issue, but `link` is still not a global Tcl 9 command: `info commands ::link` is empty and top-level `link x` raises `invalid command name`, while `::oo::Helpers::link` exists and becomes bare-callable only from a method's namespace path. Registering the spec as global `link` therefore suppresses W123 and offers hover/completion in top-level Tcl 9 code that cannot run. This should be a qualified `::oo::Helpers::link` entry plus the existing method-context resolution, rather than a global command spec.

## What PR #1020 already landed

The **availability** half is fixed on the branch (`oo_link.rs`): `link` is `TCL90_PLUS` core + a `TCL86` `ooutil`-gated twin, so 8.6-vs-9.0 (W120) is correct. What remains is the **global-vs-method-context precision**.

## Why this isn't a drop-in (investigated during review)

The LSP models TclOO method bodies with `Scope::oo_global_resolution = true`: bare command calls in a method body are statically approximated as resolving from the **global** namespace, **not** `::oo::Helpers`. Consequently `my` / `next` / `self` are **all** registered today as plain global specs (`oo_my.rs` / `oo_next.rs` / `oo_self.rs`, `TCL86_PLUS`) — the same top-level imprecision. So:

- The reviewer's "qualified `::oo::Helpers::link` + existing method-context resolution" does **not** drop in: there is no `::oo::Helpers` method-body resolution today; it would have to be added (a new candidate-generation path gated on `oo_global_resolution`).
- Modelling `link` precisely while `my`/`next`/`self` stay global introduces an inconsistency within the oo::Helpers family.

## Options

1. **Fix `link` only, precisely** — add `::oo::Helpers::<name>` method-body resolution candidates + register qualified `::oo::Helpers::link` (version-gated) + drop the global `link` spec. Fixes the new imprecision this PR added; leaves `my`/`next`/`self` as-is (older, separate gap).
2. **Do the whole family** — model `link`/`my`/`next`/`self` as method-context-only consistently. Larger; touches pre-existing specs beyond this PR.

## Repro

```tcl
# tcl-dialect: tcl9.0
link foo
```

Top-level `link foo`: real Tcl 9 raises `invalid command name "link"` (`info commands ::link` is empty). **Expected:** W123 (unknown command); no hover/completion for a runnable `link`. **Actual:** resolves via the global spec — no W123, hover/completion offered.

Deferred from PR #1020 per owner triage (fix-all-7 decision); tracked here.

issues.title: namespace import resolved against final export state, not per-import-site snapshot (Codex review, PR #1020)
issues.body:
## Summary

Owner/Codex review on PR #1020 (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:1545`):

> A Tcl `namespace import` creates aliases from the export list that exists when the import executes. Later `namespace export -clear` does not revoke those aliases, and exporting a name after an earlier import does not add it retroactively. The resolver instead joins every import against the final `namespace_exports` vector, so both directions are wrong. For example, importing `::src::*` while `p` is exported, then clearing `src`'s exports, still leaves `p` callable in Tcl, but this code stops resolving it. Record the imported aliases/snapshot at each import site (with ordering) rather than consulting final export state.

## Repro (both directions are wrong)

**Direction A** — `namespace export -clear` after an import wrongly revokes:

```tcl
namespace eval ::src { proc p {} {} ; namespace export p }
namespace eval ::dst { namespace import ::src::* ; namespace export -clear }
::dst::p
```
Real Tcl: `::dst::p` is still callable (the import happened while `p` was exported). LSP: stops resolving it.

**Direction B** — exporting a name *after* an import wrongly adds it retroactively:

```tcl
namespace eval ::src { proc p {} {} }
namespace eval ::dst { namespace import ::src::* }
namespace eval ::src { namespace export p }
::dst::p
```
Real Tcl: `::dst::p` is NOT callable (`p` was not exported at import time). LSP: resolves it.

## Fix direction

Record the imported aliases (or an export snapshot) **at each import site, with ordering**, instead of joining every import against the final `namespace_exports` vector. This is the largest of the PR #1020 review items — a change to the import-resolution model in `definition.rs` / `references.rs` (and the workspace `resolve_wildcard_import` path).

Deferred from PR #1020 per owner triage (fix-all-7 decision); tracked here.

issues.title: `Traits` bit 61 is assigned twice: `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` aliases `TRANSFERS_CONTROL` (the `u64` is full)
issues.body:
## Summary

`tcl_registry::Traits` is a `bitflags` over `u64`, and **all 64 bits are allocated**. `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` was added on top of `TRANSFERS_CONTROL`'s bit, so the two are the *same flag* at run time:

```rust
// rust/tcl-registry/src/traits.rs
const TRANSFERS_CONTROL          = 1 << 61;   // line 306
...
const SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN         = 1 << 61;   // line 397
```

```
Traits is u64; bits used: 64, highest: 63
free bits 0..63: []
COLLISIONS: {61: ['TRANSFERS_CONTROL', 'SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN']}
```

`Traits::TRANSFERS_CONTROL == Traits::SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` evaluates to `true` today, so every `contains()` query for either trait answers for both.

## Impact

Both traits are live and both have consumers, so the aliasing is bidirectional. Observed against `registry_for_dialect("tcl9.0")`:

```
cd:         frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
exec:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
open:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
source:     frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
file:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
socket:     frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
exit:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
load:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
glob:       frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
pwd:        frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
encoding:   frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
unload:     frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
fconfigure: frame_sensitive=true  safe_hidden=true  transfers=true
---
break:      safe_hidden=true (wrong)  transfers=true
continue:   safe_hidden=true (wrong)  transfers=true
yield:      safe_hidden=true (wrong)  transfers=true
yieldto:    safe_hidden=true (wrong)  transfers=true
tailcall:   safe_hidden=true (wrong)  transfers=true
```

Two concrete consequences:

**1. Every safe-interp-hidden command is treated as control-transferring.**
`FRAME_SENSITIVE_TRAITS` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs:43`) unions `TRANSFERS_CONTROL`, so `is_frame_sensitive()` now returns `true` for all 31 specs carrying `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` — `cd`, `exec`, `open`, `source`, `file`, `socket`, `glob`, `load`, `pwd`, `encoding`, … None of them transfer control. The inline-proc code action and the inliner's splice-safety query consume this, so they are conservatively refusing to inline bodies containing any of those commands.

**2. Every control-transferring command is treated as hidden in a safe interpreter.**
The analyser's safe-interp visibility gate (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:292`) tests `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN`, so inside a `interp create -safe` evaluation body `break`, `continue`, `yield`, `yieldto`, and `tailcall` all look hidden. Per that gate's own comment the command is then flagged **W129** and *skipped entirely* — "no invocation record, no handler dispatch, no source / package / definition edges". That is a false W129 plus dropped analysis for five core keywords that C Tcl never hides (they are not in `tclBasic.c`'s `unsafeEnsembleCommands` row).

`rust/tcl-vm/tests/safe_interp_e2e.rs:211` documents the intended `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` set as 13 commands; it is currently indistinguishable from the `TRANSFERS_CONTROL` set.

## Cause

`Traits: u64` had no free bit left when `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` was added (issue #945 fault 7). `bitflags` does not reject a duplicate bit value — it treats it as a deliberate alias — so this compiled silently and no test caught it, because no test asserts the two traits are distinct.

## Suggested fix

Widen the backing integer and give `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` its own bit:

```rust
pub struct Traits: u128 {
    ...
    const SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN = 1 << 64;
}
```

`bitflags` supports `u128`, and `Traits` is a compile-time metadata field on specs that live in `.rodata`, so the extra 8 bytes per spec is the whole cost. Worth checking whether any consumer round-trips `Traits` through a `u64` (serialisation, the snapshot dump, FFI) before widening.

Whatever the fix, it wants a guard so this cannot recur — either a test asserting every pair of trait constants is distinct, or a `const` assertion that the count of declared bits equals `Traits::all().bits().count_ones()`.

## How this was found

While building the command-registry spec studio (`rust/tcl-spec-studio`), whose catalogue test asserted that each trait bit maps back to exactly one name. It reported `TRANSFERS_CONTROL` and `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` for one bit.

The studio deduplicates by bit value for now so a rendered `.rs` stays bit-identical to the spec it was seeded from, and pins the collision in `catalogue::tests::traits_catalogue_pins_the_known_bit_collision` — that test fails once `Traits` is widened, which is the cue to remove the workaround.

issues.title: Constructor typing is not rename-aware: `rename Dog Cat; set d [Cat new]; $d fly` draws no W308 (typing half of the PR #1045 liveness fix)
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #1045 made class **liveness** rename-aware: `class_live_by_name_for_call` consults the `renamed_commands` reverse map, so `set d [Dog new]; rename Dog Cat; $d fly` now correctly draws W308 (the object keeps its class through the rename of its class command). The **typing** side was deliberately left open: a constructor call under the *new* name is never typed at all, so the mirror shape still silently degrades.

## Repro (oracle-confirmed on tclsh8.6 and tclsh9.0)

```tcl
oo::class create Dog { method bark {} { return woof } }
rename Dog Cat
set d [Cat new]
$d fly
```

Real Tcl: `Cat new` works (rename re-establishes the class command under the new name), and `$d fly` fails with `unknown method "fly": must be bark or destroy` — a genuine, reachable method typo. Also `Dog new` after the rename fails `invalid command name "Dog"` (W123 fires correctly for that today).

Current analyser output: `W307 Non-literal command name — cannot statically analyze` on `$d fly`, **no W308**. The correct diagnostic is lost and replaced by noise.

## Root cause

`type_infer::constructor_object_type` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/type_infer.rs, ~:191-221) types `[X new]` only when `X ∈ known_classes`. `known_classes` is assembled by `collect_known_classes` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs, ~:1591) from class-creation statements only — `Cat` never enters the set, and neither `type_infer` nor `collect_known_classes` has access to the analyser's `renamed_commands` map (recorded by `handle_rename`, rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs ~:3444). So `d` gets no `Object(...)` type, and the dispatch site falls back to W307. During the PR #1045 review round this was initially misdiagnosed as a liveness bug; the liveness half is fixed, and instrumentation confirmed the residual is purely that the constructor is untyped.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the class-name resolution that feeds constructor typing alias-aware rather than threading analyser state deep into `type_infer`:
- When `collect_known_classes` (or a thin wrapper at the `CompilationUnit`/analyser boundary) has rename facts available, extend `known_classes` with alias entries: `Cat → ::Dog` (the class's canonical identity stays `::Dog` so `ClassDef`/method lookup keeps working), valid for call sites after the rename offset.
- Note offset sensitivity: `[Cat new]` *before* the `rename` must **not** type (real Tcl: `invalid command name "Cat"`), so a flat alias set is not enough — the same call-site-offset discipline the liveness gate now uses (`class_live_by_name_for_call`) should decide which name is live at the constructor call site. Reusing that predicate for name→class resolution may collapse both into one query.
- `interp alias {} Cat {} Dog` deserves the same treatment (the analyser already records `command_aliases`) — worth handling in the same change or explicitly documenting as out of scope.

## Verification bar

- The repro draws W308 naming class `::Dog` (or the aliased spelling) on `$d fly`, and no W307 for this shape.
- TN: `[Cat new]` before the rename stays untyped (no false W308; W123 on `Cat` fires).
- The PR #1045 tests stay green: `set d [Dog new]; rename Dog Cat; $d fly` (liveness half), the three issue-1013 gate tests, and the re-establishment FP guard.
- Oracle transcripts for 8.6 + 9.0; `cargo test -p tcl-compiler`; no new clippy allows.

## References

- PR #1045 review round, FIX item 5 (the agent's report explicitly scoped this out rather than half-fixing silently).
- Relevant code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/type_infer.rs` (`constructor_object_type`, `return_type_for_command`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/compilation_unit.rs` (`collect_known_classes`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs` (`handle_rename`), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs` (`class_live_by_name_for_call` — the offset-aware predicate to mirror or reuse).

issues.title: TclOO method-context dispatch keywords (`my`/`next`/`nextto`) are hardcoded string literals in two LSP consumers — needs a registry facility (pairs with #1026)
issues.body:
## Summary

Two consumer modules match the TclOO method-context dispatch keywords by literal string, violating the registry-first rule (AGENTS.md: per-command knowledge lives in `tcl-registry`, never as name literals in walkers):

1. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs` — the pre-existing `== "my"` and `h == "next" || h == "nextto"` matches in the dispatch-site scanners (`scan_my_method_sites` and friends).
2. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/call_hierarchy.rs:556` and `:962` — `matches!(head.as_str(), "my" | "next" | "nextto")`, added by the PR #1047 call-hierarchy work, which copied the existing pattern because **no registry facility exists to query instead**.

Flagged by the adversarial rules review of PR #1047: "a second file adopting the same debt is exactly what the rule is meant to prevent" — but correctly assessed as un-fixable today, since there is nothing in `tcl-registry` the code could call.

## Why this belongs with #1026

#1026 is the decision to model the `::oo::Helpers` family (`link`/`my`/`next`/`self`) as qualified, method-context-only specs with a method-body candidate-generation path, instead of today's global specs. That work necessarily creates exactly the registry vocabulary this issue needs: a way to ask "is this head word a method-context dispatch keyword under this dialect, and what kind?" (`my` → instance self-dispatch; `next`/`nextto` → superclass chain — the specs already carry `Traits::TCLOO_NEXT_CHAIN`; `self` → introspection, not dispatch). Doing #1026 without also converting these two consumers would leave the literals stranded against a registry that now knows the answer.

## Suggested fix direction

- As part of (or immediately after) #1026: add the query surface — either a `Traits` bit per role (`TCLOO_SELF_DISPATCH` already half-exists via `TCLOO_NEXT_CHAIN`) or a small `ProfileQueries` method (`method_dispatch_keyword(head) -> Option<MethodDispatchKind>`), dialect-aware (all are TclOO-era, 8.6+; `link`-created barewords are per-class data, not keywords).
- Convert both consumers to the query; grep for further literal matches (`"my"`, `"next"`, `"nextto"`, `"self"`) across `tcl-lsp-core`/`tcl-compiler` while there — `oo_body.rs`, `definition.rs`, and the analyser's method-scope handling are the likely other holders.
- Guard with a registry contract test: the keyword set the consumers see must equal the specs carrying the relevant trait, so a new dialect's variant (e.g. an itcl equivalent) propagates without touching walkers.

## Verification bar

- Zero string-literal matches for these keywords in consumer dispatch paths (enforced by the contract test or a grep-based lint note).
- All existing `my`-dispatch and call-hierarchy tests (30 in `call_hierarchy.rs` alone) stay green.
- `make check-all`; no new clippy allows.

## References

- PR #1047 adversarial rules review, finding 3. AGENTS.md "The registry is the source of truth". #1026 (the `oo::Helpers` modelling decision this should ride with).

issues.title: Multi-word `eval` (word-concatenation form) draws false E002/W210 — the analyser reads only the first argument as the script
issues.body:
## Summary

Tcl's `eval` concatenates **all** its arguments (list-style, space-joined) into the script it runs. The analyser instead treats `eval`'s first argument alone as the script body, so the multi-word form produces a cascade of false positives — including an **error-severity** E002.

Found by the adversarial C Tcl fidelity review of the PR #1045-#1047 round (finding 9). Pre-existing — not introduced by those PRs — but squarely on the same `scan_script`/eval-modelling surface they touched, and unfiled until now.

## Repro (oracle-confirmed on tclsh8.6 and tclsh9.0)

```tcl
eval set l2 hello
puts $l2
```

Real Tcl: prints `hello` — `eval` concatenates `set l2 hello` and runs it; `l2` is set.

Analyser output:
```
1:6: error   E002  Too few arguments for 'set': expected at least 1, got 0 — usage: set varName ?value?
2:6: warning W210  Variable 'l2' is read before it is set
```

Both wrong. The braced form `eval {set l2 hello}` is analysed correctly. Note the sibling command `uplevel` already handles this correctly by *declining*: `try_lower_uplevel_static` returns `None` for multi-word bodies and falls back to a conservative barrier (verified in the same review, probe `upmw.tcl`) — `eval` should be at least that conservative, and can be more precise.

## Root cause

The `eval` handling path (analyser hook / `ArgRole::Body` treatment of `eval`'s first argument) segments argument 0 as a complete script. With `set` as word 0 of a one-word "script", the remaining real words (`l2 hello`) are analysed as... nothing — `set` appears zero-argument (E002), and the `l2` write is never recorded (W210 downstream, plus any dead-store/liveness consumers of the same facts).

## Suggested fix direction (registry-first)

Model concatenating script commands as data, not a special case:
- Add a registry marker (a `Traits` bit such as `CONCATENATES_SCRIPT_ARGS`, or an `ArgRole` variant) on `eval` — and audit the same family: `uplevel` (post-level words), `interp eval` (post-path words), `namespace inscope` (post-namespace words) — they all concatenate trailing words per Tcl's `Tcl_ConcatObj` semantics.
- In the analyser/scanners: when every trailing word is a static literal (bare/braced with no substitution), join with single spaces per concat semantics and analyse the joined text as the script (offset mapping: either per-word range attribution or fall back to whole-command spans for diagnostics inside the joined script).
- When any word is dynamic, decline like `uplevel` does today (no E002, no false definedness facts) rather than mis-analysing word 0.

## Verification bar

- The repro produces zero diagnostics (or at most an advisory), and `l2` is a recorded write feeding W210/dead-store correctly.
- TP guard: `eval {set}` (genuinely arity-broken script) still draws E002.
- TN guard: `eval $cmd arg` (dynamic) declines — no arity or definedness claims.
- Same matrix for `uplevel 1 set x 5` and `interp eval foo set x 5` if the family marker lands in the same change.
- Oracle transcripts 8.6 + 9.0; `cargo test -p tcl-compiler`; no new clippy allows.

## References

- Adversarial review probe `evx.tcl` (PR #1045-#1047 round, finding 9).
- Relevant code: the analyser's `eval` handling (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs` `handle_eval`-family / `ArgRole::Body` dispatch), `rust/tcl-compiler/src/var_escape/walker.rs:203` (which already joins args with spaces — the correct model, inconsistently applied), `try_lower_uplevel_static` (the conservative precedent).

issues.title: `body_has_dynamic_barrier` matches `uplevel` by name literal and re-implements the level-word sniff, diverging from the registry's arg_role_resolver
issues.body:
## Summary

`rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/mod.rs:487` (inside `body_has_dynamic_barrier`):

```rust
let body_idx = if name == "uplevel" || name == "::uplevel" { … } else { args.len() - 1 };
```

This violates the registry-first rule (AGENTS.md) and duplicates knowledge the registry already models precisely: `uplevel`'s `arg_role_resolver` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/uplevel_.rs:141-148`) returns the script index after the optional level word, and `registry.arg_indices_for_role("uplevel", args, ArgRole::Body)` is contract-tested for all five call shapes (`registry.rs:2149-2183`). The literal also:

- misses `uplevel` reached through a namespace path spelling, and
- re-implements the level-word sniff with a *different* heuristic from the registry's, so the two can disagree on which word is the script.

Errors here are conservative (the flag only decides whether to decline a lowering relaxation), so this is debt with low blast radius rather than a user-visible bug — hence filed separately from the #1050/#1051 round it was found in (gap review finding C4).

## Suggested fix direction

Replace the literal with `arg_indices_for_role(name, args, ArgRole::Body)` from the registry handle the lowerer already holds, and delete the local level-word heuristic. A unit test should pin that the registry-resolved index and the lowering behaviour agree for `uplevel`, `uplevel 1`, `uplevel #0`, and the multi-word forms.

## References

- #1050 / #1051 (the registry-first round this was found in).
- Gap review finding C4, 2026-07-29 session.

issues.title: VM: `namespace inscope` space-joins its trailing args — C Tcl list-appends them (`concat script [list args…]`)
issues.body:
## Summary

`rust/tcl-vm/src/cmd_namespace.rs:376-392` implements `namespace inscope`'s trailing arguments with a plain space-join:

```rust
let body = parts.iter().map(|v| v.to_str().to_string())
    .collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
```

That is correct for `ns_eval` (line 394 — `namespace eval` *is* a concat) but wrong for `ns_inscope`: C Tcl 9 builds `Tcl_ConcatObj(script, Tcl_NewListObj(extra_args))`, i.e. the extra args are appended as **list elements** (`namespace inscope ::foo $s $x` ≡ `namespace eval ::foo [concat $s [list $x]]`). The `namespace code` idiom generates exactly this shape for callbacks, so it occurs in real code.

## Repro (oracle: tclsh 9.0)

```tcl
namespace eval ::n {proc p {a} {return $a}}
namespace inscope ::n p {x y}
```

Real Tcl 9: runs `p {x y}` → returns `x y` (one argument). This VM: joins to `p x y` → "wrong # args". Also divergent for any tail word containing a space, brace, or `$`.

## Suggested fix direction

List-quote each trailing word before appending (the VM has list-building helpers), matching `Tcl_ConcatObj(script, Tcl_NewListObj(...))`. Good differential-fuzz seed for `rust/tcl-fuzz` once fixed.

Note: the analyser-side sibling (multi-word `namespace inscope` mis-analysed as a script walk of the first word) is being fixed in the #1051 round; this issue is the VM's runtime semantics only.

## References

- #1051 (analyser-side family fix).
- Gap review finding D3, 2026-07-29 session.

issues.title: runtime/rust: command-resolution conformance vector fails — braced proc name corrupts dispatch (`invalid command name "if"`)
issues.body:
## Summary

`cmd_namespace::tests::dispatch_matches_every_conformance_vector` in the standalone `runtime/rust` crate fails on vector line 21:

```
proc {p} {} { return {::p} }
if {[catch {::p} __r]} { set __r - }
puts $__r

error: invalid command name "if"
```

The runtime errors with `invalid command name "if"` — the *builtin* `if` stops resolving after a proc is defined via a braced name word (`proc {p} …`), which suggests the braced name corrupts the command-table registration or the subsequent dispatch path rather than just the one proc.

## Not a regression

Verified failing identically at `6fdd4f12` (the current shared tip) with the same assertion — pre-existing, discovered while running `make runtime-rust-test` as a pre-PR gate for the #1048–#1051 round (2026-07-29). The other 324 runtime lib tests pass.

## Notes for the fix

- The vectors come from the shared `tcl_syntax::naming::conformance` module (`rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs:908-1000`), which exists precisely so every backend resolves names identically — so this is a real conformance divergence, not a test artefact.
- Real Tcl 9: `proc {p} {} { return {::p} }` defines a command literally named `p` (the braces are word quoting), and `::p` then resolves fine; `if` is of course unaffected.
- Suspect area: `runtime/rust/src/cmd_namespace.rs` dispatch/registration around name normalisation of the defining word.

issues.title: Go-to-definition ignores `rename` for procs and classes (single-file path) — `resolve_class_target_at` / `lookup_alias` need the rename hop
issues.body:
## Summary

Single-file go-to-definition follows `interp alias` but not `rename`, for both procs and classes:

- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:1711` — `resolve_class_target_at` resolves only through `bareword_resolution_candidates` + wildcard imports; it never consults `analysis.renamed_commands`.
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:990` — `lookup_alias` looks up `command_aliases` by name only, with no rename hop.

The workspace path (`workspace_index.rs:561-593`) indexes both maps, so behaviour differs depending on whether the workspace index has been populated — an observable inconsistency, not just a missing feature.

## Repros

```tcl
proc ::impl {} { puts hi }
rename ::impl ::newname
newname                 ;# go-to-definition here → nothing
```

```tcl
oo::class create ::Impl { method go {} {} }
rename ::Impl ::Thing
set o [Thing new]       ;# go-to-definition on `Thing` → nothing
```

Real Tcl 9: `Tcl_RenameCommand` moves the command entry; `::newname` / `::Thing` are the live names.

## Models to follow

- `validity.rs:2006-2060` documents the hop rules, including the alias-vs-rename re-resolution asymmetry (an alias re-resolves by name every call; a rename moves the command once), verified against tclsh 9.0.4.
- `class_reachable_by_indirection` (added by PR #1062 for #1049's constructor typing) is a ready-made template with the hop cap and offset order-gate already right.
- Partial coverage by a different route exists: `preview_tickets_e2e.rs:787` resolves a *dynamic* `rename $old ::foo` via the const-dispatch settle path — the static `rename ::impl ::newname` proc case and the class case are the gaps.

Related smaller cleanup while in the file: several sites call `registry_for_dialect("")` where the real document dialect could be threaded (correct today only because `PLAIN_TCL`'s mask is `ALL_TCL`; documented at the shared `method_dispatch_keyword_in` helper added in PR #1062).

Deferred from the #1049/#1050/#1051 round (PR #1062) as the explicitly-scoped stretch item.

issues.title: uplevel level-word recognition: 8.6/9.0 divergence on `-1`, and `+1`/`-0`/` 1` accepted by C Tcl but rejected by word_is_literal_level
issues.body:
Found while converting `body_has_dynamic_barrier` to registry arg-roles (PR #1068; transcripts pinned in a test comment there).

Two precision gaps in the registry's `word_is_literal_level` (first byte `#` or digit):

1. **`uplevel -1` is a genuine C Tcl version divergence.** tclsh 8.6.14 treats `-1` as *not a level* and runs it as a command name (`uplevel -1 {set x 1}` → `invalid command name "-1"` only if undefined — it dispatches!), while tclsh 9.0.4 errors `bad level "-1"` (changed `TclObjGetFrame`). The registry currently rejects `-1` as a level in all dialects, which matches 9.0 but not 8.6's dispatch-as-command behaviour.
2. **Both versions accept `+1`, `-0`, and whitespace-padded levels** (` 1`) as levels; `word_is_literal_level` rejects all of these, so e.g. `uplevel +1 {…}` is mis-shaped (the level word gets treated as the script start).

The fix belongs in the registry's level-word data/callback (per-dialect if needed for the `-1` divergence), with the arg-role resolver consuming it — no consumer changes should be needed. Pin the full matrix (`1`, `#0`, `+1`, `-0`, `-1`, ` 1`, `x`) against both interpreters per dialect.

issues.title: False W210 on apply lambda parameters in bare-statement position: `apply {{a} {puts $a}} 5` reads `a` as read-before-set
issues.body:
Found while fixing audit idx 0 (PR #1068).

`apply {{a} {puts $a}} 5` as a bare top-level statement draws `W210 Variable 'a' is read before it is set` — the lambda's parameter binding isn't credited as a write on the top-level `handle_apply_command` path. The command-substitution form `set r [apply {{a} {puts $a}} 5]` is clean (it goes through `descend_command`'s lambda-literal descent, which models the body correctly).

The two paths should share one lambda-body analysis that seeds the parameter list (including `args` and defaulted params per `proc` semantics) as writes before walking the body. Pre-existing before #1068; repro pinned there in a test comment but not fixed to keep that PR scoped.

issues.title: lower_proc homes a body-defined proc to its lexical namespace, not its defining namespace (W214 names the wrong FQN)
issues.body:
Split out of audit idx 45 during PR #1075: the finding had two independent root causes, and only the order-sensitivity half was in scope there. This is the other half.

`lowering/mod.rs::lower_proc` resolves a proc defined inside another proc's body against the lexical namespace at the definition site, but Tcl resolves the name in the namespace current *when the body executes* — for the common `proc outer {} { proc inner {} {…} }` at top level they agree, but a body evaluated under `namespace eval`/`uplevel` re-homing diverges, and W214's reported FQN is wrong for those shapes.

Fix direction: the lowering should consume the same defining-context fact the analyser's `register_proc_definition` (post-#1075) records, rather than re-deriving lexical position. Oracle-pin the divergent shapes on 9.0/8.6 first.

issues.title: Naming layer normalises brace-literal variable names: `set {$n} 1` lands defs/reads/rename/highlighting on `n`
issues.body:
Found and measured during PR #1076's review round; recorded with measurements in `docs/design/compiler/ssa-construction.md` ("Known limitation") — filing so it's schedulable.

Tcl treats a brace-quoted `{$n}` as the literal variable name `$n`, distinct from `n` (oracle: `set {$n} v; puts [set {$n}]` → `v`; `info exists n` → 0; an array key `{arr($i)}` stays literal). The shared naming helper (`element_var_name_braced`) normalises the braced spelling down to `n`, so every consumer keys the wrong variable. The barrier-side FP was fixed in #1076, but the naming layer itself still mis-keys: the measured one-parameter fix produced a missed true positive (`set {$n} 1; puts $n` — tclsh errors, we say nothing) plus two new false W220s, so it was reverted rather than half-landed.

A proper fix must teach the naming layer that a braced literal keeps its `$`, and land across defs, reads, rename, and semantic highlighting together, with the #1076 measurements as the acceptance tests. Related family: the computed parameter-list stub `VarDef` issue (filed separately) — both are "the analyser keys a variable by the wrong spelling".

issues.title: Analyser records a stub VarDef named after a computed parameter-list word (`proc p [makeargs] {}` → VarDef literally named "[makeargs]")
issues.body:
Found during PR #1073's review round. For a computed formal-parameter list — `proc p [makeargs] {}`, `proc q $params {…}` — the analyser reads the unresolved word as a one-parameter literal and registers a stub `VarDef` whose *name is the source text* (`"[makeargs]"`, `"$params"`) with its definition span over that word. The LSP now refuses to trust it (#1073 suppresses the bareword-declaration step for `Computed` parameter lists in `position_definition` and `variable_hover`), but the stub itself remains a wrong analyser fact that any future consumer could trip over.

Fix: a computed parameter list should register no per-parameter `VarDef`s (arity unknown, names unknown) — the proc's params are simply unmodelled, the same abstention the arity checker already applies. Regression tests exist in `mathfunc_and_word_recognition.rs` (the `Computed` classification tests) to build on. Related family: the brace-literal naming issue (filed separately).

issues.title: `self method` members missing from the document-symbol outline
issues.body:
Noted in audit idx 96's own finding text and confirmed during PR #1074: a `self method NAME …` inside an `oo::class create`/`oo::define` body (a class method on the class object itself) is analysed for dispatch (classmethod machinery finds it) but never appears in the document outline, unlike ordinary `method`/`classmethod` members.

Small, self-contained: the definer grammar already classifies the member; the document-symbols walker just doesn't emit a node for the `self`-scoped shape. Emit it with the same kind/detail convention `classmethod` uses, TP outline test plus a TN that plain `self` introspection calls don't produce symbols.

issues.title: Rename doesn't rewrite cross-file `$::ns::var` sites (the workspace variable tier now provides the reference set)
issues.body: Follow-up from the cross-document tiers PR: definition/hover/references for qualified namespace variables now work cross-file via the workspace `WorkspaceVariable`/`WorkspaceVariableRef` tables, but `core_rename::rename` still takes a single `AnalysisResult`, so renaming a namespace variable from its declaring file leaves cross-file `$::ns::v` reads stale. Audit idx 65 raised this as plausible-but-untested; the reference set needed to do it correctly now exists, so this is a contained wiring follow-up — route rename's edit collection through the same `qualified_variable_cell_at` + workspace-ref tier, with the usual rename safety conventions (tail-only edits, no delimiter rewrites).

issues.title: Namespace names are not navigable symbols: `namespace children ::tomato` resolves to nothing
issues.body: Split out of audit idx 75's secondary claim during the cross-document tiers work: a namespace *name* as a bare argument (`namespace children ::tomato`, `namespace exists`, `namespace eval` targets from a call site, etc.) has no definition/hover/references answer even in a single file — namespaces aren't modelled as navigable symbols at all. Distinct from the qualified-variable tier (which landed): this needs namespace declarations as first-class indexed symbols with the registry's namespace-name arg-roles marking which argument positions reference them. Single-file first; the workspace tier follows the established qualified-only pattern.

issues.title: Rename safety gate skips pure-consumer documents: an untracked-receiver dispatch living only in a consumer file doesn't refuse
issues.body:
Residual from the rename safety gate PR (#1091), documented in STATUS.md §6b — filing so it's schedulable.

`Backend::method_rename_refusal` runs the hazard scan over the request's document plus every override-family document the index names (files declaring part of the class). But the *edit collector* also rewrites call sites in pure-consumer documents — files that call the method without declaring any part of the class. Those documents are never hazard-scanned, so an untracked-receiver dispatch (`set other [lindex $args 0]; [$other X]`) living only in a consumer file slips past the gate: rename applies, and the consumer file's dynamic dispatch breaks at runtime — exactly the idx 79 failure mode, one document over.

Fix direction: a `Backend::consumer_scan_plan` that feeds the gate the same document set the edit collector uses, so scan coverage and edit coverage are equal by construction. FP e2e test: hazard only in a consumer document → refusal; FN guard: consumer documents with only tracked/literal dispatches still rename.

issues.title: Namespace-variable rename refusal for dynamic names is blunter than needed (per-site provenance would allow safe renames)
issues.body:
Residual from the rename safety gate PR (#1091), documented in STATUS.md §6b — filing so it's schedulable.

`rename_safety::namespace_variable_rename_hazard` refuses a namespace-variable rename whenever a registry `VarWrite`/`VarRead` word beside the cell names a dynamic variable (`dynamic_names::names_a_dynamic_variable`) — e.g. `variable $n` inside the namespace. The refusal is *correct* (oracle-pinned: `namespace eval ns { variable v 1; proc bump {n} {variable $n; set $n 2} }; ns::bump v` really does reach the cell), but it's blunt: any dynamic variable word in the namespace refuses, even when dataflow can prove the dynamic name can never spell this cell's tail.

The command-side already has the finer treatment — `WorkspaceInvocation`'s `rename_safe` per-site provenance. The variable side should get the same: consult the `DynamicNameBarrier` lattice / dominating-constant facts to prove the dynamic word's value set excludes the renamed tail, and refuse only when it can't. Abstain-toward-refuse stays the rule; this just shrinks the abstention set.

Enhancement, not a soundness bug — the current behaviour never produces a wrong edit, only unnecessary refusals.

issues.title: `namespace qualifiers` / `namespace tail` have no const_fold (blocks the ticklecharts `${ns}::setdef` chain)
issues.body:
Found during the `[self class]` folding PR (#1095): issue #1080 asserted these "already fold" — verified false. With `[self class]` now folding, the real-corpus chain `set ns [namespace qualifiers [self class]]; ${ns}::setdef …` (ticklecharts; audit idx 44/54's mechanic) still stops after the inner hop because `namespace qualifiers`/`namespace tail` have no fold callback.

The full edge-case behaviour is already oracle-pinned (9.0.4 + 8.6, identical) and captured in #1095's probe transcripts, ready to become the acceptance tests:

| input | `qualifiers` | `tail` |
|---|---|---|
| `:::` | `{}` | `{}` |
| `a:::b` | `a` | `b` |
| `::a::b::` | `::a::b` | `{}` |
| `::x:y` | `{}` | `x:y` |

Fix direction: registry fold callbacks on both subcommands (same `CommandSpec` fold surface `string`/`expr` folds use), string-math only — no namespace existence checks (the commands are pure string operations, per the man page and the transcript). Second blocker for the full chain is tracked separately: variable propagation inside method bodies needs the instance-variable escaping model.

issues.title: Block-scoped `export`/`unexport` inside `self { … }` abstains — `set_member_visibility` flips both instance and class-side tables by bare name
issues.body:
Residual from #1095, pinned there by `self_block_member_records_but_block_scoped_unexport_abstains`. The `self { method … }` block form now records members through the normal path, but an `export`/`unexport` written *inside* the block abstains: `set_member_visibility` flips visibility by bare member name across **both** the instance-side and class-side tables, so honouring a block-scoped (class-side-only) `unexport` would also wrongly un-export an identically-named instance method the block never touched.

Fix direction: give `set_member_visibility` a side parameter (instance / class-object) and have every caller pass the side it's scoped to — the block expansion (`expand_wrapper_block_members`) then routes its visibility members to the class side only. Oracle to pin first: `oo::class create C { method m {} {}; self { method m {} {}; unexport m } }` — verify with `info object methods ::C` / `info class methods ::C` and dispatch which of the two `m`s each form reaches on 9.0 and 8.6.

issues.title: Method rename edit/gate coverage is bounded by `documents_invoking_classes` — instances handed across documents without a constructor call are invisible
issues.body:
Residual from PR #1091's review round (documented in the fix, filing per the always-file rule). After that round the rename safety gate provably scans the same document set the edit collector rewrites (`consumer_scan_plan`: override family + inheritors + consumers). But both legs share one ceiling: consumers are found by `documents_invoking_classes`, i.e. a document must invoke a family constructor (`Dog new`/`Dog create`) *in its own text* to be a candidate.

A consumer that receives an instance without constructing it — via a global variable, a dict entry, a callback registered in another file, a proc parameter fed from elsewhere — is in none of the candidate sources, so its dispatches are neither rewritten (missed edit → runtime `unknown method` after rename) nor scanned for hazards (gate can't refuse what it can't see). The gate currently equals the collector, which was the #1092 fix; this issue is about both being bounded by the same missing fact.

Fix direction: cross-document **instance provenance** in the workspace index — track object-handle flow across documents (return values, parameters, globals holding instances of indexed classes), the interprocedural analogue of what `object_handle_classes` does within a compilation unit. Overlaps deliberately with #994 (type-map unification): the lattice #994 wants to surface for references/rename is the natural carrier for this fact — consider designing them together when #994 is picked up.

issues.title: Unwrapped `deletemethod`/`renamemethod` in class bodies are ignored — deleted methods stay in the outline and navigation
issues.body:
Pre-existing gap surfaced (and pinned) during PR #1095's review round: `apply_oo_subcommand` has no arm for `deletemethod`/`renamemethod`, so `oo::class create ::C { method gone {} {}; deletemethod gone }` and `oo::define ::C { deletemethod gone }` both retain `gone` in the `ClassDef` — stale document symbol, and navigation/method validation answer a method that doesn't exist. The **wrapped** forms (`self deletemethod`, `self { … deletemethod … }`, `private { … }`) were fixed in #1095's review round via the new `MemberSpec::retracts_named_members` registry flag.

Oracle (9.0.4/8.6.16, pinned in #1095's transcripts): the unwrapped forms really delete/rename on the instance side; retracting a not-yet-declared member is a hard error that aborts the whole definition (`method ghost does not exist`), so declare-then-retract is the only legal order and no ordering state is needed.

Fix: one more `apply_oo_subcommand` arm keyed on `retracts_named_members` (already in place), dropping from `methods`/`class_methods` per the member's side — ~5 lines, but it changes the recorded shape of plain class bodies that neither #1095 nor its review touched, so it wants its own review with TP/TN outline + navigation tests. `renamemethod old new` should drop `old` and record nothing for `new` (false negative over false positive). The residual is pinned by `unwrapped_destructive_members_are_a_documented_residual`, which fails loudly if fixed without updating the note.

issues.title: Import-edge lifecycle is not modelled: `namespace forget`, `-force` shadowing, source rename/delete following, import chains
issues.body:
Residuals from PR #1102 (per-import-site export snapshots), each oracle-confirmed in that PR's matrix (9.0.4 + 8.6.14 identical). The import edge is currently a static name-visibility fact; real Tcl makes it a *live link* with a lifecycle, and four behaviours fall out of that:

1. **`namespace forget` is not modelled at all.** `namespace forget ::src::p` removes the alias — a later bare call is `invalid command name` — but nothing is recorded (the registry has the subcommand; there's no analyser hook), so navigation keeps resolving a forgotten name.
2. **`namespace import -force` / conflict semantics.** A non-`-force` import onto an existing command *errors* (everything after it never runs); `-force` silently replaces the local command, so a later bare call reaches `::src::p`, not the same-named local (`namespace origin` → the source). The resolver has no notion of an import shadowing a local definition.
3. **Source rename/delete/redefine after import is not followed.** The alias holds the command token: `rename ::src::p ::src::pp` keeps `::dst::p` working, `rename ::src::p {}` kills it, and a redefinition is seen through the link. The import edge is not run through `analyser::indirection`, which already models exactly this for `rename`/`interp alias`.
4. **Import chains abstain.** A imports `::B::*`, B imported `::C::*`: `::A::p` runs C's body and `namespace origin` follows to `::C::p`. Statically the middle hop isn't in `all_procs`, so the export gate passes and the proc lookup fails — safe, but a missed navigation.

Fix direction: make the import edge an indirection-tracked link on the same ordered event log #1102 introduced — `forget` and `-force` are lifecycle events beside the export tombstones, and rename-following/chains come from routing the edge through `indirection`'s existing latest-binding-wins machinery rather than new code.

issues.title: Wildcard-import gating precision: call-site ordering not gated, single-file simple-name fallback masks the gate, cross-file exports unordered
issues.body:
Residuals from PR #1102 (per-import-site export snapshots), oracle-confirmed there. The new gate decides "was this name exported when the import ran"; three orthogonal leniencies remain around it:

1. **Call-site ordering is not gated.** A bare call written *before* its `namespace import` still resolves through it (oracle: first call `invalid command name`, post-import call works). Deliberately out of scope in #1102: `WorkspaceIndex::resolve_wildcard_import` receives no call-site offset, so gating only in-document would make the two tiers disagree — the fix is plumbing the call offset into the workspace entry point and applying `in_effect` on both.
2. **`fallback_proc_by_simple_name` masks the gate for single-file go-to-definition.** With the source proc in the same document, `resolve_called_proc`'s lenient tail-match answers regardless of import/export state, so #1027's Direction-B false positive is still visible via single-file `textDocument/definition` (references and cross-document definition flip correctly). Pre-existing, documented leniency; tightening it needs care not to break the deliberate same-file fallbacks other tests pin.
3. **Cross-file exports are unordered.** There is no static order between one file's import and another file's export, so foreign patterns count and foreign `-clear`s revoke nothing — abstention toward answering. A `source`-graph / `package require`-derived partial order could tighten this where a load order is provable.

Also noted in #1102, same surface, minor: imports rooted at the global namespace (`namespace import ::p`) are skipped by both tiers; dynamic export patterns (`namespace export $pat`) are skipped, so a post-`-clear` snapshot may miss names they covered (deliberate abstention); a body-local `namespace export -clear` forces a full per-item rebuild (correct but an incremental-analysis pessimisation).

issues.title: Variable reference completeness: `[set X]` reads unrecorded in scope references; cursor inside a brace-literal name answers empty
issues.body:
Two find-references completeness gaps surfaced while fixing #1078 in PR #1106 (neither produces a wrong answer post-#1106; both drop true sites):

1. **`[set X]` reads are not recorded as `VarDef.references`** in the analyser scope model — for both spellings (verified: plain `set m 1; puts [set m]` leaves `f::m` with `refs=[]`). The diagnostics-side scanners see these reads (post-#1106); the scope model's reference list doesn't, so Find References under-reports. Pre-existing, now at parity between spellings.
2. **A cursor inside a brace-quoted name word returns `[]`** — `find_var_at_position` reads the inner `$n` of `{$n}` as an ordinary `$`-reference to plain `n`, finds no such cell, and answers nothing. No longer wrong (it used to answer the merged set), but incomplete: it should answer the literal `$n` cell's own sites. Rename already covers this cursor via the #1106 typed refusal.

Fix direction: record `[set X]` argument reads through the same registry `VarRead` role path the diagnostics scanners use (one recording site, not a second scanner), and teach `find_var_at_position` the braced-word case using `naming::element_var_name_braced` so the cursor resolves the literal cell.

issues.title: Namespace navigation coverage refinements: implicit parents, `namespace path` lists, computed targets, apply-lambda namespace element
issues.body:
Four coverage residuals from PR #1112 (#1088's namespace-symbol tier), each documented there and oracle-grounded:

1. **Implicit parent namespaces have no declaring site.** `namespace eval ::p::q::r {}` really creates `::p::q` (both interpreters), but its name is written nowhere, so navigation on `namespace children ::p::q` abstains rather than jumping into the middle of another namespace's word. Needs a synthetic declaration identity the span model currently has no place for (e.g. the covering prefix of the deepest written name, surfaced as a labelled "implicitly created by" answer).
