2. **`namespace path {::a ::b}` is unmarked** — the argument is a *list* of namespace names inside one word, and `ArgRole` marks whole words; the subcommand stays unannotated rather than half-marked. Needs list-element role granularity (also the shape `oo::Helpers` path handling touches).
3. **Computed targets (`namespace eval $ns {…}`) resolve nowhere by design** — the analyser's per-site `@dynns@<offset>` domain could carry the constant-dominated case, the idx-44 treatment already applied to command heads.
4. **An `apply` lambda's third list element names a namespace** (`apply {{x} {…} ::ns}`) — the analyser models its semantics (`namespace_overrides`) but not its reference identity; it sits inside an `ArgRole::LambdaLiteral` word no whole-word role reaches. Same granularity gap as (2).

issues.title: Namespace rename tier: renaming a namespace must rewrite every qualified name beneath it, with the refusal gate for what it can't prove
issues.body:
Residual from PR #1112: the namespace-symbol tier covers definition/hover/references only — rename is deliberately unwired. Renaming a namespace is a materially larger design than the variable tier's: every `namespace eval` block on the name, every qualified proc/variable/class name beneath it (`::old::p` → `::new::p`, including partially-qualified spellings resolved through the enclosing context), every `NamespaceName`-role argument, import/export patterns naming it, and `namespace code`/callback strings that embed it.

The safety story is the #1091 refusal precedent: refuse with a typed reason when any occurrence is unprovable — dynamic targets (`namespace eval $ns`), string-embedded names the analyser can't span (callback scripts), implicit-parent identities (#1113), and collisions with an existing namespace. The #1102 event-log ordering and #1112's `WorkspaceNamespaceRef` table provide the reference set; the gate needs the same scan-coverage-equals-edit-coverage discipline as #1092.

Suggested slotting: after the C6/C7 import-edge work (rename must understand import lifecycles to rewrite import patterns safely).

issues.title: Import-lifecycle gating precision: in-document -force observability, exact-link forget-gating, workspace removal ordering, error control flow, dynamic forget patterns
issues.body:
Residuals from PR #1115 (#1103's import-edge lifecycle), each documented there:

1. **In-document `-force` shadowing needs the export declaration visible in the same document.** `ForcedShadow` presumes the export when the source namespace is wholly unobservable in-file (the in-document twin of `observable_namespaces`), but when the namespace is *partly* observable with its export in another file, the shadow doesn't fire and single-file go-to-definition still answers the local. Cross-document is handled.
2. **Exact-import links are not forget-gated cross-document.** `live_command_links` is a whole-index liveness mask with no call site, so `namespace forget` can't revoke a `WorkspaceCommandLink`; only the glob path (which gets a `CallSite`) applies removals. Abstains toward the link existing.
3. **Workspace-tier removals are ordered by plain offset, not `in_effect_within`** — the index stores an enclosing-body span per import row, not per invocation (O(procs × invocations) to do better at index time). Safe direction (a removal can only look not-yet-run), but a body-local call after a top-level forget in the same file keeps resolving.
4. **Import-error control flow unmodelled** — a failed non-`-force` import aborts the rest of its script; only "installed nothing" is modelled.
5. **Dynamic forget patterns (`namespace forget $pat`) are skipped**, matching dynamic export patterns.

Items 1–3 share machinery with #1104 (call-site ordering, which #1115 made nearly free — `alias_live_at` gates removals only, and applying `in_effect` to installs is a one-line change awaiting its own corpus before/after); consider folding this into C7's round.

issues.title: W-code for definition-aborting TclOO bodies (retract-first, cross-side retraction, rename-onto-existing)
issues.body:
Residual from PR #1118. Real Tcl aborts the whole class definition — no class is created at all — for three oracle-pinned shapes (9.0.4/8.6.14 identical): `deletemethod ghost` before `method ghost` (`method ghost does not exist`), `deletemethod` of a member that exists only on the other side (same error — unlike `export`/`unexport`, whose cross-side form is a silent no-op), and `renamemethod a b` onto an existing `b` (`method called b already exists`). The analyser currently records a *partial* class in each case and emits no diagnostic — so the outline shows a class that can never exist.

Now that member sides are modelled (#1118's `MemberSide`), detecting all three is cheap at the retraction site: the retract call knows whether the name is present in its side's table. Emit a W-code ("this class definition cannot run: …"), keep recording the partial class for navigation resilience (consistent with how parse errors degrade), and TN-pin the legal orders (declare-then-retract; rename onto a fresh name; cross-side visibility words). Abstain for dynamic member names.

issues.title: `renamemethod old new` records nothing for the new name — no outline entry, hover, or navigation target
issues.body:
Residual from PR #1118, deliberate at the time (false negative over false positive, per campaign direction): `renamemethod old new` drops `old` from the member table and records nothing for `new`, so a method Tcl really dispatches (`[::C new] new` → runs the old body; oracle-pinned in #1118) has no outline entry, hover, or navigation target.

Fix: move the source `MethodDef` under the new name with a synthetic name span anchored at the `renamemethod`'s new-name word (the natural go-to-definition target for the renamed member), keeping the body span pointing at the original method body so navigation lands somewhere real. Cross-side and rename-onto-existing are definition-aborting errors (see #1120) and stay out. Pin dispatch + outline + hover on the renamed name, both dialects.

issues.title: Per-item corpus differential is red on `rust`: 45 tcllib files diverge between `analyse_per_item` and `analyse` (offset-carrying synthetic names, interp/dynns identities)
issues.body:
Found while gating stage C5a of #994, and A/B-proved **pre-existing**: `cargo test -p tcl-compiler --test per_item_corpus -- --ignored` (the corpus-gated byte-identity differential over `tmp/` tcllib) fails with **45 findings on `origin/rust` base and the C5a commit alike — identical file sets, identical structural divergences** (the only run-to-run variance is the describer sampling different HashMap entries for its `global_scope[line N: …]` quote, which is itself worth making deterministic).

Dominant divergence classes across the 45 files:
- **Offset-carrying synthetic names differ by construction**: `@dynclass@152` (per-item, body-relative) vs `@dynclass@1538` (full, absolute), same for `@dynns@` and `@interp@@autoname@` — the per-item path mints these from rebased offsets, so `all_classes`/`all_variables`/`command_aliases` keys and `resolution_candidates` strings disagree even when the underlying facts match (e.g. `docstrip_util.tcl`, `ensemble.tcl`, `pop3d_dbox.tcl`).
- **`instance_classes` missing entries on the per-item side** (4 files): e.g. `dialect.tcl`/`oodialect.tcl` lose `MotherOfAllMetaClasses` — a real fact gap, not just naming.
- One W001 diagnostic present only on the full path (`bench_wtext.tcl`), and a handful of "no field pinpointed" findings the describer can't attribute.

These are `#[ignore]`d corpus tests, so CI never runs them — the gate has silently rotted. Two work items: (1) make synthetic-name minting rebase-stable (mint from absolute offsets in the per-item path, or normalise before comparison if the identities are genuinely per-run); (2) chase the real fact gaps (`instance_classes`, the W001) once naming noise is gone; then consider a small deterministic corpus slice that CAN run in CI so the gate can't rot again. Repro: fetch tcllib to `tmp/`, run the command above; finding lists in this issue's provenance (session scratchpad `peritem-{base,c5a}.txt`).

issues.title: `definition()` ignores an already-resolved indirect command head and jumps to a same-named decoy
issues.body:
Residual from PR #1131's probe, pre-existing and independent of the fold work: the analyser resolves `set ns ::tc; ${ns}::setdef` to `::tc::setdef` and records it as `command_invocations` with `indirect: true` — but `definition()` never consults that entry, falling straight through to the bareword proc lookup, which answers an unrelated same-named proc (`::other::setdef` in the probe, with the decoy present). A wrong answer, not a miss — and it partially undercuts audit idx 44's "go-to-definition … now resolves" claim (STATUS.md annotated additively in #1131; no counts changed pending this fix).

Fix looks small: prefer an `indirect` `command_invocations` entry whose range covers the cursor before the bareword fallback — which would also fix M7-settled `$cmd` heads. But it changes a widely-tested resolution path, so it wants its own round with TP (resolved indirect head wins over decoy), FP guard (an *unresolved* indirect head must not block the bareword fallback), TN (plain bareword behaviour unchanged), and a cross-file e2e.

issues.title: Bareword command resolution in `definition`/`hover`: no command-position gate (wrong answers) and no `::oo::Helpers` / cross-file tail fallback (missed answers)
issues.body:
Two audit findings that land on the same code path from opposite directions: the final "otherwise it is a CALL" fallback shared by `definition.rs::definition()` and `hover.rs`, which hands whatever word the pure text scan (`find_word_span_at_position`) returned straight to `resolve_called_proc`. That fallback consults neither the enclosing command's head position (so a word that is merely an *argument* gets resolved as a command — a wrong answer, not an abstention) nor the invocation's own `resolution_candidates` (so a bare command inside a TclOO method body, whose real resolution path includes `::oo::Helpers`, is unresolvable across documents — a miss, plus a false W123). One over-resolves, one under-resolves, and both are fixed at the same seam: make the fallback ask the resolution machinery what this word actually is before answering from text.

### idx 50 — nico-robert/ticklecharts (`tricky_indirection`)

An ensemble *subcommand argument* beside a correctly-abstained non-literal command word is resolved as if it were a command name, landing on an unrelated same-named proc — structurally impossible for any run. `huddle_patch.tcl:64-69`'s `return [$types(callback:$tag) jsondump $huddle_object …]`: the LSP correctly flags `$types(callback:$tag)` as non-literal (W307) and then resolves the next word, `jsondump`, onto `::huddle::jsondump` — the very proc containing the call. Reduced to a 9-line control with zero indirection (`anotherproc dump`, `dump` a plain string argument) it reproduces identically, and hover shares the false positive.

Repro pointer: audit `50/` (`full_verbatim/` = unmodified corpus `huddle_patch.tcl` + `ehuddle.tcl`, the primary LSP evidence; `control/`, `control2/`, `control3/` = the minimal isolated repros proving the bug is general and unrelated to huddle).

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints may be stale against current code):

> `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs`, `pub fn definition()` (~lines 180-197): once the cursor's word fails the variable / instance-method / next-nextto / own-proc-name-span / class checks, the final fallback ("Otherwise it is a CALL — resolve namespace-aware…") unconditionally calls `resolve_called_proc(analysis, source, &namespace, &word, …)` for whatever bareword `find_word_span_at_position` (hover.rs:2104, a pure text word-boundary scan with zero command-position awareness) returned — with no check that the word actually occupies the enclosing command's head position (contrast: `command_head_and_namespace_at` at definition.rs:1113 exists but isn't consulted here to gate this). `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs` (~line 267, "Proc hover — namespace-aware…") calls the exact same `resolve_called_proc` the same way, so hover shares the identical false positive. `references.rs`/rename appear to key off a different, more conservative path that does not exhibit this […] so the fix should likely bring `definition`/`hover`'s fallback in line with whatever position-check `references` already applies before calling `resolve_called_proc`.

### idx 51 — nico-robert/ticklecharts (`tricky_indirection`)

A bare `callback` call inside a TclOO method body (the "TclOO Tricks" wiki helper `proc ::oo::Helpers::callback`, version-guarded in `utils.tcl`, and a genuine native command on 8.7/9.0) resolves only when the declaration and the call site share a file. Split across files — exactly ticklecharts' layout, helper in `utils.tcl`, call in `esnap.tcl:200-203` — it produces a false "Unknown command 'callback'" and empty definition/hover/references. Real Tcl always finds it: a method body's `namespace path` is unconditionally `::oo::Helpers` (verified on 8.6 and 9.0).

Repro pointer: audit `51/` (`classes.tcl`, `utils.tcl`, `esnap.tcl`, `main.tcl` — the `foreach class {…} { oo::define $class { … fileevent $f readable [callback ReadBrowser $f] … } }` shape, with the capitalised auto-private methods that force the `callback` idiom).

Quoted `root_cause_hint`:

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs`: `advance_command_resolution_namespace`'s `ScopeKind::Method if child.oo_global_resolution => "::".to_string()` (~line 137) approximates every TclOO method body's bare-command resolution as global-namespace-only (per its own doc comment, "the class's defining namespace is never searched") — but never adds `::oo::Helpers`, which real Tcl always also puts on the method body's `namespace path` […]. The same function's finalisation pass (~lines 437-474, `inv.resolution_candidates = crate::naming::command_resolution_candidates(&ns, path, &inv.name)`) bakes that collapse into each `CommandInvocation`'s candidate list, so for a bare `callback` call it records only `["::callback"]`, never `::oo::Helpers::callback`. `rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs` `resolve_workspace_symbols` (~3970-4032) — the single function backing cross-file `definition`/`references`/rename per its own doc comment — walks exactly `inv.resolution_candidates`, so it can never see a proc declared as `proc ::oo::Helpers::NAME {…}` in another file. Same-file calls only survive by accident via a *different*, unrelated mechanism: `definition.rs`'s `fallback_proc_by_simple_name` […] which the cross-file path never calls. A fix likely means either (a) adding `::oo::Helpers` as a standing extra candidate namespace for `ScopeKind::Method` invocations (mirroring how `namespace_paths` already stacks explicit `namespace path` entries), or (b) giving `resolve_workspace_symbols`/`cross_document_definition` the same lenient tail-name fallback `definition.rs` already has for the single-file case.

### Fix direction

Both halves want the resolution facts the campaign already built rather than a second text-level guess. For idx 50 the gate is `command_head_and_namespace_at` (`definition.rs`) plus `innermost_namespace_at` / `command_resolution_namespace_at` — STATUS.md §4's canonical "what does an unqualified name at this offset resolve against" — consulted *before* the `resolve_called_proc` fallback, with references' more conservative treatment as the reference behaviour. For idx 51 the candidate list itself is the fix site: `command_resolution_candidates` in `scope.rs`'s finalisation pass is where the method-body `namespace path` belongs, so that the one cross-file resolver (`resolve_workspace_symbols`) inherits it everywhere at once rather than each consumer growing its own lenient fallback — the same "one recording site, not a second scanner" discipline the C-series PRs used. Worth scheduling with **#1133**, which is the third direction on the identical fallback (an already-resolved *indirect* head ignored in favour of a same-named decoy); a single round can add the position gate, the indirect-entry preference, and the candidate-list fix with one shared TP/FP/TN matrix. **#1113**'s item 2 also touches `oo::Helpers` path handling from the namespace-navigation side.

issues.title: `[list …]`-built script arguments are never walked as scripts: variable declarations and reads inside them are invisible
issues.body:
Two audit findings sharing one mechanism: a script argument built as a `[list …]` command substitution rather than written as a literal `{…}` block is never unwrapped into the nested command it provably is, so every pass that keys on "a literal braced body" skips it. `analyse_body` returns early unless the body token is `TokenType::Str`; the semantic-token upvar override only matches a *segmented* command whose `texts[0]` is literally `upvar`; and `body_has_dynamic_barrier` classifies a command-substitution body as a dynamic barrier end to end. The two findings are the two consumers this starves — variable *declarations* (semantic tokens) and variable *references* (hover/definition/find-references) — for constructs real Tcl executes deterministically, and the codebase already has the literal-`[list …]` unwrap machinery, just wired elsewhere.

### idx 100 — tk (`uplevel`, low)

`library/tk.tcl:289`'s `uplevel #0 [list upvar #0 ::tk::Priv.$disp ::tk::Priv]` has a fully static literal destination word (`::tk::Priv`), which the semantic-token pass tags `namespace` instead of `variable [declaration]` — while the identical literal text one line later in a plain `variable ::tk::Priv` statement is tagged correctly. A 3-way controlled comparison (direct `upvar`, braced `uplevel {upvar …}`, `uplevel [list upvar …]`) proves on 9.0/8.6 that all three are functionally identical and only the `[list …]` form — the one Tk actually uses — is misclassified. The audit explicitly measured **no** navigation differential here, so confirmed impact is highlighting-only.

Repro pointer: audit `100/` (`core.tcl`+`widget.tcl`+`main.tcl` = faithful `tk.tcl:280-321` analogue, oracle-verified; `probe_semtok.tcl` = semantic-token-only isolation; `control_plain_variable.tcl`, `control2_a/b.tcl`, `control3_writer/reader.tcl` = non-uplevel controls).

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints may be stale against current code):

> `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs`, fn `insert_ref_var_overrides` (~lines 1474-1511): matches upvar-declared locals only when a *segmented command's* `texts[0]` is literally "upvar" (or "namespace upvar"/"dict update"). That fires for a direct `upvar` call and, via the separate "braced uplevel/eval bodies are recursed as nested scripts" mechanism (see test `uplevel_body_recurses_as_script`, ~line 7951, "Issue #837"), for `uplevel N {upvar …}`. It never fires for `uplevel N [list upvar …]` because the `[list …]` argument is never unwrapped into a synthetic nested command. Consistent with `rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/mod.rs::body_has_dynamic_barrier` (~405-483), which requires the uplevel/eval body word to be `TokenType::Str` […] and `rust/tcl-compiler/src/cfg_builder/upvar_info.rs::walk_stmt` (~250-307), which only discovers upvar via a literal `Statement::Call{command=="upvar"}` or by recursing into `Statement::UpFrame` […]. Note the codebase already has the conceptual building block for recognizing `[list <literal-head> …]` dispatched via eval/uplevel/interp-eval — `rust/tcl-compiler/src/taint.rs::list_wrapped_arg_command_is_literal` (~2854-2886) — but it is currently wired only into the T1xx taint/injection-diagnostic path, not into the semantic-tokens/variable-declaration path, which is where a fix would plausibly generalize from.

### idx 102 — tk (`source`)

`proc ::tk::SourceLibFile {file} { namespace eval :: [list source [file join $::tk_library $file.tcl]] }` — the `$file` read, unambiguously the proc's own parameter substituted in the calling frame before `namespace eval` even runs, is invisible to hover, go-to-definition and find-references, because the `namespace eval` body is a `[…]` substitution rather than a `{…}` block. Reproduced on a verbatim copy of the corpus file (`library/tk.tcl` lines 533-536) as well as the minimal analogue. A second bug in the same three lines: hovering the `{file}` *parameter declaration* shows the built-in `file` command's documentation, because the identifier collides with a registry command name.

Repro pointer: audit `102/app.tcl` (+`lib/helper.tcl`, `lib/optional.tcl`) as the minimal faithful analogue; `102/real_tk/tk.tcl` verbatim corpus reproduction; `102/control_param2/a.tcl` isolating "qualified global var resolves at identical nesting depth, local param does not"; `102/control_param/*.tcl` separating the hover misattribution from the missing-reference bug.

Quoted `root_cause_hint`:

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs::Analyser::analyse_body` (~line 129): `if body_tok.kind != TokenType::Str { return; }` skips all per-command processing — including `record_arg_var_reads` (line ~244, the mechanism that populates `VarDef.references` consumed by hover/definition/references) — whenever a body is a `[…]` command-substitution rather than a literal `{…}` block. `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs::Analyser::handle_namespace_eval_command` (~line 1099-1167) is the caller for `namespace eval NS BODY`: for `BODY = [list source [file join $NS_VAR $PARAM.tcl]]` it still creates the child namespace scope […] but the `analyse_body` call on that body is a no-op per the gate above, so nested `$var` reads are never captured into the enclosing proc's scope chain — even though the separate nested-substitution walker used for bareword command-name recognition (`run_nested_command_diagnostics`/`collect_substitution_heads` […]) does reach the same region, which is why "source"/"file" still hover correctly there. This mirrors the already-fixed idx=110 gap (`detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown`, same file) which added a narrow command-shape detector for `[list namespace unknown …]` but not a general variable-reference recorder for list-wrapped/dynamic body arguments of namespace eval (or uplevel/eval/after, likely similarly affected). The secondary hover-misattribution bug is most likely in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs`'s word/position classification (`pub fn hover_with_profile`, ~line 193 onward) for a parameter-list declaration token that happens to also be a registry command name — it resolves the registry command before/instead of recognizing the position as inside a `{param …}` declaration list.

### Fix direction

The unwrap itself is solved machinery worth reusing rather than re-deriving: `signature_scan::command_prefix::list_quoted_command_segment` already turns a `Cmd` token whose sole inner command is a `Traits::BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX` call (`list`) with a literal first word into a fully segmented command, registry-gated and with the `looks_unresolvable` abstention for `[list $cb …]` — that is exactly the "is this `[list …]` a statically known script?" predicate both findings need, and `taint::list_wrapped_arg_command_is_literal` is the second existing instance of the same idea. The natural shape is one shared "resolve a list-quoted script argument to a segmented command" helper consumed by `analyse_body`'s body gate, `insert_ref_var_overrides`, and (if it can be done without perturbing IR relaxation) `body_has_dynamic_barrier` — one recording site rather than a third parallel unwrap, per the discipline that landed the `[list …]` callback shape for the command-prefix substrate. Note the direction stays abstain-on-doubt: only a literal head with literal words unwraps, everything else keeps today's barrier behaviour. idx 102's secondary hover misattribution is independent and small (position classification before registry lookup). Adjacent but distinct: **#1108** (find-references completeness for `[set X]` reads and braced name words) is the other open "reads the scope model doesn't record" issue and shares consumers, not this mechanism.

issues.title: Caller-frame `upvar` targets the call site never spells: the `literal_targets` residual of the frame-effect summary (audit idx 22 / 98, plus idx 59's cross-file half)
issues.body:
The caller-frame injection model built in PR C1a/C1b (the per-procedure frame-effect summary in `cfg_builder/upvar_info.rs`, consumed through `tcl-lsp-core/src/caller_frame.rs`) answers "which names does a call to this procedure write in *my* frame?" whenever the name arrives as an argument word at the call site — that is what killed the W210 false positives of idx 7/38/57/59 and the navigation half of idx 58. The two findings below are the shape it deliberately left abstaining: the callee names the caller-side variable **literally in its own body** (`upvar 1 name name`, or a fully-qualified `upvar ::ns::Array(elem) alias`), so there is no argument word at the call site to key on. STATUS.md §6b records both as PARTIAL for exactly this reason: closing them needs the summary's `literal_targets` bucket recorded per procedure on `ProcDef`, which the analyser does not yet do. Today those reads take the abstaining answer rather than a wrong one, so this is a false-negative/completeness issue, not a soundness one.

### idx 22 — georgtree/SpiceGenTcl (`upvar`, PARTIAL)

Go-to-definition/hover/find-references never resolve a variable a callee creates in the caller's frame via `upvar 1 literalOther literalMy`, even for a fully static single-hop case. The corpus shape is `Utility::NameProcess` (`generalClasses.tcl:117-125`, `upvar name name`), mixed into every `Dc`/`Ac`/`Tran`/`pulse`/`sin`/… constructor, called as `my NameProcess $arguments [self object]`, after which the constructor reads `$name` (e.g. `specAnalysesClassesCommon.tcl:52` then `:57` `next dc $params -name $name`) without ever `set`/`variable`-declaring it.

Repro pointer: audit `22/repro.tcl` — the `Utility` mixin with `method NameProcess {arguments object} { upvar name name; … }`, mixed into `Widget`, whose constructor calls `my NameProcess …` then reads `$name` at line 40. Both interpreters print `name=W1 params=…`; the LSP answers `(no hover)` / `Definition (0 locations)` with no diagnostic — a silent miss.

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints predate the C1a/C1b model and are stale about what exists today):

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs::handle_upvar_command` (~2019-2038) only defines the `myVar` alias in the callee's own `scope_path` via `Analyser::define_var` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs:746`); there is no interprocedural step in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs` (plain proc calls) or `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/oo_my.rs` (`my <method>` OO dispatch) that, given a literal call target, looks at the callee's body for a static `upvar 1 literalOther literalMy` and injects `literalOther` as a defined variable in the caller's scope for hover/definition/find-references purposes.

### idx 98 — tk (`upvar`, PARTIAL)

`upvar ::tk::FocusGrab($index) data` (`tk.tcl:177`) aliases a literal, fully-qualified global array under a runtime-computed element; a fully-qualified upvar target is level-independent (tclsh-verified), so the target array is 100% statically determinable. The audit measured every occurrence of `::tk::FocusGrab` — inside the `upvar` itself and in sibling proc `RestoreFocusGrab`'s three matching accesses — returning empty for hover/definition/references, while the local alias `data` was tracked flawlessly. **Partly landed since**: `handle_upvar_command`'s `otherVar` link now exists and is pinned in `handlers.rs` citing this idx; the ledger nonetheless keeps idx 98 PARTIAL alongside idx 22, so the first job here is to re-measure which half of the finding survives.

Repro pointer: audit `98/focusgrab.tcl` — a self-contained shrink of `tk.tcl:175-178`+`202-206` (`SetFocusGrab`'s `upvar` vs `RestoreFocusGrab`'s independent `info exists`/read/`unset` of the identically-recomputed key), with both interpreters agreeing on `array get ::tk::FocusGrab` before/after.

Quoted `root_cause_hint`:

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs`, `Analyser::handle_upvar_command` (~L2306-2325): loop only touches `args[i]` (myVar) via `define_var`; never reads or registers `args[i-1]` (otherVar), so a literal/fully-qualified upvar target (here `::tk::FocusGrab`) never gets a `VarDef`, `set_var_link_target`, or reference recorded anywhere — contrast with `handle_global_command` (~L277-305), `handle_variable_command` (~L313-351), and `handle_namespace_upvar_command` (~L2336-2374) in the same file, all of which resolve and link the qualified "other" target. Registry side: `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/upvar_.rs`'s `spec()` sets `analyser_hook: Some(AnalyserHookId::Upvar)` but no `arg_roles`, so there's no generic role-driven fallback either.

### Also open here: idx 59's cross-file half (ticklecharts, ticked FIXED)

Recorded in STATUS.md §6b so it is not lost with the ticked finding: idx 59 landed single-document in PR C1a, but `detect_upvar_procs` remains single-`Module`, so a proc whose upvar-based out-parameter lives in another file still gets no frame-effect summary. Same subsystem, same PR-sized round.

### Fix direction

The model exists; this is the missing bucket in it. `upvar_info.rs`'s per-procedure summary should record `literal_targets` — caller-frame names the callee writes under a name spelled in the *callee's* text, not derived from a call-site argument — recorded on `ProcDef` so `caller_frame.rs`'s consumers (SSA def-creation for W210, hover, definition, references) pick them up through the same single path they already use for the argument-derived bucket, with no second scanner. The abstention discipline stays: a literal target injects a caller-frame definition, a computed one keeps today's abstaining answer, and (per the C1a work) `proc`/`apply`/`namespace eval`/`uplevel` bodies remain excluded as fresh frames. Cross-file (idx 59's residual) is the same summary keyed workspace-wide, which the cross-document tiers PR C2 built the index shape for. Re-verify idx 98 against current `handle_upvar_command` first — its `otherVar` link is already pinned — and pin whichever half remains with the campaign's TP/FP/TN/FN + `lsp_e2e` matrix.

issues.title: Document-tier providers answer from a weaker model than navigation: `documentLink` fabricates targets for computed `source` paths, `documentSymbol` homes procs lexically
issues.body:
Two findings whose shared property is the fix site's tier rather than one code path: `textDocument/documentLink` and `textDocument/documentSymbol` are the two providers still answering from their own local reading of the source text while the navigation tier (hover/definition/references) answers the same questions correctly from the analyser's resolved facts. In both cases the LSP already computes the right answer elsewhere in the same response — go-to-definition sees through the computed `source` chain that documentLink fabricates a bogus target for, and hover reports the qualified name that documentSymbol contradicts — so the defect is visible as self-inconsistency, and the fix in both cases is consuming an existing model rather than improving one.

### idx 41 — georgtree/tclopt (`source`)

`documentLink` fabricates a non-existent-file target for any `source` argument that is a computed path (`[file join $dir …]`, nested `[file dirname [info script]]`, or a bare `$var`) instead of resolving it or abstaining: it percent-encodes the raw unevaluated Tcl text and joins it onto the workspace directory, so `source [file join $dir .. pkgfile.tcl]` in `test/all_codeCoverage.tcl` yields `file:///…/test/%5Bfile%20join%20$dir%20..%20pkgfile.tcl%5D` instead of the tclsh-verified `…/pkgfile.tcl`. Go-to-definition, find-references, and (with `crossFileResolution` on) W123 all see through this exact 3-hop chain correctly — this is specifically a document-link bug.

Repro pointer: audit `41/` mirroring the real `test/all_codeCoverage.tcl → test.test → benchmarkFuncs.tcl` chain (`minimal_doclink_bug/` isolate, `literal_baseline/` control, `bare_var/` corroboration, `orphan/` side note); probe scripts `probe_doclinks.py` / `probe_cross_file.py`.

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints may be stale against current code):

> `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/document_links.rs`, function `document_links()` (~lines 164-185) together with `literal_file_join()` (~line 220). When the source argument is a bracket expression that `literal_file_join` can't fully reduce to literals […] the code falls through to `if let Some(&single) = seg.single_token_word.get(idx) && !single { continue; } path.clone()`. The comment assumes `single_token_word[idx]` is false for "variable substitution / command substitution" arguments, but per `rust/tcl-compiler/src/segmenter.rs`'s own semantics […] `single_token_word` only distinguishes "one token" from "multiple concatenated tokens" within a word — a whole-word bracket substitution `[file join $dir x.tcl]` or a whole-word bare `$var` is exactly one token, so `single_token_word[idx]` is `true` for these too, and the code wrongly falls through to treating the raw unevaluated text as a literal path, which `resolve_path()`/`file_uri_for_path()` (~lines 273-318) then percent-encode and join onto `workspace_root` into a syntactically-valid but semantically-bogus `file://` URI. Fix direction: when `literal_file_join` fails on a word whose token kind is a command/variable substitution (or more generally whenever the reconstructed text still contains `$`/`[`), skip (continue) rather than falling through to `path.clone()`; optionally, reuse `tcl_compiler::auto_path_eval::evaluate_auto_path_expr` (already used by `resolve_source_edge` in `tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs` ~11529 for the M9 namespace-rehoming source graph) to actually resolve the common `[file dirname [info script]]`/`[file join …]` idioms — note that evaluator itself also doesn't substitute a preceding `set dir [...]` assignment for a bare `$dir`, so even reusing it as-is would still require adding simple same-file copy-propagation of a single preceding `set VAR EXPR` to fully solve the note's exact idiom; short of that, correctly abstaining (no link) is the minimum fix.

### idx 67 — nico-robert/pix (`proc_args`)

`proc pix::svg::parse {…}` written with a namespace-qualified name at file top level, textually outside any `namespace eval` block (the earlier `namespace eval ::pix { namespace eval svg {…} }` has already closed). tclsh confirms the proc lands at `::pix::svg::parse`, and the LSP's own hover/definition/references all agree on that qualified name — but `documentSymbol` places `parse`/`newImage` as bare top-level Function symbols, disconnected from the `Namespace pix > svg` tree shown in the very same response, while a proc lexically written inside a real `namespace eval` block nests correctly. (The note's two sub-concerns — nested-brace defaults and namespace auto-creation — are REFUTED in the JSON entry.)

Repro pointer: audit `67/minimal/m.tcl` (6 lines), `67/svg_onefile.tcl` (richer single file with a contrasting correctly-nested `caller` proc), `67/{svg.tcl,main.tcl}` (split-file variant closer to the corpus), `67/autoviv_check.tcl` (the auto-vivification refutation).

Quoted `root_cause_hint`:

> `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/document_symbols.rs`: `document_symbols_from_analysis` (~line 184) calls `scope_symbols` (~line 375), which builds the outline by walking the analyser's LEXICAL `Scope` tree (`scope.procs`, iterated at whatever `scope_path` the source text was physically nested at, and `scope.children` for `ScopeKind::Namespace`). Meanwhile `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs::handle_proc_command` (~line 667-824) already computes the semantically-correct fully-qualified name via `let ns_prefix = self.command_resolution_namespace(scope_path); let qualified = qualify(&ns_prefix, raw_name);` (parsing `::` out of the proc's own written name, per the comment "Home the proc to the *command-resolution* namespace, not the purely lexical one") — but it registers the `ProcDef` into `scope.procs` at the raw *lexical* `path`, not at a scope matching `qualified`'s namespace. Hover […], go-to-definition/references […], and completion […] all read `result.all_procs` / `ProcDef.qualified_name` and so get it right; `document_symbols.rs` is the one consumer still walking the lexical Scope tree directly. `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/item_tree.rs::ItemTree::from_analysis` (~line 200) shows the analyser already has the right building block for this (`enclosing_namespace(qualified)`, pure string manipulation of the qualified name, no lexical-scope dependency) but that path isn't wired into `textDocument/documentSymbol`.

### Fix direction

idx 67 is the last consumer left behind by the idx 85 sweep — that finding's fix replaced lexical namespace derivation with `command_resolution_namespace` across the analyser (handlers, `oo.rs`, ensembles, imports) precisely so a qualified-name definition outside `namespace eval` homes correctly everywhere; the outline should be built from `ProcDef::qualified_name` via `ItemTree::from_analysis`'s `enclosing_namespace`, not from the lexical `Scope` tree, so the outline and hover cannot disagree by construction. idx 41 has a documented minimum (abstain — never emit a link whose reconstructed text still carries `$`/`[`, which is strictly better than a bogus one) and a documented maximum (reuse `auto_path_eval::evaluate_auto_path_expr` the way `resolve_source_edge` already does for the source graph, plus single-`set` copy propagation for the `$dir` idiom); the source-graph resolver is already the campaign's one place that knows how to evaluate these path expressions, so the link provider should consume it rather than grow a second path evaluator. Both are self-contained, and both want an `lsp_e2e` assertion that the document-tier response agrees with the navigation response on the same span.

issues.title: Un-hooked command bodies get a naive walk: false W210/E003 and inert navigation inside a `tcl::OptProc`-shaped definer body
issues.body:
A command the registry has no analyser hook for, but whose trailing brace-shaped argument really is a procedure body, gets a generic walk that notices `$var` reads for the "read before set" check yet never records the body's own definitions, never registers an arity or a parameter-scoped child scope, and never creates a `VarDef`/`Scope` that hover, definition or references can look up. The result on real code is a triple: false W210 on every parameter the definer binds, a stale arity that produces a false E003 at legitimate call sites, and completely inert navigation inside the body. The audit isolated this as generic — an invented, unknown command name with a plain `set y 1; return $y` body reproduces the same false W210 — rather than specific to the command or the upvar mechanic the finding was assigned to.

**Read this one against current code before planning.** The finding's stated root cause was `::tcl::OptProc` having no `AnalyserHookId`, and that is exactly what the campaign's idx 90 fix landed (`AnalyserHookId::OptProc` + `handle_opt_proc_command` + `handle_opt_proc` on the signature-scan side, plus the `resolve_analyser_hook` fix that unblocked `::`-qualified hook heads). So the OptProc-specific half is very likely already closed and what remains is the generic half — an un-hooked definer of any other spelling. The first step is re-measuring the repros below and splitting "still true" from "fixed by idx 90".

### idx 99 — tk (`upvar`)

The assigned line (`safetk.tcl:84`, `namespace upvar ::safe S$child state`) sits inside `::tcl::OptProc ::safe::loadTk {optlist} {body}`. The dynamic-upvar-target mechanic itself is handled correctly in an ordinary proc scope — the narrow claim is not the bug. On the real unmodified corpus file the LSP emits 3 false W210 "read before it is set" warnings for `child`/`use`/`display` (all legitimately bound by the literal, fully-static optlist), reports `loadTk`'s arity as 0 params in the outline, and — in a same-file repro using the real optlist and a real call pattern from `tests/safe.test` (`safe::loadTk a`) — a false `E003 Too many arguments … expected at most 0, got 1` on code both interpreters run successfully. Hover/definition/references are inert for every variable in such a body, including `state`, which works fine outside the wrapper.

Repro pointer: audit `99/safetk_optproc.tcl` (closest-to-real: real OptProc + real namespace-upvar line + 2 valid calls → false E003+W210), `99/safetk_min.tcl` (upvar mechanic alone, no OptProc → clean), `99/optproc_isolate.tcl` and `99/unknown_cmd_control.tcl` (root-cause isolation with no upvar at all → same false positives), `99/real/safetk.tcl` (unmodified corpus file → 3 false W210s at the exact assigned statement).

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority for repro detail; this hint is the one most likely stale — `AnalyserHookId::OptProc` now exists):

> `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/stdlib/tcl__optproc.rs`: `CommandSpec` for "tcl::OptProc" sets no `analyser_hook` (contrast `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs:354` `analyser_hook: Some(AnalyserHookId::NamespaceUpvar)` for `namespace upvar`, which IS correctly wired and IS what makes the narrow upvar mechanic work in an ordinary proc). `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:749` `handle_proc_command` is the only code path that (a) registers a command's real arity/param list and (b) opens a properly parameter-scoped child scope for a body; it is dispatched off the literal command word "proc", so `::tcl::OptProc ::safe::loadTk {optlist} {body}` never reaches it and the stale 0-arg stub from the preceding literal `proc ::safe::loadTk {} {}` (auto_mkIndex placeholder) stays canonical. Whatever generic per-command walker processes un-hooked commands' brace-shaped trailing arguments (not pinned to an exact function within the time budget) does a naive scan that notices `$var` reads for the W210 "read before set" check but never records `set`/optlist-establishment as a def, and never registers a `VarDef`/`Scope` that hover.rs/definition.rs/references.rs can look up — confirmed generic (not upvar- or OptProc-specific) via `unknown_cmd_control.tcl` reproducing the same false W210 on a totally invented command name with plain `set y 1; return $y`.

### Fix direction

If the generic half survives re-measurement, the campaign's answer is registry-driven rather than a per-command branch: the missing fact is a body classification, and `body_kind` (the `Structural` classification added for `itcl::class`/`snit::widget`/`snit::type`/`snit::widgetadaptor` when the idx 125 quoted-body work exposed the same flat-scan false W210s) is the existing knob for "this brace-shaped argument is not an ordinary expression-bearing script walked in the enclosing scope". The direction that landed for idx 90 is the template for a definer with real parameter semantics — a hook plus `arg_roles`/`body_kind`/`command_table_effect` on the spec, with the signature-scan tier given its own handler so cross-file arity does not inherit the wrong words — and STATUS.md §6b's idx 90 row documents both halves. For a genuinely unknown command name (no spec at all), the honest behaviour is abstention rather than a naive read-before-set scan: whatever the walker cannot classify should not feed W210/E003. Pin the `unknown_cmd_control.tcl` shape as the FP guard and the real `safetk.tcl` as the corpus-level regression.

issues.title: W307 fires on an object dispatch the LSP itself resolves: no object-type edge through a `$var method` return captured into a variable
issues.body:
The object-type story has suppressions for a handle produced by a direct construction (`set x [C new]; $x run`) and for a method return consumed in one expression (`[my obj] run`), but not for the shape in between: a handle returned by a `$var`-dispatched method and captured into a variable before being re-dispatched (`set b [$a make]; $b greet`). Because the type does not flow across that edge, the analyser emits a visible false `W307 Non-literal command name — cannot statically analyze` — a wrong *warning*, not the correct silent abstention it produces for genuinely runtime-dependent dispatch — and go-to-definition answers nothing at the same site, while the LSP's own hover/definition on the producing call resolve the callee correctly. The self-contradiction within one file is what makes this user-visible.

### idx 14 — georgtree/SpiceGenTcl (`tricky_indirection`)

The note's assigned mechanic (`generalClasses.tcl:2809-2822`, `$topNetlist add [{*}$element]` with `$element` a runtime-built `[list …::Class new …]` string) is REFUTED — the LSP correctly abstains there, with no diagnostic and no false reference. Building a faithful runnable analogue of the surrounding code shape (a parser method returning an object handle that callers capture and dispatch on, as `buildTopNetlist`'s own docstring describes) uncovered the distinct confirmed bug above.

Repro pointer: audit `14/minimal/t.tcl` —

```tcl
oo::class create A { method make {} { return [B new] } }
oo::class create B { method greet {} { return "hi" } }
set a [A new]
set b [$a make]
$b greet
```

Both `tclsh9.0` and `tclsh8.6` exit 0 (B's `greet` runs). The LSP reports `WARNING W307 8:0-8:2` on `$b greet`, while `definition` on the `make` call correctly answers `::A::make` and hover names it — i.e. the information needed to type `b` is present and simply not propagated.

Quoted `root_cause_hint` (the JSON is the authority; hints may be stale against current code):

> `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs` has W307 suppression tests covering `[my obj] run` (test `w307_my_method_literal_vs_object_return`, ~line 2288) and `set x [C new]; $x run` (test `w307_known_class_new_var_suppression`, ~line 2411), but no test/coverage for the shape `set b [$a make]; $b greet` — a variable assigned from a `$var`-dispatched method's return value, later re-dispatched on. Likely the object-type tracker (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/object_types.rs`) only records a variable's inferred object type when the RHS is a direct `[ClassName new]`/`[my method]` literal-return pattern, not when it's the return of a `$var method` call whose callee […]

### Fix direction

This is the compiler-side complement of **#994** rather than a duplicate of it: #994 is about the LSP's navigation consumers keying off the weaker single-pass `instance_classes` map instead of `object_types.rs`'s interprocedural lattice, whereas this finding is about the edge itself — a *method*-return edge on a receiver that is already typed — and about the W307 diagnostic that fires when it is missing. Worth scoping together: if the lattice already carries method-return edges, the fix is entirely on the consumer side and lands with #994's unification (and the definition-half of this finding disappears with it); if it does not, the edge belongs beside the existing proc-return/parameter/constructor-parameter edges in `object_types.rs`, and W307's suppression should consult the same map so the diagnostic and navigation cannot disagree. **#1099**'s cross-document instance-provenance work is the same family one tier up. The invariant worth pinning either way is the one the audit measured: whenever hover/definition resolve the producing dispatch, W307 must not fire on the consuming one — with the REFUTED `{*}$element` shape from this same finding kept as the TN that must stay abstaining.

Split from #1019; the audit JSON entry is authoritative for repro detail.

issues.title: Method-dispatch propagation barrier is module-wide: one upvar-reaching or redefined method disables method-local SCCP for the whole module
issues.body:
## Context

PR #1131 (issues #1096/#1097) gave method bodies an escaping model so method-local constants can propagate through the `[self class]` fold chain. Its safety gate — hardened during Codex review (see the three P1 threads on #1131) — is deliberately **whole-module**: if *any* method body in the module can reach a caller frame (`upvar 1`/`uplevel 1` via `cfg_builder::upvar_info`), or *any* method is redefined via a later `oo::define`, method-local propagation is disabled for **every** method in the module.

## Why it was built that way

`my`/`next`/object dispatch does not name its callee, so the per-call-site widening the CFG builder does for upvar *procs* cannot apply; and per-class scoping of the redefinition switch is unsound without the MRO (a method replaced in a superclass is reachable from a subclass body — shape documented and tested in `a_redefined_method_bars_propagation`). Abstention is the only sound answer with the machinery the pass currently has.

## Why it will bite

Real TclOO code uses `uplevel 1`/`upvar 1` in methods — the `classvar` helper idiom is exactly this — so one such helper anywhere in a module switches off method-local propagation everywhere in it, including the ticklecharts-style chains #1131 exists to enable.

## Precise fix

Per-object-graph reachability: compute which methods can `my`-reach (transitively, along the MRO) a caller-frame-reaching or redefined method, and bar only those. Requires the MRO, which `optimiser/propagation.rs` does not currently compute — the analyser side already has MRO machinery (PR B2, #1026), so the likely shape is exporting that as typed lowering/compilation-unit data the optimiser can consume rather than recomputing it.

## Where

- Gate: `methods_reach_caller_frames` + the `redefined_methods` switch, `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/propagation.rs`
- Barrier contract doc to update: `docs/design/compiler/sccp-core-analyses.md`, "The method-dispatch barrier and its evidence rules"

Found as a design residual of PR #1131's fix round; split out per the campaign convention rather than guessed at inside that PR's targeted gate.

issues.title: upvar with dynamic local name (`upvar 1 x $dst`) is invisible to detect_upvar_procs, so proc callers do not widen
issues.body:
## The bug

`cfg_builder`'s `record_upvar_call` drops an `upvar` pair whose **local** side is dynamic — `upvar 1 x $dst` `continue`s because there is no local name to file the alias under. PR #1131 closed this for the *method-dispatch barrier* by adding `UpvarInfo::unnameable_local_aliases` (recording the caller-side word), but that field is deliberately outside `UpvarInfo::is_empty()`'s summary contract and is read only by the barrier's `reaches_caller_frame`.

The consequence on the **proc** side is still live:

```tcl
proc p {dst} { upvar 1 x $dst; set $dst 2 }
proc caller {} {
    set x 1
    p x
    puts $x   ;# tclsh prints 2; the caller's defs never widened, so $x can fold to 1
}
```

`p` is not registered as an upvar proc (its `UpvarInfo` still reads as empty), so `detect_upvar_procs` excludes it and *call sites of `p` do not widen the caller's defs* — the same bug class as #1131's Finding 3, on the caller side.

## The fix and its cost

Folding `unnameable_local_aliases` into `is_empty()` is a one-line change, but it shifts CFG-building for every call site of every proc that does this — every such call site starts widening. That needs a full workspace differential gate (FP/FN sweep on the corpus), not a targeted per-crate gate, which is why #1131 did not carry it.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/cfg_builder/` — `record_upvar_call`, `UpvarInfo::{is_empty, unnameable_local_aliases}`, `detect_upvar_procs`
- Oracle repro above should be pinned against tclsh 9.0.4/8.6.x before the change, per the standing oracle-first rule.

Found during PR #1131's Finding-3 fix (the shared-evidence-source rewrite); the method-side consumer is already correct.

issues.title: Lowering discards replacement method bodies on redefinition — retaining them would let SCCP and O126 scan instead of abstain
issues.body:
## Current state

When a method is redefined in a later `oo::define` block, lowering keeps the *first* body and records only the qualified name in `redefined_methods` (a `HashSet<String>`; the replacement body is discarded — the `continue` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/mod.rs` fires before the insert). Confirmed during PR #1131's Finding-2 fix: with only the name available, the method-dispatch propagation barrier can do nothing but abstain module-wide when any redefinition exists.

## Opportunity

If lowering retained later bodies keyed by definition order (e.g. `redefined_methods: HashMap<String, Vec<MethodBody>>` or equivalent typed carrier), consumers could scan *all* bodies a name may dispatch to instead of giving up:

1. **SCCP method-dispatch barrier** (`optimiser/propagation.rs`): instead of the whole-module kill switch for redefinitions, check every retained body with the same `reaches_caller_frame` evidence — strictly more precise, still sound (the union of bodies over-approximates whichever is live at dispatch time). Interacts with #1164: MRO-based refinement and body retention compose.
2. **O126 method purity**: abstains on the same "was redefined" fact today; scanning retained bodies would sharpen it identically.

## Constraints

- Definition order must be preserved (last-writer semantics for navigation stay as they are — this is about *analysis* consumers seeing the full candidate set, not about changing which definition wins).
- Memory cost is bounded by real redefinition frequency, which is low; no cost when nothing is redefined.

Found as a residual of PR #1131's fix round (Finding 2: the reviewer's suggested abstention was implemented; this issue tracks the strictly-more-precise alternative it noted).

issues.title: Cross-file renamemethod on a via_define stub cannot record the arrival name — destination needs a workspace-level join
issues.body:
## The gap

The D10/D11 side-awareness PR made `renamemethod old new` fully navigable when the class definition is in reach: the `MethodDef` *moves* to the new key, carrying params/body/visibility (oracle-pinned: visibility travels with the body, not the new name's leading-capital default).

But when the `renamemethod` sits in a **cross-file `oo::define` stub** (`via_define`), the stub has no `MethodDef` to move — the member's params/body/visibility live in the defining file's record. The stub channel can tombstone `old` (retraction works), but it has nowhere to put `new`: recording arrival needs the *other* file's method record re-keyed, which the additive stub-merge deliberately never does.

## Symptom

```tcl
# a.tcl
oo::class create C { method old {} { ... } }
# b.tcl
oo::define C { renamemethod old new }
```

Workspace-tier members of `C`: `old` correctly disappears, but `new` never appears — completion/outline/definition lose the member entirely instead of showing it under its new name.

## Fix shape

A tombstone variant carrying a destination (`MemberRetraction` event with `arrival: Some(name)`), plus a workspace-join consumer that, when folding a class's member events, re-keys the defining record's `MethodDef` to the destination. This is new machinery beyond the additive stub merge — and it must respect the unordered-cross-file abstention rule (unordered events revoke nothing; the #1116 source-graph partial order is the eventual foundation, same as the existing tombstone channel's caveat).

Left undone (and documented) in the D10/D11 PR because it is a workspace-model change, not an additive one.

issues.title: Lowering's OO extraction literal-matches oo::class create / oo::define — objdefine, snit, and itcl method bodies never become method units
issues.body:
## The gap

`is_oo_definition_shape` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/mod.rs` (the `match form { "oo::class" … "oo::define" … }` around line 125) recognises exactly two spellings. Consequences, confirmed during the #1129 fix:

1. **`oo::objdefine` bodies produce no `MethodDef` at all.** `oo::objdefine $obj { variable z; method m {…} }` contributes no method unit — no per-method CFG/SSA, no `instance_vars`, no diagnostics of any kind inside `m`. Oracle (9.0.4 + 8.6.14): `oo::objdefine $k { variable z }` then `my variable z; info exists z` → `0`, so there are real semantics to model. Currently *benign* for the #1129 fold (no unit → no fold → no FP) but it is the same class of false negative that #1130 fixed for `cu.methods` — whole method bodies invisible to every analysis.

2. **snit / [incr Tcl] method bodies never become method units.** The analyser's `oo.rs` finished the registry migration for member *recognition*, but lowering did not follow: no `MethodDef`, no `instance_vars`, no method-body analysis family for snit/itcl at all.

## Why this is also a registry-first violation

The literal `match` is exactly the pattern AGENTS.md bans in analysers: behaviour keyed on command spelling. The registry already carries the typed knowledge (`Traits::DECLARES_*`, member grammars used by `analyser/oo.rs`); a `DefinitionBodyGrammar`-driven walk in lowering would cover `oo::objdefine`, snit, and itcl from data, and delete the match.

## Interaction with open work

- #1170 (per-object member state has no home) is the *workspace/member-table* side of the objdefine gap; this issue is the *lowering/method-unit* side. Fixing this one gives #1170's W315-for-objdefine a `MethodDef` to hang state on.
- Any fix must preserve the #1131 `class_instance_vars` cross-block union semantics (objdefine variables are per-object, NOT per-class — they must not pollute the class union; oracle case K in the #1129 transcripts pins the difference).

Found during the #1129 fix (see that issue's consumer audit); pre-existing lowering debt, filed on its own.

issues.title: Two parallel channels carry instance-variable facts into method-body analyses — consolidate before they drift
issues.body:
## The duplication

After the #1129 fix, `MethodDef::instance_vars` reaches method-body analyses through two independent channels:

1. **`FunctionUnit::build_for_method`** threads it as `FunctionBuildInputs::object_state` → `sccp::ExistenceFrame` — consumed today only by the existence fold (I230 analyser path + O100/O101 optimiser path).
2. **`emit_method_body_diagnostics`** feeds the same fact to the W210/W211/W220 family via its own `known_bound` / `cross_event_vars` channel.

They agree today because both read the same `MethodDef`, but two parallel mechanisms carrying one fact into the same bodies is exactly the shape that produced #1129 in the first place (the analyser and optimiser copies of the existence fold sourcing parameters from *different* maps — one of which silently lacked methods entirely, the second FP shape fixed there).

## The consolidation

Make `ExistenceFrame` (or a widened `MethodBodyFacts` carrier on the function unit) the single source: build it once in `build_for_method`, have `emit_method_body_diagnostics` consume it instead of reconstructing `known_bound` from the IR a second time. One construction site, every consumer reads the same struct — the same "cannot diverge by construction" argument the #1129 fix used for the I230/O100 pair, extended to the W-family.

Also worth folding in when this happens: the SCCP escaping-set channel from #1131 (`sccp_with_extra_escaping(…, &method.instance_vars)`) is a third reader of the same field — three call sites constructing method-body views of instance state, one struct would do.

Pure refactor — no behaviour change expected; the value is the invariant. Found during the #1129 consumer audit.

issues.title: Method callees reached via `my` are invisible to the caller's upvar context — info-exists FP on upvar-defined locals in method bodies
Semantic tokens and format inlay hints bypass CommandRegistry grammar
issues.body:
## Problem

The semantic-token and format-specifier inlay-hint paths still encode command grammar by literal command spelling instead of consuming `CommandRegistry` data.

Confirmed at `d834636aadd05658b2f8187af09c3a1425b9e7ed`:

- `semantic_tokens.rs::insert_loop_var_overrides` names `foreach` and `lmap`.
- `insert_ref_var_overrides` names `upvar`, `namespace upvar`, and `dict update`, and re-derives their repeated argument layouts.
- `insert_multiname_var_overrides` names `global` and `variable`, and re-derives stride rules.
- `insert_oo_define_keyword_overrides` names `oo::define` and `oo::objdefine`.
- `insert_format_overrides` names `format`, `scan`, `clock`, and `binary`.
- `inlay_hints.rs::format_arg` independently repeats the same format-family dispatch and also names `regsub`.
- `CommandSpec::format_string_type` and the equivalent subcommand field already exist, but no command or subcommand populates them; their only assignments are the default `None`.

This violates the registry-source-of-truth contract and has already created observable drift.

## Reproduction and Tcl oracle

C Tcl 9.0.3 accepts the fully-qualified global command spelling and resolves it to the same command:

```tcl
puts [::format %d 7]                  ;# 7
namespace which -command ::format    ;# ::format
```

The direct `match head { "format" => ... }` and equivalent spelling tests do not fire for `::format`. The same false-negative class applies to `::scan`, `::clock`, `::binary`, `::foreach`, `::lmap`, `::upvar`, `::global`, `::variable`, `::oo::define`, and `::oo::objdefine` where the corresponding literal branch is the only source of the richer classification.

Examples to pin:

```tcl
::format {%08x} 42
::foreach {a b} {1 2} { puts $a }
proc p {} { ::upvar 1 source local; return $local }
namespace eval ::n { ::variable x 1 y 2 }
::oo::define ::C method m {args} { return $args }
```

This issue is adjacent to #1138: that ticket covers a statically list-built script that is never walked. This ticket covers direct, statically resolved calls whose grammar is bypassed because consumers match surface spelling.

Static `rename` and `interp alias` facts should use the effective command identity when the analyser can prove it. Dynamic `rename`, `unknown`, traces, safe/sub-interpreter command tables, and computed command heads must remain conservative and abstain rather than guess.

## General registry model

Extend registry data rather than adding another consumer branch. The existing fields cover part of the problem, but repeated/option-relative layouts need a typed descriptor, for example:

- repeated argument-role layout: start, stride, optional end-relative exclusion;
- alternating pair roles and optional-leading-level forms;
- option value role, including option arity and `--`;
- format family plus location: fixed argument, subcommand-fixed argument, or option value;
- definition invocation shape for script form versus inline-member form.

Alternatives considered:

1. **Typed layout descriptors on `CommandSpec`/`SubCommand` (preferred).** Generic consumers ask the registry for resolved roles and format locations.
2. **One callback returning invocation roles.** Flexible, but harder to inspect, document, serialise, and exhaustively test than data for the common repeated shapes.
3. **Normalise by stripping leading `::` inside each consumer.** Reject as incomplete: it fixes one spelling while preserving duplicated grammar and still misses aliases/renames.
4. **Keep per-command token helpers.** Reject: every new dialect command or grammar correction must then update multiple consumers.

Populate the existing `format_string_type` field or replace it with a descriptor that is actually sufficient; do not leave dead registry API beside a second source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

- Semantic tokens and inlay hints contain no command-name switch for these layouts.
- Command identity is resolved once through the registry/analyser environment, including leading-`::` forms and provable static aliases/renames.
- Dynamic command identity abstains without misclassifying data words.
- TclOO, snit, and [incr Tcl] inline/script member layouts flow from their definition-body grammar.
- Tcl 8.4–9.1 version/dialect gates and safe/sub-interpreter visibility remain correct.
- Update the registry/shared-utility design docs with the new descriptor, examples, and explicit limits.

Test matrix:

- **TP:** bare and leading-`::` calls for every affected layout; multiple `foreach` varlists; optional `upvar` level; multiple pairs; `args` parameter lists; format/clock/binary/regsub families.
- **FP:** same-named user proc in another namespace, an overwritten command after `rename`, hidden command in a safe interpreter, and data words which happen to equal a keyword.
- **TN:** dynamic heads, dynamic aliases, `unknown` fallback, malformed arity/options, and unsupported dialect/version.
- **FN:** nested command substitutions, `namespace eval`, `uplevel`, `interp eval`, TclOO inline and script forms, traces/callback prefixes, and static `interp alias`.
- Add registry unit tests, semantic-token and inlay unit tests, native LSP e2e tests, and VS Code tests which assert decoded token types/hints for qualified and aliased forms.

Do not add clippy allows; use named descriptor/context types where an API would otherwise become unwieldy.

issues.title: Compact minification renames observable Tcl array keys
issues.body:
## Problem

`compact_array_members` globally rewrites every statically spelled `arr(longmember)` to a short member such as `arr(a)`. Array member names are Tcl data, not private compiler symbols.

Reproducer:

```tcl
proc f {} {
    set arr(longmember) 1
    return [array get arr]
}
puts [f]
```

C Tcl 9.0.3 original output:

```text
longmember 1
```

Current `tcl minify --compact` output:

```tcl
proc f {} {set arr(a) 1;return [array get arr]};puts [f]
```

and C Tcl prints `a 1`.

The current safety decision is a name-prefix heuristic (`uri`, `path`, `header`, etc.). No spelling heuristic can prove a member name is unobservable. `array get/names`, `parray`, `upvar`, traces, callbacks, serialization, dict conversion, and native extensions can observe any key. The scan also merges same-named arrays across scopes.

## Fix direction and alternatives

Preferred default: remove array-member compaction from semantics-preserving tiers.

A future closed-world/obfuscating mode could rename a member only with a proof that:

- the array identity is scope-specific and never escapes;
- there is no enumeration, trace, alias, dynamic index, serialization, callback, reflection, or external/native access;
- every use is rewritten through shared place/alias analysis.

Alternatives are an explicit user annotation or an explicitly non-equivalent obfuscation tier. Expanding the prefix deny-list is not sound.

## Tests and acceptance

- C Tcl differential tests compare array contents, ordering-insensitive key sets, traces, output, and errors.
- TP/FP/TN/FN: private fixed-key use, `array get/names`, `upvar`, `global`/`variable`, namespace arrays, same local name in different procs, dynamic members, traces, dict conversion, TclOO variables, and safe/sub-interpreter boundaries.
- Add compact/aggressive tests, native LSP minify e2e, VS Code tests, and corpus execution.
- Update minifier documentation to distinguish symbol names from observable data.

Do not add clippy allows.

issues.title: Name compaction changes Tcl reflection and public command identities
issues.body:
## Problem

Compact/aggressive minification renames proc-local variables and procedure names while claiming semantics-preserving compaction. Tcl exposes both through reflection and command APIs.

### Local reflection

```tcl
proc f {} {
    set longvariable 1
    return [info locals]
}
puts [f]
```

Original C Tcl 9.0.3 output is `longvariable`. Current compact output uses `set a 1` and returns `a`.

### Command reflection/public API

```tcl
proc longprocedure {} {return ok}
puts [info procs longprocedure]
puts [longprocedure]
```

Current compact output renames the definition and direct call to `a`, but leaves `info procs longprocedure`. The reflected result disappears. External callers, `rename`, `namespace export/import`, `interp alias`, traces, callbacks, `unknown`, TclOO method installation, and native extensions can likewise observe or invoke the original name.

`find_barrier_scopes` only suppresses variable compaction for registry dynamic-barrier invocations; it does not model reflection generally and does not guard procedure renaming.

## Fix direction

Split the contract:

- Semantics-preserving compact mode may rename only symbols proven non-observable by whole-program escape/reflection analysis.
- Public procedures should be preserved unless a closed-world/isolated proof covers all registry-declared command-name consumers and external entry points.
- Variable reflection/name-as-data roles must be registry descriptors/hooks consumed by a generic escape analysis.
- Dynamic/unknown reflection should conservatively block the relevant scope.
- An explicitly named obfuscating/ABI-changing mode may keep broader renaming with clear documentation and a symbol map.

## Tests and acceptance

- Compare `info locals/vars/procs/args/body/default`, `namespace children/which/origin`, traces, aliases, rename, callbacks, unknown, TclOO, safe/sub-interpreters, and native entry points against C Tcl 9.
- TP/FP/TN/FN include fully private locals, reflected locals, exported/public procs, static aliases, dynamic command-name construction, `args`, and nested namespaces.
- Add compact/aggressive differential tests, LSP e2e, VS Code tests, and a corpus audit for reflective commands.
- Document the ABI/reflection boundary and exact limits in plain English.

Do not add clippy allows.

issues.title: Minifier-generated alias variables can shadow live Tcl variables
issues.body:
## Problem

Both the default template-deduplication tier and aggressive command/argument/string aliasing inject `set a …`-style preambles. Their collision checks are incomplete.

Default minification only reserves names found in `$name` syntax. Tcl can read a variable through name-taking commands such as `set a`, `upvar`, `global`, `variable`, array operations, and traces.

Input evaluated in a context where `x=X` and `a=SENTINEL`:

```tcl
puts "very long dynamic value $x here"
puts "very long dynamic value $x here"
puts "very long dynamic value $x here"
puts "very long dynamic value $x here"
puts [set a]
```

Current default minification emits:

```tcl
set a {very long dynamic value $x here}
puts [subst $a]
# repeated…
puts [set a]
```

The final value changes from `SENTINEL` to the literal template.

Aggressive aliasing is worse: `collect_symbol_shorts` reserves compacted names, not every existing/global/free variable. For example repeated literal arguments plus `puts $a` can become a preamble `set a verylongliteralvalue` followed by every use as `$a`, overwriting an external or global variable.

Preamble writes can also trigger traces and change `info vars` even when no collision exists.

## Fix direction

Semantics-preserving minification must not introduce a Tcl variable unless it proves the name and write are unobservable in the exact frame.

Options:

1. Avoid runtime aliases in the default tier.
2. Use a fresh namespace/private container only where its creation and writes are themselves unobservable and valid for the dialect.
3. In a closed-world mode, reserve every variable name discovered through registry argument roles, alias/place analysis, reflection, traces, free-variable analysis, and dynamic barriers.
4. Keep runtime-alias transformations only in an explicitly behaviour-changing compression tier.

A longer deny-list or scanning only `$…` is not sufficient.

## Tests and acceptance

- C Tcl differential tests with pre-existing variables, `set name` reads, `upvar`, globals, namespace variables, arrays, traces, `info vars`, TclOO frames, safe/sub-interpreters, and callbacks.
- TP/FP/TN/FN for top-level and nested-body aliasing, dynamic names, Unicode names, and all alias phases.
- Add default/compact/aggressive tests, LSP execute-command e2e, VS Code tests, and corpus execution under a seeded interpreter.
- Document whether each minification tier may add variables or observable writes.

Do not add clippy allows.

issues.title: O102 forwards stale globals across a called proc’s `uplevel #0` write
issues.body:
## Problem

The optimiser has a confirmed silent miscompile, already documented by a test which asserts the known-wrong output.

```tcl
proc setter {} {
    uplevel #0 {
        set x 99
    }
}
set x 5
setter
puts $x
```

C Tcl 9.0.3 prints:

```text
99
```

Current `tcl opt` emits:

```tcl
proc setter {} {
    uplevel #0 {set x 99}
}
setter
puts 5
```

and reports O109 plus O102. The rewritten program prints `5`.

`run_load_forwarding` sees the top-level literal definition and direct read, but the interprocedural effect model does not propagate the called procedure's frame/global write through `uplevel #0` to the caller-visible location. The existing `o102_uplevel_hash_zero_in_called_proc_is_a_known_gap` regression test explicitly expects `puts 5`.

## General fix direction

Model caller/global-frame effects in procedure summaries and memory SSA, rather than naming `uplevel` in O102:

- evaluated-script/frame target behaviour must come from CommandRegistry descriptors/hooks;
- literal levels (`#0`, positive/relative levels) should map to abstract frame locations;
- dynamic levels/scripts conservatively clobber the reachable frame set;
- propagate effects through direct calls, aliases, rename, callbacks/traces, TclOO dispatch, unknown, and SCCs;
- safe/sub-interpreter frames remain isolated.

O102, O109/DSE, SCCP, branch folding, and code sinking should consume the same effect facts so another pass cannot reintroduce the miscompile.

## Tests and acceptance

- Original and fully optimised programs have identical stdout, result, error options, trace effects, and global state under C Tcl 9.
- TP: direct `uplevel #0`, nested call chains, relative levels, list-built scripts, namespace/global writes, and mutual recursion.
- FP: an unrelated local write must not block safe forwarding.
- TN: empty/non-writing uplevel and child-interpreter writes.
- FN: static aliases/renames, callbacks, traces, unknown, TclOO methods, and dynamic scripts/levels.
- Flip the known-wrong test, add per-pass and multipass differentials, native optimisation-diagnostic/LSP e2e, and VS Code apply-optimisation coverage.
- Document the frame-effect lattice and conservative limits.

Do not add clippy allows or compiler command-name branches.
