issues.title: Namespace deletion is implemented twice with different teardown: tcl-vm leaves `namespace path` entries, `namespace unknown` handlers and ensemble commands behind, and resurrects them when the namespace is recreated
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). `namespace delete` is written independently in each runtime, and only one of the two does the full C-compatible teardown.

## runtime/rust's teardown (complete)

`runtime/rust/src/namespace.rs`'s `delete_namespace_by_id` (`:647`) drops the deleted namespaces from *every other* namespace's `namespace path`, citing `TclResetNamespaceParameters` in its own comment (C's path-fixup routine). `runtime/rust/src/interp.rs`'s namespace-delete path (`:2985`) also calls `remove_ensembles_for(&ids)` — deleting ensemble commands whose configured namespace is in the deleted subtree, the C ensemble namespace-deletion hook — before firing unset/command-delete traces and tombstoning the arena node.

## tcl-vm's teardown (incomplete)

`rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs`'s `delete_namespace` (`:3147-3170`) is four `retain` calls over flat maps, starting at `:3160` (`self.commands.retain(...)`): it prunes `commands`, `imported_commands`, global-frame locals, `namespaces`, `ns_exports`, and `ns_intern` — but never touches `ns_paths` or `ns_unknowns`, in either direction (neither the deleted namespace's own entries, nor other namespaces' entries naming it as a path member). It never removes ensembles either. Separately, `ns_path_set` (`:2677`, the only writer of `ns_paths`) has no removal counterpart anywhere in the file, and tcl-vm's `namespace path` *set* (`cmd_namespace.rs:245`) does no existence check at all, where `runtime/rust`'s `ns_path` (`cmd_namespace.rs:504`) errors `namespace "X" not found in "::ns"` for an unresolvable entry.

## Divergence

Verified against tclsh8.6.16:

```tcl
# (a) stale namespace path survives deletion, resurrects on recreation
namespace eval a {proc p {} {return A1}}
namespace eval b {namespace path ::a}
namespace delete ::a
namespace eval b {namespace path}
# tclsh:  {}
# tcl-vm: keeps ::a on b's path; after recreating ::a, `namespace eval b {p}`
#         dispatches the recreated proc where tclsh gives "invalid command name"

# (b) namespace path and namespace unknown both resurrect
namespace eval z {namespace path ::a; namespace unknown {puts UNK}}
namespace delete ::z
namespace eval z {}
namespace eval z {namespace path}
# tclsh:  {} / {}
# tcl-vm: resurrects both

# (c) ensemble command outlives its namespace
namespace eval ens1 {namespace export *; proc sub {} {return S}; namespace ensemble create -command ::myens}
namespace delete ::ens1
info commands ::myens
# tclsh:         {}
# runtime/rust:  deletes it
# tcl-vm:        ::myens stays live

# (d) missing existence check on `namespace path`
namespace eval outer2 {namespace path inner}   # no ::outer2::inner exists
# tclsh & runtime/rust: error: namespace "inner" not found in "::outer2"
# tcl-vm:                succeeds silently
```

## Why it matters

A deleted-and-recreated namespace should start clean; in tcl-vm it inherits stale `namespace path` and `namespace unknown` state from before the deletion, and an ensemble command built over a deleted namespace keeps dispatching. Both are the kind of bug that only shows up after a namespace is torn down and rebuilt — a pattern test suites and interactive `tclsh` sessions hit routinely.

## Relationship to open issues

#1412 covers WASM-runtime rename/re-home defects; this is namespace-scope teardown and points the other way (tcl-vm is the deficient side).

## Cleanup

Lift the teardown invariants (path fixup across all namespaces, ensemble removal, per-namespace parameter reset) into a `tcl-cmd-core::namespace` core over the `Namespaces` role trait, so the flat-map and tree stores implement one checklist; add the existence check to the VM's `namespace path` set, mirroring `ns_not_found`. The VM already gates the *resolution* path tier on `TclVersion::has_namespace_path()` (8.4 has none) at `interp.rs:2876`; runtime/rust has no equivalent gate, but `namespace path` is registry-gated `TCL85_PLUS` so it is unreachable there in practice.

**Scale:** medium — one shared crate (`tcl-cmd-core`) gains the teardown core, and both runtimes' `delete_namespace`/`delete_namespace_by_id` switch over to it.

issues.title: Ensemble subcommand resolution and the `namespace ensemble create` option table are hand-rolled twice (tcl-vm inline, runtime/rust `ensemble.rs`) instead of `tcl-cmd-core::prefix`, and disagree with C on which options exist and abbreviate
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). The contract's only documented ensemble exception is the VM's `oxford_or` enumeration wording — the resolution rule and the option table are not exceptions, yet both are written twice.

## tcl-vm's inline resolution and option table

`rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs`'s `dispatch_ensemble` inlines `exact, else unique starts_with` resolution itself (`:2421`: `subs.iter().filter(|s| s.starts_with(&sub))`) with its own `oxford_or`. `rust/tcl-vm/src/cmd_namespace.rs`'s `ns_ensemble_create` option parsing is a hand-rolled `match` whose catch-all arm (`:410-415`) rejects `-parameters` while the error message it prints lists `-parameters` as valid — and accepts `-namespace` above it (`:383`), an option C has no such flag for.

## runtime/rust's separate `ensemble.rs` copy

`runtime/rust/src/ensemble.rs` has its own `resolve_subcommand` (`:67-84`) — the same exact-then-unique-prefix algorithm, a second copy — and its own `must_be` (`:89`), a second oxford-or enumeration beside the VM's. Neither goes through `tcl_cmd_core::prefix::scan`/`choice_list`. `runtime/rust/src/cmd_namespace.rs`'s `apply_ensemble_option` catch-all (`:824`) is an exact-match table with C's message text but no abbreviation support. The contract only documents `oxford_or`'s enumeration wording as an exception (`docs/design/contracts/shared-utility-contracts-rust.md:173`) — not the resolution rule or the option table.

## Divergence

Verified against tclsh8.6.16/9.0.4:

```tcl
namespace ensemble create -comm ::ab5 -sub go
::ab5 go
# tclsh:               succeeds, ::ab5 go works
# tcl-vm/runtime-rust: both reject the abbreviations

namespace ensemble create -namespace ::x
# tclsh:  bad option "-namespace": must be -command, -map, -parameters,
#         -prefixes, -subcommands, or -unknown
# tcl-vm: accepts it

namespace ensemble create -parameters {p}
# tclsh & runtime/rust: accept
# tcl-vm:               errors with a message that lists -parameters among
#                       the valid options

namespace ensemble create -command   # odd arity
# tclsh:         wrong # args: should be "namespace ensemble create ?option value ...?"
# tcl-vm:        missing value to go with "-command"
# runtime/rust:  missing value for option
```

## Why it matters

`namespace ensemble create`'s option handling disagrees with C on which options even exist (`-namespace` accepted where it shouldn't be, `-parameters` rejected where it should be accepted) and neither runtime supports C's standard option abbreviation, so scripts written against real tclsh's ensemble API fail or behave differently under both engines — in different ways from each other.

## Cleanup

Move the subcommand resolution (and the ensemble-flavoured enumeration, keeping the documented `, or`-for-two quirk) into one shared home — `tcl_cmd_core::prefix::scan` for the match plus one ensemble enumeration helper — and declare the `namespace ensemble` option set as a `prefix::OptionTable` both runtimes resolve through, as the contract requires of new command modules.

**Scale:** medium — one shared crate gains the resolution/enumeration helper and an option-table type; both runtimes' `namespace ensemble create` switch over.

issues.title: The workspace index splits `namespace import` patterns with `rsplit_once("::")` — the exact colon-run drift tcl-vm fixed and pinned — and three more sites fake globbing with `strip_suffix('*')`
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). The LSP has the same colon-run bug tcl-vm already found and fixed in itself, plus three more sites that reimplement glob matching badly.

## tcl-vm's fix (already shipped)

`rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs`'s `import_commands` (`:3033-3040`) used to split with `rsplit_once("::")`, leaving a trailing colon behind on a colon-run pattern; it now uses `tcl_cmd_core::namespace::tail`/`qualifiers` (`:3038`, `:3040`), with its own comment noting the old rule "left `src:` behind". `rust/tcl-vm/tests/namespace_colon_runs_e2e.rs:221`'s `import_and_forget_collapse_runs_in_patterns` pins `::src7:::im*` against tclsh8.6.

## The workspace index's unfixed copy

`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/workspace_index.rs`'s `index_command_links` derives a glob import's source namespace with the exact old rule: `imp.pattern.rsplit_once("::")` (`:1661`). The exact-import branch beside it uses a *third*, different rule again: `imp.pattern.rsplit("::").find(|s| !s.is_empty())` (`:1674`). Separately, three sites decide "does this import pattern bind this bare name?" with `strip_suffix('*')` plus string concatenation — a hand-rolled pseudo-glob that only handles a trailing `*` — in `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs:770`, `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:1280`, and `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:1983`, while `tcl_syntax::glob::string_match` is the owner and is used correctly for `tail_pattern` elsewhere in the same workspace-index file (`:4811`).

## Divergence

```tcl
# file 1
namespace eval src {namespace export im*; proc imp {} {return I}}
# file 2
namespace eval use {namespace import ::src:::im*}
```

`rsplit_once("::")` yields source namespace `::src:` (trailing colon), so the glob-import row never matches — cross-file go-to-definition, references, and W123 suppression through the import all fail — while tcl-vm resolves the same script (its own e2e test asserts it). For the `strip_suffix('*')` copies: `namespace import ::src::he*r` or `::src::helpe?` binds `helper` in real Tcl and in the runtimes' `is_exported` glob, but matches nothing at these three LSP/analyser sites.

## Why it matters

A colon-run in an import pattern is unusual but not invalid Tcl, and tcl-vm proved it needs handling by fixing the identical bug in itself; the LSP silently drops cross-file navigation for exactly that shape. The `strip_suffix('*')` sites miss any import pattern using `?` or `[...]` glob syntax, or a `*` that isn't at the very end — quietly under-resolving real imports rather than erroring.

## Cleanup

Split import patterns with `tcl_cmd_core::namespace::qualifiers`/`tail` (one rule for both the glob and exact branches) and match the tail with `tcl_syntax::glob::string_match`, folding the three `strip_suffix('*')` copies into one helper next to `tcl_lsp_core::namespace_import`'s existing shared decision functions.

**Scale:** medium — four call sites across two crates (`tcl-lsp-core`, `tcl-compiler`'s analyser) converge on two already-existing shared functions.

issues.title: `naming::qualify` / `key_holder_and_tail` exist as "the one shared join/split", but the lowerer, item tree, document symbols and workspace symbols each hand-roll their own — and they disagree
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). A helper documented as the one shared join/split for namespace keys has five more re-derivations beside the one correct copy, and they produce different answers on the same colon-named input.

## The canonical shared join/split

`rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs`'s `qualify` (`:764`) is documented as "the one shared join for the analyser / signature-scan / class-lattice qualifiers, so the absolute-name rule cannot drift between them" — its doc explicitly forbids re-parsing the joined result. `key_holder_and_tail` (`:266`) is the construction-inverse split that exists precisely because `rfind("::")` gets colon-named segments wrong (#934). The analyser's own `scope.rs` uses both correctly: its `join_namespace` (`:78`) calls `qualifier_segments_owned(part)` (`:82`) on the *written* component, then joins with one exact `::`, never re-parsing the accumulated key.

## Four re-derivations that disagree

`rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/mod.rs` has its own `join_namespace` that joins then re-parses: `normalise_qualified_name(&format!("{parent}::{child}"))` (`:81`) — exactly the re-parse `qualify` documents as forbidden — and its `proc_namespace` splits the key with `n.rfind("::")` (`:88`). `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/item_tree.rs` has a third join, `join_ns` (`:188`, no written-name canonicalisation) and an `enclosing_namespace` via `rsplit_once("::")` (`:180`). `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/document_symbols.rs` has a fourth join, `join_namespace` (`:242`), whose `enclosing_namespace`-derived `home` (`:499`) is then *compared for equality* against `join_namespace`-built node names in `place_under_namespace` — so the two locally-invented rules have to agree byte-for-byte with each other, and don't. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/workspace_symbols.rs`'s `namespace_of` (`:113`) is a fifth rule again (`strip_prefix("::")` + `rfind`).

## Divergence

```tcl
namespace eval a:::b {}
proc a::b::q {} {}
```

The analyser (via `qualify`) homes the proc at `::a::b`; `item_tree::join_ns` and `document_symbols::join_namespace` name the namespace node `::a:::b` instead, so `place_under_namespace` never matches and the outline strands the proc outside its own namespace node.

On the analyser's own colon-named key `proc : {} {}`:
- `item_tree`/`document_symbols` → `":"`
- `workspace_symbols` → `None`
- canonical `key_holder_and_tail` → `"::"`

And `lowering::join_namespace(":::", ":")` collapses to `"::"` — losing the colon-named namespace entirely — where `qualify` yields `"::::::"`.

## Why it matters

Document outline and workspace symbols are user-facing navigation features; a namespace containing a colon-named segment (unusual, but legal Tcl, and the exact shape issue #934 was filed over once already) strands its own members outside their namespace node in the outline, and the five helpers can disagree on the same key well before colon-naming enters the picture, since each was hand-rolled independently.

## Relationship to open issues

#1387 (LSP diagramData reimplements tcl-diagram) and #1397 (diagnostic-builder literals) are the same *genre* of LSP-side duplication but different subjects; nothing open covers the `::` join/split helpers specifically.

## Cleanup

Delete the four local helpers and call `tcl_syntax::naming::qualify` and `key_holder_and_tail` (the analyser's `scope.rs` shows the correct pattern: canonicalise the *written* component, join the *constructed* key verbatim); `proc_namespace` and both `enclosing_namespace`s become one `key_holder_and_tail(...).0`.

**Scale:** medium — four call sites across three crates (`tcl-compiler`'s lowering and analyser, `tcl-lsp-core`) converge on two already-existing shared functions.

issues.title: scan_var_name / parse_var_ref_parts stop after two colons, splitting $a:::b into var a:: plus literal :b
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). Both runtimes' subst-engine bareword scanners independently re-derive `$name` parsing and both stop short of the colon-run rule their own lexer already gets right.

## The canonical rule (tcl-lexer, pinned)

Tcl's `Tcl_ParseVarName` consumes an entire colon run once a `::` separator starts — a bare `$a:::b` names the single variable `a:::b`. `rust/tcl-lexer/src/lexer.rs`'s `parse_var` implements this explicitly: once `ch == ':' && self.peek_byte(1) == Some(b':')` (`:800`), a trailing `while self.current_byte() == Some(b':') { self.pos += 1; }` loop (`:805-807`) consumes the whole run. `var_consumes_entire_colon_run` (`:2049`) is a regression test citing issue 162, pinning `$a:::b` → `Var` token `a:::b`. `tcl_syntax::naming::qualifier_segments` documents the same rule: a colon run of any length is a single separator.

## Two runtime scanners that stop short

`runtime/rust/src/parse.rs`'s `scan_var_name` (`:174-188`) only consumes `::` pairs — `else if c == b':' && p + 1 < len && src[p + 1] == b':' { p += 2; }` (`:181-182`) — with no loop to eat a third-or-later colon, so it stops mid-run; `scan_parts_at_depth` (`:276`) calls it for a bare `$name`'s extent inside subst/array-index substitution. `rust/tcl-vm/src/subst.rs`'s `parse_var_ref_parts` has the identical shape: `while j + 1 < n && b[j] == b':' && b[j + 1] == b':' { j += 2; ... }` (`:455`) with the same missing trailing-colon consumption; `subst_var` (`:319`) calls it for both the `subst` command and PUSH-time literal resolution.

## Divergence

Verified against tclsh 8.6/9.0: with no `a:::b` defined,

```tcl
subst {$a:::b}
# tclsh: error: can't read "a:::b" (the whole name)
```

Both engines compute the truncated extent (base `a::`, exactly 2 colons consumed), so they either attempt to read `a::` and, on success, append the literal `:b` after its value, or raise the `a::`-named error instead of tclsh's `a:::b`-named one.

## Why it matters

`subst` and ordinary word substitution are on every script's hot path; a colon-run variable name (unusual, but not invalid — namespace separators can repeat) is silently mis-split into a truncated variable reference plus stray literal text, or raises an error naming the wrong variable, in both runtime engines at once.

## Relationship to open issues

Distinct from #1393 (compiler lowering; this is the runtimes' subst engines). Not covered elsewhere. A sibling finding covers the same functions' brace-nesting dialect-blindness — a distinct bug, at the same call sites.

## Cleanup

Extract the "consume `::` then every subsequent colon" loop into one shared byte-oriented helper next to `tcl_syntax::naming::qualifier_segments`, and have `tcl-lexer::parse_var`, `runtime/rust::scan_var_name`, and `tcl-vm::parse_var_ref_parts` all call it. Not dialect-specific — the colon-run rule is invariant 8.4-9.1 per contract rule 3.

**Scale:** small — one shared helper, three call sites updated to use it.

issues.title: Both runtimes hardcode the Tcl 8.x first-close-brace rule for ${...} in subst, even when emulating Tcl 9
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). A dialect split that both the lexer and the analyser gate correctly is hardcoded to the 8.x answer in both runtimes' subst engines, regardless of which release they're emulating.

## The dialect gate that exists (tcl-lexer, analyser)

Tcl 9's `Tcl_ParseVarName` tracks brace depth and backslash pairs inside `${name}` (`${a{b}c}` names `a{b}c`), while 8.x stops at the first literal `}`. `rust/tcl-lexer/src/lexer.rs`'s `parse_var` gates this explicitly: `if self.config.braced_var.nests()` (`:729`) selects the Tcl 9 nested-tracking branch versus the 8.x first-close behaviour. `rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs`'s `is_brace_substitutable` models the same split via its nesting parameter (`:567`), and `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs:2035` is an existing correct consumer, passing `self.lexer_config().braced_var.nests()`.

## Two runtime scanners that never check the dialect

`runtime/rust/src/parse.rs`'s `scan_parts_at_depth` scans its `${name}` branch to the first `'}'` unconditionally (`:258`) — `scan_parts` takes no dialect parameter at all. `rust/tcl-vm/src/subst.rs`'s `parse_var_ref_parts` does the same: its brace branch finds the first close-brace with no dialect check (`:440`). This is despite `rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs`'s `InterpState` tracking the emulated release on every interpreter (`runtime_version`, `:420`) — a fact `subst.rs` never reads — and `runtime/rust`'s module doc claiming to follow reference Tcl 9.0.

## Divergence

Verified against tclsh9.0.4 and tclsh8.6.16:

```tcl
set {a{b}c} WORLD
subst {${a{b}c}}
# tclsh9.0.4:  WORLD
# tclsh8.6.16: error: can't read "a{b"
```

Neither runtime engine consults the active dialect, so a Tcl-9-configured VM or WASM build still applies the 8.6 answer inside `subst`.

## Why it matters

A build explicitly configured to emulate Tcl 9 should parse `${a{b}c}` per the Tcl 9 grammar; instead both engines silently fall back to the Tcl 8.x rule inside `subst`, so a script relying on Tcl 9's nested-brace variable names either errors or reads the wrong variable, even though the interpreter otherwise believes itself to be Tcl 9.

## Relationship to open issues

Distinct from #1419's doc-note (`expr` `#`-comments, `tcl-vm/src/expr.rs`); this is `${...}` nesting in `subst.rs`. Distinct from #1393. Related to the dialect-threading agent's host-`LexerConfig` finding but different code (runtime subst scanners vs. compile-time host configs).

## Cleanup

Thread the interpreter's fixed dialect fact into both engines' `${...}` scan: give `runtime/rust::scan_parts` a nesting flag, and have `tcl-vm::parse_var_ref_parts` read `self.runtime_version()` — ideally calling `tcl_syntax::naming::is_brace_substitutable`'s braced-name walk instead of a third re-derivation. This finding *is* the missing dialect gate: Tcl 9 nested vs. 8.x first-close `${...}` parsing, which neither runtime engine gates on at all today.

**Scale:** small — two call sites gain a dialect parameter, ideally routed through the existing `is_brace_substitutable` walk.

issues.title: elem_ref's open > 0 guard makes set (x) 5 a scalar named (x), not array "" element x
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). tcl-vm's single choke point for array-element name splitting adds a condition absent from both C Tcl and every other Rust copy of the same split.

## What C (and the rest of the codebase) does

C Tcl's array-element parse (`TclObjLookupVarEx`) only requires a trailing close paren; it takes everything before the first open paren as the array name, even when that's empty — so `(x)` is array `""` element `x`. `rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs`'s `split_array_name` (`:973-995`) mirrors this with no base-non-empty requirement in its no-braces fallback branch (`:988-993`). `runtime/rust/src/frame.rs`'s `split_array_ref` (`:697`) matches it too — no `open > 0` guard.

## tcl-vm's extra guard

`rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs`'s `elem_ref` — the single choke point gating `var_get` (`:4491`), `var_set` (`:4499`), `exists_var`, `trace_key`, and `ensure_trace_variable` — adds an extra condition: `if open > 0 && name.ends_with(')')` (`:359`), refusing to recognise a leading-paren reference as an array element. `unset_one` (`:4280-4283`) re-derives the identical `open > 0` guard inline instead of calling `elem_ref`, so the bug is duplicated even within the same file.

## Divergence

Verified against tclsh9.0/8.6:

```tcl
set (x) 5
array exists {}
# tclsh: 1
array names {}
# tclsh: x
array get {}
# tclsh: x 5
```

tcl-vm instead creates an ordinary scalar variable literally named `(x)` — a different variable, with different `array exists`/`info exists` answers than real Tcl.

## Why it matters

`(x)` as shorthand for the empty-named array's element `x` is an obscure but real Tcl idiom (arises naturally from a variable substitution that evaluates to an empty array name, e.g. `set arr {}; set $arr(x) 5`); tcl-vm silently reinterprets it as a scalar with a parenthesis in its name instead, so `array exists`/`array get`/`array names {}` disagree with tclsh on the same script.

## Cleanup

Drop the `open > 0` condition from `elem_ref` to match `split_array_name` and `split_array_ref` (both already correct); make `unset_one` call `elem_ref` instead of re-deriving the guard inline.

**Scale:** small — one function's guard condition, plus one inline duplicate folded into a call.

issues.title: simple_var_name (wasm/backend.rs) and variable_name (wasm/leaf_invoke.rs) are byte-for-byte the same $name/${name} extractor, twice
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). A documented, deliberate exception to a shared helper has picked up two more independent re-derivations inside the very module the exception names.

## The documented exception

The WASM codegen backend needs to decide whether a word is a whole simple variable reference eligible for direct load — the decision `rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/values.rs`'s `is_bare_var_name` (`:34-39`) makes for the bytecode backend: alphanumerics, `_`, and `:` (any run), documented as the "looser codegen-side contract" exception at `docs/design/contracts/shared-utility-contracts-rust.md:161`, versus the stricter `::`-segmented `tcl_syntax::naming::is_bare_var_name` quick fixes use. The exception names only `codegen/values.rs`; it is `fn is_bare_var_name`, not `pub`, so the wasm files cannot call it as written.

## Two more re-derivations

`rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/wasm/backend.rs`'s `simple_var_name` (`:1379-1389`) strips `${...}` or `$` then validates the alnum/underscore/colon charset. `rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/wasm/leaf_invoke.rs`'s `variable_name` (`:501-514`) is identical logic with renamed locals (`spelling`/`byte` instead of `word`/`b`). Neither calls `values::is_bare_var_name`, nor each other.

## Divergence

Structural duplication; no user-visible divergence yet — both copies encode the identical charset rule, so nothing has drifted between them yet, but nothing keeps them in sync either.

## Why it matters

Two files inside the WASM codegen backend independently reimplement the exact predicate the contract already carved out one documented exception for; a future edit to the charset rule (e.g. tightening it, or handling a new dialect quirk) has three places to change instead of one, with no compiler error to catch a missed site.

## Relationship to open issues

Adjacent to #1376 but distinct: #1376 is clause-body text reconstruction, not the bare-variable-name predicate.

## Cleanup

Hoist one `pub(crate)` function in `codegen::values` that strips `$`/`${...}` and validates the charset; both wasm sites call it.

**Scale:** small — one function made crate-visible, two call sites deleted in favour of it.

issues.title: Five ad hoc $/${...} strippers in tcl-lsp-core disagree on unclosed ${x: three silently drop the stray brace
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). tcl-lsp-core reimplements "strip the `$`/`${...}` decoration" five times instead of calling the shared helper, and three of the five copies handle malformed input differently from the other two.

## The canonical helper (and two correct copies)

`rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs`'s `var_reference` (`:346-354`) strips a variable reference's substitution sigil while keeping any array-index suffix. On a joint `${`-prefix-and-`}`-suffix match it returns the inner text; otherwise it strips only a leading `$`. Critically, on an *unclosed* `${x` it falls to the plain-`$`-strip branch and returns `{x` — the stray `{` survives, so the result never accidentally equals a real symbol name. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/semantic_tokens.rs`'s `object_handle_name` (`:2742`) and `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/completion.rs`'s `strip_instance_var` (`:1251`) independently reimplement the same fail-safe shape (the latter's stray `{` then gets rejected by a later bareword check).

## Three that silently do the wrong thing

`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs`'s `instance_method_at_cursor` (`:1338-1342`) strips the leading `$` and then does `rest.strip_prefix('{').map_or(rest, |r| r.strip_suffix('}').unwrap_or(r))` — on unclosed `${x` this succeeds the inner `strip_prefix('{')`, fails the `strip_suffix('}')`, and `unwrap_or` falls back to the *already-brace-stripped* remainder, silently discarding the stray `{` and producing the clean-looking name `x`. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs`'s `strip_var_decoration` (`:3440-3446`) is byte-for-byte the same wrong shape. `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/declaration.rs`'s `bare_name` (`:327-334`) is a third, differently-wrong mechanism — unpaired `trim_start_matches('{')`/`trim_end_matches('}')` char-class trims, plus it strips a leading `::` that none of the other four siblings do.

## Divergence

For mid-edit `${x` (unclosed) where `x` is a real symbol defined elsewhere: `definition.rs` and `references.rs` both compute the bare name `x`, so Go to Definition on `${x method` and Find References on `${x}` resolve to the unrelated real symbol `x` — a wrong navigation target that the LSP's own `semantic_tokens.rs`/`completion.rs` copies correctly avoid, two files over.

## Why it matters

Mid-edit, unclosed-brace variable text is exactly the state a user's buffer is in while typing `${myvar}`; three of five LSP features silently resolve it to an unrelated existing symbol instead of failing safe, giving Go to Definition and Find References a plausible-looking but wrong target during ordinary editing.

## Cleanup

Replace all five local helpers with `tcl_syntax::naming::var_reference` (layering the bareword check where needed), so every feature agrees on the fail-safe unclosed-brace behaviour.

**Scale:** medium — five call sites within one crate (`tcl-lsp-core`) converge on an already-existing shared function; mechanical, not exploratory.

issues.title: `builtin_command_visible_for_surface` gates only `::tcl::mathfunc::*`: `lassign`, `dict`, `coroutine`, `try`, `lmap`, `lpop`, `lseq` and TclOO stay callable on both engines at every `--tcl-version`
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). The command registry records every builtin's introducing release and every static consumer enforces it, but both runtime engines' only version filter is scoped to math functions, leaving the rest of the builtin table reachable at any emulated release.

## The registry fact (enforced everywhere static)

`CommandRegistry::get_for_dialect` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs:645-653`) is the availability primitive, documented at `rust/tcl-registry/src/profile_queries.rs:56` as the single query `ProfileQueries::resolve_command` wraps. W002/W123, the lifecycle diagnostics, completion, formatter keywords, and the minifier all route through it. Individual commands carry the fact plainly: `lpop` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/lpop.rs:82`) is declared `dialects: Some(DialectSet::TCL90_PLUS)`, a Tcl-9.0-only command; `lassign` (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/lassign.rs:43-53`) carries two dialect-scoped forms, `TCL86_PLUS` for the shape that makes every `varName` optional and an exact `TCL85` form for the older, stricter shape — so `lassign` itself is unavailable before 8.5 by the same table.

## The runtime gate (mathfunc-only)

Both engines' sole version filter is narrower than the table it reads from. `Vm::builtin_command_visible_for_surface` (`rust/tcl-vm/src/interp.rs:1733-1740`) is documented as "the registry's only versioned command filter", but its entire body is `RuntimeExprSurface::permits_builtin_math_function_command(name)` — a predicate that (`rust/tcl-registry/src/expr_surface.rs:247-254`) resolves to `true` for any name outside the `::tcl::mathfunc::*` table, by design ("Commands outside the registry's builtin math-function table remain visible: they may be user-defined replacements or extensions"), which is correct for *that* predicate but wrong as the *only* gate. `runtime/rust/src/interp.rs:1127` repeats the identical single-predicate body in the WASM runtime. Neither engine ever calls `get_for_dialect` for a non-mathfunc command, so `lassign`/`dict`/`coroutine`/`try`/`lmap`/`lpop`/`lseq` and TclOO stay invocable at every `--tcl-version`. The iRules test harness works around exactly this gap in Tcl rather than in the engine: `rust/tcl-irule-test/tcl/compat84.tcl:20` polyfills `dict`/`lassign`/`lrepeat`/`lreverse` and leans on `tmm_shim.tcl` to hide the natives it cannot otherwise suppress.

## Divergence

```tcl
# tclvm --tcl-version 8.4 -c 'puts [lassign {a b} x]'
# tclvm:    b
# tclsh8.4: invalid command name "lassign"
```

Fuzz campaigns pinned with `--subject-tcl-version 8.6` record every 8.6-absent command as a spurious divergence rather than a real one.

## Why it matters

A script written and validated against an older `--tcl-version` gets no signal that it is calling a command the real interpreter at that release does not have — the exact failure mode dialect pinning exists to catch. It also pollutes fuzz campaigns pinned to an older subject release with divergences that are really just registry availability the runtime never checked.

## Relationship to open issues

Not #1390 (hardcoded names) and not #1373 (missing commands — that is the reverse shape, commands absent when they should be present; this is commands present when they should not be).

## Cleanup

Widen `builtin_command_visible_for_surface` to `registry_for_profile(profile).get_for_dialect(name, profile.availability_mask)`, keeping the mathfunc branch as one case alongside it. This requires interps to carry a `&'static DialectProfile` rather than a bare `TclVersion` — today an iRules-pinned VM validates against plain `tcl8.4`, discarding the vendor bit. The runtimes hold only a `TclVersion`, never a profile, so vendor availability is unreachable at run time; fixing the command gate and giving interps a profile handle are the same change.

**Scale:** large

issues.title: `tcl-fuzz` can pin the subject engine's Tcl release but not the reference's or the replay's, and the pinned release is not part of the findings namespace
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). `--subject-tcl-version` pins one half of a fuzzing pair, but the reference engine, the replay path, and the findings namespace were never extended to match.

## What is pinned

`subject_tcl_version` (`rust/tcl-fuzz/src/main.rs:118-127`) is documented as existing so a campaign against an older `tclsh` does not "record every deliberate 8.6-vs-9.0 semantic change as a divergence — which is exactly how issue #1328's eight 'findings' were produced." When set, `main.rs:322-324` extends only `pair.subject_args` — `reference_args` is never touched in the same function. Both halves of a `tclvm` ↔ `runtime-rust` pair independently accept `--tcl-version` (`rust/tcl-vm-cli/src/main.rs:127`, `runtime/rust/examples/run_script.rs:86`), so the reference side of such a pair could in principle be pinned too; `Engine::args()` simply has no per-engine release setting to make that possible for a general pair.

## What is not pinned

`replay_command` (`rust/tcl-fuzz/src/main.rs:434-440`) takes no version argument at all. When a recorded finding is replayed, the closest it comes to honouring the release it was found at is `main.rs:462-469`, which prints a "replay backend versions differ from the finding" warning rather than reproducing at the recorded release — so an 8.6-pinned finding replays at each engine's default (typically 9.0) and may simply not reproduce. The findings registry compounds this: `fn findings_dir` (`main.rs:270-273`) keys `pair_findings_dir` on the engine pair alone, so campaigns run at different releases against the same pair share one seed registry, and a finding recorded at 8.6 collides in the same directory as one recorded at 9.0.

## Divergence

```
An 8.6-subject vs 9.0-reference campaign records every genuine 8.6-vs-9.0
semantic change as a "finding" -- the exact failure mode
--subject-tcl-version was added to prevent, reproduced one level up
(subject pinned, reference not).

A seed recorded at --subject-tcl-version 8.6 replays at 9.0/9.0 by
default and may not reproduce; the tool's only response is a WARNING,
not a refusal or an automatic re-pin.
```

## Why it matters

A campaign that pins only the subject can still generate the exact class of spurious cross-release findings the pinning feature exists to eliminate, just by leaving the reference engine unpinned. A recorded finding that cannot be reliably replayed at its own recorded release is a triage dead end.

## Relationship to open issues

Related to #1328's motivation, but that fix is already in-tree as `--subject-tcl-version`; this is the remaining half — the reference side, replay, and the findings namespace. Not #1399.

## Cleanup

Make the release a campaign-level fact: one `--tcl-version` applied to every pinnable engine in the pair (refused, not silently ignored, for an engine that cannot be pinned — mirroring the existing refusal for an unpinnable subject), carried into `Cmd::Replay`, and folded into `pair_findings_dir` so different releases of the same pair get separate registries. The fuzzer already treats the release as a per-campaign fact; the gap is applying it to only one of the two engines and never persisting it into replay or the registry key.

**Scale:** medium

issues.title: Claude Skills read a stale AI-prompt copy where W308/O102 name different diagnostics than the registry
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). VS Code's Copilot chat and 21 Claude Code skills read two independently-maintained copies of the same diagnostic catalogue, and the copies have silently diverged on what individual codes mean.

## The generated copy

`ai/prompts/tcl_system.md` is regenerated by `cargo xtask gen-ai-diagnostics` from the `DiagCode` registry (`rust/tcl-core-types/src/diag_code.rs`) and correctly lists `W308 => diag(Warning, true, "Unknown TclOO method — …")` (`diag_code.rs:588`), matching the generated prompt. `rust/xtask/src/gen_ai.rs:43-52`'s `AI_TEMPLATES` list enumerates every file the generator writes — four prompt/skill files under `ai/prompts/` and `ai/claude/skills/{tcl,irule}-optimise/` — and `ai/claude/skills/_prompts/*.md` is not among them.

## The stale copy

21 Claude Code skills instead read `ai/claude/skills/_prompts/tcl_system.md`, a hand-maintained file with no generator and no regeneration step. It has drifted from the registry: `ai/claude/skills/_prompts/tcl_system.md:27` defines W308 as "`subst` without `-nocommands` — risk of unintended command execution", a different diagnostic entirely, and line 30 defines O102 as "Fold constant `[expr {...}]` command substitutions" against the registry's "forward a variable's single reaching literal load to its use sites". The same stale file is also missing a dozen codes present in the generated copy and the registry — E005, E006, W107, W109, W135 through W147, W217, W218, W305, and S103 are all absent from its Errors/Style/Security/Shimmer lines. `ai/claude/skills/tcl-explain/SKILL.md:13` (and `ai/claude/skills/irule-explain/SKILL.md:13`, reading the equally stale `irules_system.md`) instructs the agent to read this file at runtime as its only source of diagnostic-code domain knowledge.

## Divergence

```
Ask tcl-explain to explain diagnostic W308 in some analysed code:

Skill (reading the stale copy):        "subst without -nocommands --
                                         risk of unintended command
                                         execution"
LSP (the diagnostic actually emitted): "Unknown TclOO method -- the
                                         method is not defined on the
                                         receiver's statically-known
                                         class or any of its
                                         superclasses"
```

The same collision exists for O102.

## Why it matters

A user who asks tcl-explain (or any of the 20 other skills sharing this file) to explain a real W308 or O102 diagnostic gets a confident, wrong explanation of an entirely different diagnostic — the skill has no way to notice the mismatch, since it never sees the registry, only its own stale snapshot.

## Relationship to open issues

Not #1404 (false generator-provenance headers) — that is a different defect on a different file; this is two genuinely independent delivery paths for the same content with no sync mechanism between them.

## Cleanup

Either delete `ai/claude/skills/_prompts/` and point every `SKILL.md` at the registry-generated `ai/prompts/*.md` files directly, or add the skill copies as further `AI_TEMPLATES` outputs of `gen-ai-diagnostics` so its `--check` mode catches drift between them going forward. The generated copy tracks the live registry on every xtask run; the skill copy is a point-in-time snapshot with no regeneration step of its own.

**Scale:** small

issues.title: VS Code/JetBrains/Sublime hand-roll number/escape/variable regexes that miss 9.0 forms and aren't colon-run aware
issues.body:
Found by the cross-surface centralisation audit following #1419's numeral-parser precedent (sibling of the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit). The three TextMate-family grammars hand-author their own number, escape, and variable-name regexes, and all three have drifted from the lexical rules `tcl-syntax`/`tcl-lexer` actually implement.

## What the generator covers

`gen-tmlanguage-keywords`'s module doc (`rust/xtask/src/gen_tmlanguage_keywords.rs:41`) states plainly that everything except the keyword alternations is hand-authored template text the generator never touches — the number/escape/variable regex bodies are entirely outside its `--check` coverage.

## Where the hand-authored regexes diverge

The canonical colon-run rule (`rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs:57-58`) treats a run of two or more colons as a single separator of any length. VS Code's variable regex (`editors/vscode/syntaxes/tcl.tmLanguage.json:343`) instead requires exactly two literal colons per separator — `\$(?:[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*::)*[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(?:\([^)]*\))?` — so a third colon in a run breaks the repeating group and the match falls back to only the first segment. Sublime's independently-authored YAML copy (`editors/sublime-text/Tcl.sublime-syntax:209`) has the same bug, and JetBrains ships a byte-identical copy of the VS Code grammar (`editors/jetbrains/src/main/resources/syntaxes/tcl.tmLanguage.json:1`), so all three editors share it. The canonical octal escape (`rust/tcl-lexer/src/substitution.rs:189-191`) caps at 3 digits when the first is `0`-`3` but only 2 digits when the first is `4`-`7`; VS Code's escape regex (`tcl.tmLanguage.json:445`) is a flat `[0-7]{1,3}` with no first-digit cap, and has no `\U` alternative at all even though the canonical scanner accepts 1-8 hex digits after `\U` (`substitution.rs:139`). Sublime repeats the same octal/`\U` gaps independently (`Tcl.sublime-syntax:281`).

## Divergence

```tcl
set x $foo:::bar
# naming.rs: foo:::bar is one qualified name
# the grammars: highlight only $foo as a variable; :::bar is unhighlighted

puts "\777"
# substitution.rs: decodes as octal \77 (63, '?') followed by literal '7'
# the grammars: colour the entire \777 as one escape sequence
```

## Why it matters

Syntax highlighting silently disagrees with what the lexer actually parses, across all three TextMate-derived editors (VS Code, JetBrains, Sublime) at once — a 9.0 numeral literal or a `\777` escape displays with the wrong token boundaries in every one of them, and a colon-run-qualified variable name is only partially highlighted.

## Relationship to open issues

Distinct from #1394 (the dialect-id catalogue) — that issue's own fix point explicitly disclaims covering the token grammar; this is the lexical regex bodies themselves.

## Cleanup

Extend `gen-tmlanguage-keywords` (or add a sibling generator) to render the number/escape/variable regex bodies from `tcl_syntax::number`, the lexer's backslash tables, and `tcl_syntax::naming`, and gate all three grammar files with `--check` the same way the keyword alternations already are. The dialect-flavoured Tcl 8.4/9.0 `sublime-syntax` files extend the base grammar with no lexical overrides of their own, so selecting "Tcl 9.0" does not turn on `0d`/`_` recognition — the grammars are dialect-blind at the lexical level regardless of which dialect variant is active.

**Scale:** medium

issues.title: Tracking: cross-surface syntax/semantics centralisation audit (follow-on from #1419)
issues.body:
#1419 found multiple divergent numeral parsers and centralised them. This audit swept the same shape — **divergent re-implementations of logic a shared owner should hold, and dialect facts re-derived or dropped instead of threaded** — across every other tricky Tcl surface: strings/escapes/`subst`, lists/dicts/indices, `expr`, delimiter/CST re-scans, `$var`/name parsing, namespaces, traces/rename/alias/interps/shimmer, dialect threading, and the peripheral tooling (grammars, editors, AI prompts, explorer, iRules harness, pkg, fuzzer).

Found the same shape as the #1371/#1400 legacy-duplication audit; #1400 is now closed as superseded by this issue, and its 26 issues are folded into the sections below. **53 issues from this audit (#1420–#1472), one existing issue updated (#1382, comment linking its structural cause #1430), plus 26 more folded in from #1400 (#1374–#1399).** Every finding cites `file:line` on both sides and was read-verified at filing time; cross-engine claims marked as probed were run against tclsh 8.6.16 / 9.0.4.

## Cross-engine semantics (tcl-vm ↔ runtime/rust ↔ tclsh)

| Issue | Defect |
|---|---|
| #1427 | VM `dict` never collapses duplicate keys — two local `dict_pairs`; opcode vs command path disagree inside one engine |
| #1429 | runtime dict `FindElement` re-port drops backslash-newline — `llength` and `dict size` disagree on one value |
| #1443 | `subst` option matching hand-rolled twice — empty option word: `ambiguous` vs `bad` |

| #1432 | `rand()` transcribed twice; scaling differs by one ulp on dense seed families |
| #1438 | VM un-stores a write when a write trace errors — contract, C, and runtime/rust keep it |
| #1440 | trace firing order re-derived per engine per kind — three observable orderings |
| #1444 | legacy `trace variable` letter-ops: permissive VM copy, absent in runtime, correctly gated only in the registry |
| #1447 | `TclPreventAliasLoop` absent from runtime/rust — alias cycle recurses to native stack exhaustion |
| #1452 | `tcl_platform` base table hand-listed per engine — `machine`/`user`/`osVersion` differ |
| #1442 | `namespace origin` returns the caller's qualification; `which -variable` answers with proc locals |
| #1446 | `namespace export -clear` never clears in the VM; leading-flag rule encoded three ways |
| #1448 | VM qualified **variable** names not colon-run canonical — `set ::a:::b` mints a second variable |

| #1453 | ensemble resolution + `ensemble create` option table hand-rolled twice, diverging from C |

| #1464 | both engines pre-provide `Tcl` at literal 9.0.4 regardless of the threaded release |
| #1382 | `entier`/`int`/`wide` diverge between tcl-vm and runtime/rust on out-of-range floats |
| #1383 | `file` is a partial port in runtime/rust — 17 of 31 registry subcommands unimplemented |
| #1384 | `format` is reimplemented from scratch in runtime/rust instead of the shared `tcl_cmd_core::format` |

## Compiler correctness

| #1433 | SCCP double-strips braces off already-segmented `foreach` lists — corrupt constant sets |
| #1431 | lowering's `parse_param_names` (8 sites) mis-splits `{a b}` / `a\ b` — wrong recorded arity |
| #1435 | compiled `expr` path resolves neither dialect fact: `parse_expr(…, None)` + no operator version gate |
| #1437 | `!($x<$y)`→`$x>=$y` and `$x==$x`→1 unsound on NaN; `inverse()` table hand-copied ×4 |
| #1424 | O129's rewrite span from a quote scanner blind to embedded `[…]` — a corrupting auto-fix |

## Analyser / LSP feature layer

| Issue | Defect |
|---|---|
| #1436 | W230/W231/W232 local index grammar accepts `end - 2`, misses `1+1`/`0x2` |
| #1434 | `regexp -start` local parser — bogus spec silently means 0, and it const-folds |

| #1391 | W231/W201 byte-scan raw source instead of the segmenter/registry/taint lattice already in the same file — false-positive/negative `lset` bounds checks and W201 firing despite a real normalising sanitiser |

## Dialect threading

| Issue | Defect |
|---|---|
| #1461 | **Headline:** no gate anywhere on the 9.0-first number grammar — `0d5`/`1_000`/leading-zero decimal at every emulated release |

| #1463 (**REOPENED — native VM residual only**) | Direct and runtime/rust final-identity availability gates are fixed; `Vm::take_command` still lets `rename` or `interp hide`/`expose` detach a release-hidden builtin and call it under Tcl 8.4 |
| #1465 | `FormatterConfig` dialect split across three independently-set fields — `f5 irule format` runs the Tcl 9 lexer |
| #1466 | bpf backend: private `parse_int` (`--5` accepted, `0o17`/`0d5`/`1_000` rejected) + unstamped registry profile |
| #1467 | fuzzer pins only the subject's release — reference, replay, and findings namespace unpinned |

## Generators and peripheral tooling

| #1472 | `when EVENT { }` boundaries re-parsed by five scanners, comment-blind, quote handling disagrees |
| #1445 | generated test descriptions leave `$`/`[` live — the generated script self-triggers substitution |

## Cleanup / drift gates

| Issue | Scope |
|---|---|
| #1439 | second byte-level `Tcl_ConvertElement` port in runtime/rust, disjoint parity tables, no gate |
| #1450 | `SAFE_INTERP_HIDDEN` triplicated — engine consts already miss `unload` |
| #1455 | `qualify`/`key_holder_and_tail` re-derived by lowerer/item-tree/symbols — outline placement disagrees |
| #1459 | two byte-identical wasm-codegen bare-var extractors |
| #1388 | wire `RepeatedArgLayout::optional_leading_word` to `upvar` and collapse the four hand-rolled scope-alias parsers |
| #1392 | dead and unwired optimiser machinery: an unreachable second purity oracle in gvn.rs, and an unpopulated `cross_event_vars` |
| #1393 | harden the lowerer as a span producer: adopt the #1325 body-rebase guard and drop the dialect-blind tokeniser |

| #1395 | shared `first_positional_index` option-skip primitive: five hand-rolled copies, one hardcoded |
| #1396 | restore the audit↔registry drift guard: the gap it found was fixed, the guard that found it was not |
| #1397 | `Diagnostic` builder: ~130 hand-written five-field literals across the analyser |
| #1398 | replace `UnknownWorld` for procedure bodies with the workspace/package/sourced-file entry points |
| #1399 | the benchmark harness (`bench.py`) hangs intermittently with no outer deadline |

## What the audit says beyond the individual findings

**1. Contract rule 5's gate was never built.** The shared grammars are 9.0-first *by design* with "dialect gating is a lexer/analyser concern" — and no such gate exists (#1461). Centralising the numeral grammar in #1419 is what made that gate load-bearing: every consumer that adopted the shared parser silently became 9.0. The same theme recurs one layer up at #1457, #1462, #1463, and #1435 — the dialect is modelled once (`DialectProfile` is genuinely clean) but the projections onto grammar, command surface, and codegen were never wired.

**2. runtime/rust is systematically the unmigrated side.** The #1383/#1384 pattern (a shared fix that never reached the runtime port) reproduces at #1429, #1439, #1425, #1428, #1430, #1444, #1447. The `command-backing` gate checks *presence*, not fidelity — a per-utility parity gate (or deriving the runtime from the shared cores) is the structural fix.

**3. The differential fuzzer cannot reach most of this.** Its word corpus contains no brace, backslash, quote, or duplicate key (list/dict codec divergences unreachable), the release pin is one-sided (#1467), and `rand` is unseeded. A corpus/knob pass would turn this audit's divergence classes into fuzz-reachable regressions.

**4. Everything that *generates* Tcl skips the one quoting owner.** `tcl_syntax::list::list_element` exists precisely for "embed arbitrary text as one Tcl word", and the generators (#1445, #1471) concatenate instead.

**5. Doc comments asserting guarantees were again a signal to check, not evidence** (as #1400 noted): `rename-alias.md` §4.2's termination claim, `cmd_trace.rs`'s rollback doc, and `bignum.rs`'s `0 ** negative` doc are each contradicted by C or by the contract they cite.

## Updated existing issues

- #1382 — comment added linking the structural cause (#1430: `mathfunc::Num`'s missing bignum rung + the VM's separate table), which explains why that symptom family keeps recurring.

## Folded in from #1400

#1400 ("Tracking: legacy duplication and half-completed migration audit", follow-on from #1371) is closed as superseded by this issue — its 26 issues are reorganised into the sections above. Preserving its own cross-cutting observations and verified-clean list here, since they don't belong to any single issue:

**What #1400's audit found beyond its individual issues:**

1. Nothing detects an unmigrated consumer — every finding was a human-directed read, not a gate. An architecture test in the shape of #1371's own (scanning production regions against every registered command name), generalised, would have caught #1381, #1390, and parts of #1380 mechanically.
2. Three findings were contradicted by their own doc comments: #1379's `param_traits.rs:938` ("the one description" of `upvar`'s shape), #1378's `switch_arm_bodies` ("can never disagree" with its migrated twin), #1376's `codegen/structured.rs:50` ("no caller yet", while a panic backtrace shows the caller). A doc comment asserting uniqueness is a signal to check, not evidence.
3. Gate holes cluster: #1383 (presence-not-completeness), #1394 (no gate at all), #1396 (guard never landed) are one theme — the drift gates cover generated artefacts well and hand-written duplication not at all.
4. Stale "not wired up yet" comments keep dead-by-belief code alive. #1391's `path_concat` is the clearest case — a text matcher survives *because* a comment says the registry path doesn't work, and it has worked for some time.

**Verified clean:** the segmenter's completed CST migration, `oo_body.rs`'s command-name-free `MemberKind` walker, the shared `tcl_cmd_core` command families, and the LSP feature-toggle contract.

**Method:** six parallel agents, each required to cite `file:line` on both sides of a duplication and verify by reading rather than suspicion; four of six additionally reproduced their findings against a locally built `tcl`. Full working notes are at `docs/audits/legacy-duplication-2026-08/` (added in #1401; per its README, delete the directory once every issue above is closed).

## Verified clean (highlights)

Exactly one `expr` Pratt parser/AST/eval walk with three thin adopters; `scan`, `binary`, `switch`, and glob are clean single-owner stacks across both engines; command resolution is conformance-pinned in three layers (naming → compiler → VM) with runtime/rust gated by the shared vector table; the minifier and explorer thread dialect correctly; the package version comparator is a single oracle-pinned port; W129/W003 are registry-derived; bpf's `/`-`%` truncation divergence is a documented contract (#1202). Full per-subsystem clean lists are recorded in the individual issues' audit reports.

## Method note

Nine domain research agents (strings/escapes, lists/indices, expr, delimiters, varsubst/names, namespaces, dynamic semantics, dialect threading, peripheral surfaces) followed by five filing agents. Every finding required `file:line` on both sides of a duplication, verified by reading rather than suspicion; namespace/varsubst/trace claims were additionally probed against tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4. Agents were briefed on the documented carve-outs — the shared-utility contract's deliberate exceptions, the lowering fallback-to-generic-call pattern, and the analyser-local OO semantics — and declined to report them. At filing time each issue's load-bearing evidence was re-read against the tree; a handful of line-number drifts were corrected silently and one evidence mis-citation (a dialect-set constant) was corrected in the issue body.

issues.title: Under 8.4/iRules grammars, `set {*}$n 1` lowers to `AssignConst { name: "*${n}" }` — a computed name modelled as a static assignment, invisible to the dynamic-name barrier
issues.body:
Found while fixing #1393 (PR #1481, commit 1adcd5f4), deliberately left out of that change as out of scope. Same soundness family as #1374.

## The bug

With `expand_syntax` off (tcl8.4 / f5-irules grammars), `{*}` is a literal word prefix, so `set {*}$n 1` is `set` with the name word `{*}$n`. The lowerer models this as `AssignConst { name: "*${n}" }` — a *static* assignment to a literally-spelled name — even though the name text contains a `$` substitution. `dynamic_names::scan_statement` never inspects `AssignConst` names (by contract they are static), so the dynamic-name barrier does not rise, and the value-motion passes (gated on that barrier since #1374/1adcd5f4) may treat the frame's variables as unaffected.

The barrier scan itself is now dialect-correct (1adcd5f4's `an_84_expansionless_name_word_is_still_a_dynamic_write` pins the bracketed form `[set {*}{$n} 1]`, which stays on the Call path and is caught); this issue is specifically the lowering shape for the plain-statement form: a name word containing substitutions must not become `AssignConst`.

## Cleanup

In the lowerer's `set` handling, gate the `AssignConst` specialisation on the name word being a substitution-free literal (the same `seg_word_is_static_literal` predicate family used for body words since #1375); a substituting name word should stay a generic `Call` so `scan_command` sees it. Add the 8.4/iRules vectors to `dynamic_names`' dialect tests.

**Scale:** small — one gate at the `set` lowering site plus vectors.

issues.title: runtime/rust: a missing alias target errors directly instead of consulting `unknown`
issues.body:
Found while oracling the #1463 dispatch-gate fix (PR #1481 review sweep).

In real tclsh, invoking an alias whose target does not exist routes the *target* through the `unknown` machinery:

```tcl
proc unknown {args} { return "UNKNOWN:$args" }
interp alias {} la {} nosuchcmd
puts [la a b]
```

tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4 both print `UNKNOWN:nosuchcmd a b` (and without a custom `unknown` the error is `invalid command name "nosuchcmd"` — the target name, not the alias name). `runtime/rust`'s `dispatch_alias` errors directly from the alias dispatch without consulting `unknown`, so the custom-`unknown` case diverges.

The error-identity half is already right (target name, pinned by the #1463 tests); only the `unknown` fall-through is missing. Note the release-availability gate from 9393ce58 makes a release-hidden builtin take exactly this missing-target path, so fixing this also gives hidden-builtin-via-alias correct `unknown` semantics for free.

issues.title: `tcl_cmd_core::namespace::qualifiers` loses the absolute marker, so `namespace import ::globalcmd` can never import a global command
issues.body:
Found while writing regression tests for the #1463 dispatch-gate fix (PR #1481 review sweep).

```tcl
namespace eval n { namespace import ::lassign }
```

Real tclsh 8.6/9.0 import the global command fine. Both our runtimes fail with:

```
import pattern "::lassign" tries to import from namespace "n" into itself
```

Root cause: `tcl_cmd_core::namespace::qualifiers` (`rust/tcl-cmd-core/src/namespace.rs:62`) returns `""` for `"::lassign"`, losing the distinction between *no qualifier* and *the global namespace* — C Tcl's `TclGetNamespaceForQualName` treats a leading `::` as an absolute path rooted at the global namespace. `find_namespace(dest, "")` then resolves to the destination namespace itself and the self-import check fires.

Consequence beyond `namespace import`: any caller of `qualifiers` that distinguishes absolute from relative names inherits the same collapse. The #1463 import-dispatch regression test had to use `::tcl::mathop::+` instead of a global builtin to route around this.

issues.title: runtime/rust: missing-command error shapes for `rename X {}` and `interp hide` diverge from real tclsh
issues.body:
Found while oracling the #1463 dispatch-gate fix (PR #1481 review sweep). Two small divergences on the missing-command edge, both byte-checked against real tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4:

1. **`rename nosuchcmd {}`** — real Tcl distinguishes the delete spelling: `can't delete "nosuchcmd": command doesn't exist`. `runtime/rust` says `can't rename "nosuchcmd": command doesn't exist` for both spellings (`tclNamesp.c`'s `TclRenameCommand` picks the verb from whether the target is empty).
2. **`interp hide {} nosuchcmd`** — real Tcl errors `unknown command "nosuchcmd"`; `runtime/rust` is a silent no-op. The no-op is documented as deliberate in `cmd_alias.rs`, so this is a decision to revisit rather than an oversight — but it now also swallows a typo'd hide in a security-sensitive code path, which is worth weighing against whatever motivated the no-op.

Both matter for the byte-identical-vectors posture the alias/rename work (#1447, 9393ce58) otherwise holds to.

issues.title: Dynamic-name barrier fails open past depth 256, so O100 folds across a hidden computed write
issues.body:
## Context

Found while adversarially reviewing #1481, but the affected code predates that PR (`95a3760c3a`).

`scan_text` stops descending once `MAX_BRACKET_TEXT_DEPTH` is exceeded and returns without setting a conservative barrier. A dynamic variable write hidden below that depth is therefore invisible to the optimiser, even though the cap is only a native-stack safety limit. O100 can then fold a later read across the write and change the program result.

Affected code: `rust/tcl-compiler/src/dynamic_names.rs:574-580`.

## Reproduction

Build the `tcl` CLI, then run:

```bash
nested='[set $name 2]'
for i in $(seq 1 258); do nested="[list $nested]"; done
src="proc f {name} { set x 1; set sink $nested; return \$x }"
target/debug/tcl opt --source "$src" --no-colour
```

The output ends with:

```tcl
return 1 }

# optimised: 1 rewrite(s)
# O100 Fold return of constant variable
```

To observe the semantic difference, execute the original and optimised forms with:

```tcl
puts [f x]
```

The original writes `x` through `$name` and returns `2`; the optimised form returns `1`.

## Expected

Hitting a traversal safety cap must fail closed for a soundness fact: mark the scope/script as having a dynamic-name barrier (or otherwise suppress the dependent rewrite). It must not mean that no barrier exists.

## Actual

The depth-limit return leaves the barrier unset, allowing O100 to fold across an unobserved computed write.

issues.title: Neither engine fires `array` variable traces: `trace add variable arr array cb` never invokes the callback
issues.body:
Found during the #1440 fix lane's oracle work (not part of that lane's three issues).

Repro at HEAD `5a035d208`:

```tcl
array set arr {k 1}
trace add variable arr array cb
proc cb {n1 n2 op} { puts "A:$op" }
array names arr
```

tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4 fire the callback (the lane's probe printed two firings); **neither tcl-vm nor runtime/rust fires anything** — the `array` trace kind is accepted at registration but never dispatched.

Governing C: `TCL_TRACE_ARRAY` is fired from `Tcl_ArrayObjCmd`'s subcommand paths via `TclObjCallVarTraces` with `TCL_TRACE_ARRAY` (see `tcl8.6.16 generic/tclVar.c` / `tclArrayObjCmd`); the firing-order machinery both engines just gained (#1440) handles the kind correctly once dispatched, so the residual work is the dispatch sites in each engine's `array` command implementation.

issues.title: Variable-trace re-entrancy suppression uses the whole array as its unit; C suppresses per Var cell
issues.body:
Found during the trace lane's adversarial pass (pre-existing; proven untouched by that lane's diff — the guard lines changed only in indentation).

Both engines suppress trace re-entrancy per whole array; C's `TclCallVarTraces` sets `VAR_TRACE_ACTIVE` on the specific `Var` cell, so a whole-array write trace whose callback writes a **different** element fires again.

Repro at `claude/e3-traces` head (same at base):

```tcl
proc W {n1 n2 op} { set ::c(other) 1 }
trace add variable c write W
set c(k) 1
```

tclsh 8.6.16/9.0.4 fire for `c(k)` and then for `c(other)` (two firings); both engines fire once. Same divergence element→element. Note the VM's own comment documents the whole-variable unit as intentional — the comment needs correcting along with the code. C: `tcl8.6.16 generic/tclVar.c` `TclCallVarTraces`, `VAR_TRACE_ACTIVE` on the per-cell `Var`.

issues.title: Unset-trace firing sites are incomplete: proc-frame teardown (runtime/rust), namespace teardown (tcl-vm), and per-element firing on whole-array unset (both)
issues.body:
Found during the trace lane's adversarial pass (all pre-existing; that lane fixed the *ordering* of the sites that do fire, these are sites that don't fire at all). Three mirror-image gaps:

1. **runtime/rust fires no unset traces at proc-frame teardown.** A local with an unset trace, on proc return: tclsh and tcl-vm fire (newest-first); runtime/rust fires nothing.
2. **tcl-vm fires no unset traces at namespace teardown.** `namespace delete` on a namespace variable carrying unset traces: tclsh and runtime/rust fire (runtime's ordering fixed on `claude/e3-traces`); the VM fires nothing.
3. **Neither engine fires per-element unset traces when a whole array is unset.** With an unset trace on the array and on elements `j`/`k`, `unset arr` on tclsh yields the whole-array firing **plus one per element** (`arr {} unset`, `arr j unset`, `arr k unset`); both engines stop after the whole-array firing. C: `TclDeleteArrayVar`/`DeleteArray` walks elements and calls traces per cell.

Ordering for whichever sites get added is already owned by the (post-#1440) firing machinery — these are dispatch-site gaps, not ordering bugs. Note the order *across* a namespace's variables during teardown is C's hash walk and deliberately unpinned.

issues.title: runtime/rust: lassign/catch/regexp/scan/binary scan/foreach write array-element variable names as literal scalars
issues.body: Found by the E4 adversary pass (pre-existing, untouched by that lane's diff). Commands that write to caller-named variables treat `arr(a)` as a literal scalar name instead of an array element: `lassign {p q} arr(a) arr(b)` → `array get arr` is empty on runtime/rust (tclsh 8.6.16/9.0.4: `a p b q`). Reproduced for `lassign`, `catch` (message/options vars), `regexp` match vars, `scan`, `binary scan`, and `foreach` loop vars. Not specific to the zero-length-array-name case (#1458); these sites bypass element resolution entirely. C routes all of these through `TclObjLookupVarEx`/`Tcl_ObjSetVar2`, which parse the element form.

issues.title: tclvm: `array set (x)` / `array set arr(k)` succeed, creating an array literally named "(x)"/"arr(k)"
issues.body: Found by the E4 adversary pass (pre-existing). `array set (x) {a 1}` and `array set arr(k) {a 1}` succeed on tclvm, creating arrays literally named `(x)`/`arr(k)`; tclsh 8.6.16/9.0.4 and runtime/rust error `can't set "(x)": variable isn't array`. Not specific to the zero-length spelling — the `array set` target name is not element-parsed at all. C: `Tcl_ArrayObjCmd`'s set path resolves the target via the standard lookup and rejects an element-form name.

issues.title: tclvm: `upvar` linking a proc local to a namespace variable is silently accepted — C raises "can't create namespace variable that refers to procedure variable"
issues.body:
Found during the #1458 companion-guard work (pre-existing, deliberately left out of that fix so it gets a correct message rather than a wrong one).

Repro: inside a proc, `upvar 0 zz ::x::l(k)` (or any qualified namespace-variable target from a proc-local link in the offending direction) — tclsh 8.6.16/9.0.4 raise `can't create namespace variable that refers to procedure variable`; tclvm returns OK and creates the link. C: `Tcl_UpVar2`/`ObjMakeUpvar` (`tclVar.c`, the `MakeUpvar` guard rejecting a namespace-variable link to a procedure variable).

The new element-name guards on `upvar`/`global`/`variable` (E4 branch) are scoped to unqualified locals precisely so this case isn't half-handled with the wrong message; this issue tracks implementing C's actual check.

issues.title: Ensemble protocol gaps vs C: `-unknown` result must re-dispatch as a command prefix; `-map` values unvalidated; missing-target error text unrooted
issues.body:
Grouped pre-existing findings from the E2 adversary pass (all proven untouched by the E2 diff; the ensemble *tables and resolution* are fixed there — these are deeper protocol gaps):

1. **`-unknown` handler protocol**: C treats the handler's result as a replacement command prefix and re-dispatches (`tclEnsemble.c`, unknown-handler path); both engines return the handler result as the ensemble's result. `::se5 nope 1 2` → tclsh `invalid command name "UNK:::se5"`; both engines `UNK:::se5 nope 1 2`.
2. **`-map` value validation**: tclsh rejects an odd map (`missing value to go with key`), an empty target (`ensemble subcommand implementations must be non-empty lists`), and a malformed dict (`unmatched open brace in dict`); both engines silently accept the first two and give the list-noun error for the third.
3. **Missing ensemble target error**: tclsh reports the ensemble-rewrite name (`invalid command name "ghost"`); the VM reports an unrooted qualified name (`"k1::ghost"`), the runtime a rooted one (`"::k1::ghost"`).

issues.title: VM namespace-surface validation gaps: declared-unset variables invisible, `namespace which` skips option/arity checks, import self/unknown-source checks missing, `namespace delete ::` errors
issues.body:
Grouped pre-existing findings from the E2 adversary pass (proven untouched by the E2 diff):

1. **Declared-unset namespace variables have no storage**: after `namespace eval n2 {variable declared_only}`, `namespace which -variable` and `info vars` both miss it on the VM (tclsh and runtime/rust: `::n2::declared_only`). Store gap, not a `which` gap — the shared `which_variable` core is correct once a cell exists. Cross-engine split: runtime models it (`state_traits.rs:432`).
2. **`namespace which` does no option/arity validation**: `namespace which -zork puts` → `::puts` (tclsh: error), `namespace which -command puts extra` → `{}` (tclsh: `wrong # args`).
3. **`namespace import` lacks C's self-import and unknown-source checks** (`import pattern "…" tries to import from namespace "…" into itself` / `unknown namespace in import pattern "…"`) — VM silently succeeds; runtime has both.
4. **`namespace delete ::`** errors `unknown namespace "::"` on the VM; tclsh accepts it (tears down the global namespace).

issues.title: Constant-folding family folds by dialect only: a renamed, deleted, or proc-shadowed `dict`/`list`/`format` still gets the compile-time fold
issues.body:
Recorded from the E4 adversary pass. The new dialect gate on `fold_dict_create_cmd` (post-#1427) correctly answers "does this dialect have `dict`", but no fold in the family answers "is `dict` still the builtin at this call site": after `rename dict {}` or a shadowing `proc dict …`, the fold still runs and returns the builtin's answer where tclsh raises `invalid command name "dict"` / calls the shadow. Identical pre-existing hole in the untouched `list` and `format` folds (`rename list mylist; list a 1 a 2` → tclvm `a 1 a 2`; tclsh errors via unknown) — a property of the whole constant-folding family, not of any one fold.

Fix direction: folds need a conservative bail when the command's global binding could have been touched (rename/proc/interp hide of the name anywhere in the unit is the cheap static approximation), or a runtime identity check on the folded path.

issues.title: tclvm has no "parent namespace doesn't exist" check: qualified variable/global/upvar names with missing namespaces silently succeed or get the wrong error
issues.body:
Isolated during the #1458 companion-guard verification (pre-existing; the guard work moved adjacent rows toward C but this check is its own feature). C's variable lookup errors `parent namespace doesn't exist` when a qualified name's namespace path can't resolve (`TclObjLookupVarEx` → `TclGetNamespaceForQualName` failure path); the VM never performs it:

- `variable a::b(c)` / `global a::b(c)` (no namespace `a`): tclsh errors `can't define/set "a::b(c)": parent namespace doesn't exist`; the VM reports the element-name message instead (error class right, message wrong).
- `variable v(a)::b` and `variable v(a::b)c` (not element-shaped, bad qualifier path): tclsh errors; the VM returns ok.
- Bare `variable a::b 1` / `global a::b` with no namespace `a`: both silently succeed on the VM at base.

Related deliberate carve-out: #1582 (`upvar` to a qualified namespace variable needs C's `can't create namespace variable that refers to procedure variable`).

issues.title: tclvm: destroying a TclOO object reached via `rename` leaves the command listed in `info commands`
issues.body:
Found during the namespace-lane adversary vectors (pre-existing — byte-identical with that lane's diff stashed; reproduces at `--tcl-version 9.0` with ordinary names, no availability gating involved):

```tcl
oo::object create ::a
rename ::a ::b
::b destroy
info commands ::b     ;# tclvm: ::b     tclsh 9.0.4: {}
```

The rename leaves a stale entry that destroy doesn't reap — likely the object's teardown removes the command under its original registration key rather than the current name. (Separate from the VM's complete lack of `oo::copy`, noted in the same pass.)

issues.title: tclvm: variable names beginning with `{` are broken at every release: `set {{a}} V; info exists {{a}}` → 0; braced-name `upvar` executes the proc body twice
issues.body:
Two related pre-existing VM defects found by the #1568 adversary (both oracle-diffed against tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4; neither attributable to any open branch):

1. **Leading-`{` names**: `set {{a}} V; puts [info exists {{a}}]` → tclvm `0` at all five releases (both oracles: `1`). Consequently `puts ${{}}`-style direct loads and `$arr(${{}})` keys diverge, and the compile-time decline-to-runtime fallback is not equivalent to a direct load for such names (this is what falsified a "declining is always safe" assumption on the w2 branch).

2. **Braced-name `upvar` double-execution**: `proc p {} { upvar 1 {a b} v ; puts "u=$v" }; p` executes the body **twice** on tclvm (output printed twice; oracle once). No `${…}` involved — the trigger is the braced multi-word variable name in the upvar argument position. Double execution of a body is side-effect-duplicating and deserves priority within this pair.

issues.title: compiler: ~20 free-text `${…}` scanners hard-code the 8.x first-`}` rule (and ~15 more use a last-`}` rule) across optimiser/dataflow/taint/analyser — #1568's class, outside its declared scope
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of the `braced_var_name_end` owner (PR #1591 review sweep, verified at `claude/e4-codecs-subst` d5c369ec1 + diffed against `claude/w2-braced-var-1568`).

#1568 fixes the compiled-word round-trip (`segmenter.rs::word_piece`, `codegen/values.rs::parse_simple_var_ref`, `codegen/helpers.rs::parse_subst_template`, `vm/subst.rs::subst_word`). This issue covers the rest of the class: free-text `${…}` name scanners in the compiler that re-derive the close position from raw text instead of calling the release-aware owner `tcl_lexer::ranges::braced_var_name_end`.

**Rule divergence (oracles):** `set {a{b}c} HIT; subst {${a{b}c}}` → `HIT` on 9.0.4, `can't read "a{b"` on 8.6.16. Governing C: `Tcl_ParseVarName` — `tmp/tcl9.0.4/generic/tclParse.c:1315` (brace depth + `\X` pairs) vs `tmp/tcl8.6.16/generic/tclParse.c:1398` (first `}`). Default `BracedVarStyle` is `Tcl9Nesting` (`tcl-dialect/src/grammar.rs:463`), so on a default document the lexer spans `${a{b}c}` as one `Var` while each site below re-derives `a{b` from the same bytes — an in-process contradiction, not merely a cross-release one.

**First-`}` (`find('}')`) scanners:**

*tcl-syntax (already depends on tcl-lexer):*
- `rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs:486` `element_var_name_braced`
- `rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs:1044` `split_array_name`

*compiler optimiser/dataflow — a missed use is a wrong transform:*
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/elimination.rs:857` — variable-use harvest → false W211 / dead-store elimination of a live write
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/code_sinking.rs:720` — `uses_var` → sinks a statement past a real use
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/propagation.rs:2878`
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/gvn.rs:263`
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/dynamic_names.rs:297`
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/taint.rs:656`, `:1766` — taint tracks the wrong name (security diagnostics)
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/subst_nocommands.rs:91` (fails safe: declines)
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/text.rs:256`

*analyser:*
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/param_traits.rs:532` (`extract_var_name`), `:857`
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:376` (`substitute_bound_words`), `:692`
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs:2461` (`parse_namespaced_ensemble`; fails safe)

**Last-`}` strippers on free IR text** (`strip_prefix("${")…strip_suffix('}')` — the *opposite* wrong answer, the same inversion #1568's title describes): `sccp.rs:1417,1655`, `value_shapes.rs:146,162`, `static_loops.rs:147`, `path_concat.rs:91`, `interprocedural.rs`, `var_escape/state.rs:251`, `var_escape/cfg_propagation/state.rs:301`, `specialise_factories.rs:236`, `structure_elimination.rs:421`, `lowering/mod.rs:1207`, `lowering/structured.rs:179`, among others. Note: the same pattern applied to a *lexer word span* (e.g. `lsp-core/rename.rs:1996`) is correct by construction and out of scope here.

**Fix shape:** thread the resolved `BracedVarStyle` (most of these layers already carry `LexerConfig` or dialect) and locate the closer via `braced_var_name_end`; where text originates from the segmenter's normalised spelling, prefer consuming the lexer's span instead of re-scanning. Mutation-verify per AGENTS.md. Also see the contract scope-note correction landing in #1591 (`docs/design/contracts/shared-utility-contracts-rust.md:137-139` currently under-claims this gap).

Related: #1568 (compiled-word path), #1457 (subst engines, fixed), #1601 (expr_lexer's sixth scan). The lsp-core refactor/minify sites are filed separately — they produce broken user-visible edits.

issues.title: lsp-core: extract_proc/inline_proc `variable_references` and minify re-derive `${…}` names with a release-blind first-`}` scan — refactors can emit broken code
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of the `braced_var_name_end` owner (PR #1591 review sweep, verified at `claude/e4-codecs-subst` d5c369ec1). Split out from the compiler-internal sweep because these four sites are **user-facing**: a wrong variable-name parse here changes the text of a refactoring edit or minified output, not just an internal fact.
