**Sites (all hard-code the 8.x first-`}` rule at every release):**
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/refactor/extract_proc.rs:586` (`variable_references`) — a wrong captured-variable set produces a generated proc with wrong params/args
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/refactor/inline_proc.rs:575` (`variable_references`) — same class on the inline direction
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/minify.rs:2589` (`parse_var_ref`)
- `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/minify.rs:2971` (`strip_braced_var_refs`)

**Divergence rule** (oracle-verified): `${a{b}c}` is one variable named `a{b}c` under 9.x (`Tcl_ParseVarName`, `tmp/tcl9.0.4/generic/tclParse.c:1315` — brace depth, `\X` inert pairs) but ends at the first `}` under 8.x (`tmp/tcl8.6.16/generic/tclParse.c:1398`). On a Tcl-9 document (`BracedVarStyle::Tcl9Nesting`, the default) the lexer spans the whole `${a{b}c}`, while these sites re-derive `a{b` from the same bytes.

**Concrete failure:** extract-proc over a selection containing `puts ${a{b}c}` on a 9.x document computes the captured set from the truncated name `a{b`, so the generated proc's parameter list and call-site argument list are built for a variable that does not exist, while the real `a{b}c` reference in the moved body goes un-rewritten. Minify's `strip_braced_var_refs` can likewise change program meaning by rewriting the wrong span.

**Fix shape:** route through `tcl_lexer::ranges::braced_var_name_end` (re-exported as `tcl_lexer::braced_var_name_end`) with the document's resolved `BracedVarStyle` — lsp-core already resolves dialect per document — or better, consume the lexer's `Var` token spans instead of re-scanning text. Add refactor tests with a brace-bearing name on both a 9.x and an 8.x document; mutation-verify the style plumb (flip the style, show a named test fails).

Related: #1568 (compiled-word path), #1457 (subst engines, fixed), and the compiler-internal sweep filed alongside this issue.

issues.title: compiler: element-ref split predicates duplicated beside the `split_element_ref` owner (values.rs `split_array_ref`/`is_array_ref`, var_command.rs `is_array_elem`, naming.rs `split_array_name_braced`)
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of PR #1591's owners (verified at `claude/e4-codecs-subst` d5c369ec1). Drift-risk cleanup, **no observable divergence today**: `ends_with(')') && contains('(')` is logically identical to the owner's rule (one byte cannot satisfy both char tests), so these cannot diverge on any input — until one side changes.

#1591 established `tcl_syntax::naming::split_element_ref{,_bytes}` as the owner for the `name(index)` element split (governing C: `TclObjLookupVarEx`, `tmp/tcl9.0.4/generic/tclVar.c:594`, parse at `:683-686` — zero-length array name accepted). Remaining duplicates outside that PR's routing:

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/values.rs:141` `split_array_ref` / `:152` `is_array_ref` — a full re-implementation of the split. The contract's exceptions list names `values.rs::is_bare_var_name` but not these.
- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs:2630` `is_array_elem`
- `rust/tcl-syntax/src/naming.rs:537` `split_array_name_braced` — re-derives the split inline **inside the owner's own file** rather than calling `split_element_ref`.

(The two VM copies the audit also found — `tcl-vm/src/command.rs:1456` and `tcl-vm/src/exec.rs:2254` — are being routed in-PR on #1591 since that PR already edits those files.)

**Deliberately out of scope** (correctly distinct, do not conflate): `sccp.rs:978 array_element_base` is a narrower fold-safety predicate with a rationale comment, and it correctly excludes the zero-length array name the owner admits.

**Fix shape:** route each through `split_element_ref` (or `_bytes`), delete the local copies, add the sites to the owner's consumer list in `docs/design/contracts/shared-utility-contracts-rust.md`, and mutation-verify (perturb the owner's guard, show a consumer test fails). Note `cargo xtask owner-resolution` validates the manifest only — it cannot detect a consumer that never calls the owner, which is why these survived.

Related: #1458 (the guard defect that motivated the owner), #1591.

issues.title: registry: `ENSEMBLE_CREATE_OPTIONS` serves both `namespace ensemble create` and `configure`, but the real option sets differ — completion offers a guaranteed error and hides a valid option
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of PR #1592's owners (verified at `claude/e2-namespaces` 1b78b7605). Pre-dates that branch (`namespace_.rs` last touched 129439e47, 2026-08-16), but #1592 is what establishes that the two option tables differ — the engines now carry them split via `tcl_cmd_core::ensemble` while the registry keeps one merged table.

**Site:** `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs:69` (`ENSEMBLE_CREATE_OPTIONS`), used for **both** subcommands at `:749`. Consumers: `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/completion.rs:317-323`, `hover.rs:1360`, `analyser/diagnostics/validity.rs:3617`. The doc comment ("`-namespace` is deliberately excluded … rejected by `apply_ensemble_option`'s `_` arm") reasons from the *old runtime code* — exactly the drift #1592 removed.

**tclsh-pinned ground truth (identical 8.6.16 / 9.0.4):**
```
namespace ensemble configure ::E -namespace  → ::M          (valid read)
namespace ensemble configure ::E -command x  → bad option "-command": must be -map, -namespace, -parameters, -prefixes, -subcommands, or -unknown
namespace ensemble create -namespace ::M     → bad option "-namespace": must be -command, -map, -parameters, -prefixes, -subcommands, or -unknown
```

**Observable today:** `namespace ensemble configure $e -⟨tab⟩` offers `-command` (a guaranteed runtime error) and never offers `-namespace` (valid, and a real Tk-library idiom); hover on `-namespace` is silent. No false diagnostic — W004 only fires for options *in* the table.

**Gate gap:** the manifest row's `xtask-option-registry-drift` cannot catch this — it only checks that probed options exist in the registry, and `namespace ensemble` is not in its probe table. Add it when splitting.

**Fix shape:** registry-data change — split into `ENSEMBLE_CREATE_OPTIONS` / `ENSEMBLE_CONFIG_OPTIONS`, wire table selection to `sub_subcommands`, correct the doc comment, add `namespace ensemble` to the drift-gate probe table, and add completion/hover tests for both subcommands.

Related: #1592.

issues.title: lsp-core/analyser: user-ensemble subcommands resolved by exact match only — navigation abstains on abbreviated dispatch words
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of PR #1592's owners (verified at `claude/e2-namespaces` 1b78b7605). Pre-dates that branch. Soft failure only — navigation abstains, never answers wrongly.

**Sites:** `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:1801`; `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:2859,2897` — all `subs.get(sub)` exact lookups.

Real ensembles abbreviate: with `namespace ensemble create -map {foo ::e::Foo}` (default `-prefixes 1`), `e fo` dispatches to `::e::Foo`. Go-to-definition / references / rename on the abbreviated word find nothing. The analyser already records the `-prefixes 0` opt-out (`handlers.rs:3739` → `prefixless_ensembles`) but uses it only to abstain from W145 — it never feeds a prefix scan.

**Fix shape:** `tcl_cmd_core::ensemble::resolve_subcommand(subs, sub, prefixes)` (the owner #1592 established) is exactly the needed shape — call it from the three sites with the recorded `prefixes` flag, resolving only a *unique* prefix (ambiguous → keep abstaining). Tests: definition/rename on an abbreviated dispatch word, plus a `-prefixes 0` ensemble where abbreviation must NOT resolve; mutation-verify the prefixes flag plumb.

Related: #1592.

issues.title: analyser: `namespace export` records patterns past an invalid one — C aborts the loop at the first bad pattern
issues.body:
Found by an independent centralisation audit of PR #1592's owners (verified at `claude/e2-namespaces` 1b78b7605). Pre-dates that branch. Low priority — observable only in a script that carries a guaranteed runtime error anyway.

**Site:** `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:9247-9264`.

C's per-pattern-commit rule (the C4 semantics #1592 implemented in the engines): `namespace export ::bad ok` errors at the first pattern and exports **nothing** — the loop aborts before `ok` is processed. The analyser records both patterns, so a wildcard-import bareword `ok` elsewhere resolves where real Tcl would not.

Also noted: no diagnostic exists for a qualified export pattern (a guaranteed runtime error worth a warning), even though `rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/namespace_rename.rs:170` already knows the rule.

**Fix shape:** stop recording at the first invalid pattern in the analyser's export handler, mirroring the engines' C4 behaviour; optionally add a diagnostic for qualified export patterns. Small, self-contained.

Related: #1592.

issues.title: runtime: `namespace exists`/`parent`/`children` still take the lossy `&str` route — byte-valued machinery now exists, convert them
issues.body:
Split out of PR #1592's review round (thread: https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/pull/1592#discussion_r3812661830). Pre-dates that branch; deliberately left out of the round rather than widening it silently.

#1592 (commit 1d938d2e5) gave `Namespaces` byte-valued spellings (`find_command_bytes`, `find_namespace_bytes`, `namespace_var_exists_bytes`, `name_bytes`, `command_name_bytes`) with `from_utf8_lossy` default bodies — so the UTF-8-keyed VM needs no change — and the byte-native runtime overrides them, so `namespace which -variable`, `which -command`, and `namespace origin` (plus `oo_resolve_object`) now reach the `Vec<u8>`-keyed tables verbatim. `variable_fqn_bytes`/`origin_bytes`/`which_command_bytes` are the primary implementations in `tcl_cmd_core::namespace`.

**Remaining lossy paths:** the runtime's `namespace exists`, `namespace parent`, and `namespace children` still go through `String::from_utf8_lossy` before lookup.

**Reachability, stated precisely** (established in the #1592 round by mutation testing): this is *not* script-reachable — a byte array's string rep is one U+00XX per byte (`runtime/rust/src/bytearray.rs:86-99`), so `obj_bytes` always yields valid UTF-8 and the lossy hop is a no-op for any name a script constructs. The real input is the embedder-supplied non-UTF-8 plain string that `binary_bytes` documents (`bytearray.rs:125-129`) — there the lossy hop can collapse distinct names. Hardening, not a live bug.

**Fix shape:** route the three subcommands through the existing byte-valued entry points (add `_bytes` twins where the shared core lacks them), following the #1592 pattern exactly. Test with a genuinely non-UTF-8 name through the seam (the `byte_valued_command_names_resolve_without_a_utf8_round_trip` pattern — the surface-level `binary format` test cannot discriminate and must not be shipped as evidence). Mutation-verify.

Related: #1592.

issues.title: VM: quoted variable names in `set` are stored under their unsubstituted source spelling — `set "a\\" K` creates `a\\` (3 bytes) where tclsh creates `a\` (2 bytes)
issues.body:
Found on the #1615 review round while building the oracle vector for the switch-gate fix (Codex's exact spelling was blocked by this second, unrelated defect — the vector now sidesteps it via `format`, with a comment citing this issue).

**Defect:** the compiled path stores a quoted variable name without applying backslash substitution to the name. `set "a\\" K` creates a variable whose name is the source spelling `a\\` (3 bytes: `a`, `\`, `\`) instead of the substituted name `a\` (2 bytes).

**Evidence** (from `info vars a*` with byte lengths, tclvm at `claude/w2-braced-var-1568` head — pre-existing on base, not introduced by that branch):

| store spelling | tclvm name | tclsh 8.6 name |
|---|---|---|
| `set "a\\" K` (quoted literal) | `a\\` — len 3 | `a\` — len 2 |
| `set $n K` with `$n` = `[format a%c 92]` | `a\` — len 2 | `a\` — len 2 |

So the same variable name reaches the table as two different keys depending on how the script spells it; reads via one spelling miss writes via the other. tclsh substitutes the word before `set` ever sees it, so both spellings are the same 2-byte name.

**Root cause direction:** the compiled `set` path is receiving (or storing) the word's source text rather than its substituted value for the name operand — a word-evaluation defect on the store side, not a `${…}` close-rule issue (nothing to do with #1568/#1615; verified: the switch-gate fix did not change this).

**Fix shape:** find where the compiled `set` lowers a quoted-literal name operand and ensure backslash (and presumably other) substitutions are applied to the name word exactly as for any argument word. Oracle-verify the pair above at 8.6 and 9.0, plus `set "a\}" v` / `set "a\ b" v` shapes; mutation-verify.

issues.title: compiler: the `$={name}` internal marker's producer/consumer pair is release-blind by construction (mutation survivor M3b on #1615)
issues.body:
Recorded from the #1615 mutation inventory: mutant **M3b** (flipping the `$={name}` compiler-marker arm's close scan) survives the full test corpus, and survives identically on the pre-#1615 tree — pre-existing, not introduced there.

**Mechanism:** the `$={name}` escape-hatch marker (the compiler's internal spelling for a braced scalar reference) is produced and consumed by a pair that both use a release-blind rule (`strip_suffix('}')` on the consumer side; see also the #1568 handoff's note that `codegen/values.rs::parse_braced_scalar_ref` uses a *last*-`}` rule while `codegen/helpers.rs`'s `$={name}` arm inside `parse_subst_template` used `find('}')` — a third and fourth variant of the close rule). Because producer and consumer are blind in compatible ways, no current program distinguishes them — which is exactly why the mutant survives: **the seam is unpinned, and a future change to either half can diverge silently.**

This is a latent-inconsistency/drift-gate issue, not an observable bug today. It is distinct from #1604 (free-text scanners over user source): this pair operates on the compiler's own internal marker encoding.

**Fix shape:** either route both halves through one shared helper (so they cannot disagree), or — since the marker names are compiler-generated and could be constrained — document and enforce the invariant that marker names never contain `{`/`}`/`\`, and pin it with a test that a brace-bearing name is never emitted into the marker form. Then the mutant should die by name.

Related: #1568 / #1615 (the six user-visible decoder sites, fixed), #1604.

issues.title: Extension→dialect registration is only partially generator-driven: 6 drifted hand-maintained surfaces (.tmsh can't activate VS Code; .irules not indexed or recognised by f5-cli; Sublime per-dialect scopes wrong)
issues.body:
Whole-codebase audit at `origin/rust` (9934c7ab2) of every surface that maps file extensions to dialects/languages. The core is sound: `DialectProfile::file_extensions` (one-owner-per-extension invariants at `rust/tcl-dialect/src/profile.rs:2144-2174`), `cargo xtask gen-editor-extensions` (7 render targets), and a CI-wired drift gate (`Makefile:614` → `xtask-check` → ci.yml:234). All 7 generated files agree exactly on the 25-extension union, and every LSP/CLI detection path resolves through the catalogue with zero hardcoded extension arms.

**But the generator covers only 7 files, and the hand-maintained remainder has drifted in six places**, in impact order:

1. **VS Code `activationEvents`** (`editors/vscode/package.json:26-47`, explicitly hand-written per `gen_vscode_package.rs:492-493`): 16 of 19 language ids — missing `onLanguage:tcl-tmsh` and `onLanguage:tclspec`. Compounding: the generated `workspaceContains` glob (`package.json:46`) is built from `TCL_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS`, which excludes `tmsh` → **opening a lone `.tmsh` file never activates the extension.**
2. **`f5-cli`** (`rust/f5-cli/src/commands/irule.rs:90` `IRULE_SUFFIXES`, `:261`, `:1032`): all three lists omit `irules`, which the catalogue owns (`profile.rs:576-579`) — `foo.irules` is not recognised as a standalone iRule.
3. **Sublime per-dialect syntaxes** (ungated): `iRule.sublime-syntax:11-13` missing `irules`; `Expect.sublime-syntax:10-11` missing `expect`. Files open (the generated `Tcl.sublime-syntax` lists both) but with the wrong scope/highlighting. The 8 EDA/version syntaxes carry no `file_extensions` at all.
4. **`TCL_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS`** (`rust/tcl-registry/src/dialects.rs:353-358`): `irules` and `expect` are registered by every editor but not indexed — `is_tcl_source`, the watched-file glob, the rename filter, `workspaceContains`, and the CLI directory walk all skip them, so cross-file references/rename silently miss those files until opened. The doc rationale (`dialects.rs:349-352`) covers EDA suffixes but not these two; `tclspec` got an explicit rationale comment when added, these did not — drift, not intent.
5. **Two stale VS Code runtime switches** duplicating the generated `LANGUAGE_ID_DIALECTS`: `extension.ts:942-952` (6/19 extensions) and `highlightingHealth.ts:408-420` (4/19 — a `.sdc` file that lost its association is offered `tcl` instead of `tcl-synopsys`). `highlightingHealth.ts:60`'s `GENERIC_EXTENSIONS` is also hand-tuned and under-inclusive (`.do`/`.globals` collide with foreign files more than `.scf` does).
6. **The `filenames` axis has no catalogue field**: `BIGIP_CONF_NAMES` (`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/bigip.rs:52-58`) works server-side, but VS Code's `tcl-bigip` contributes no `filenames` (`package.json:90-99`) so `bigip.conf` never associates — and `BIG-IP.sublime-syntax:24-26`'s comment claiming VS Code matches those filenames is false. `tcl-apl`'s `filenames: ["presentation"]` is hand-maintained and matched nowhere else. `firstLine`/shebang: Sublime and Zed hardcode `tclsh|wish`; VS Code contributes none; the server's shebang tier (`dialects.rs:704-714`) handles `expect`/`tclsh` but not `wish`.

Docs drift (lower priority): Helix README missing `scf`/`test`; Emacs README 9/25; four identical stale 9-item lists in `INSTALL-editors.md:254/278/335/369`; `README.md:95-96`, `:1663-1664`; `editors/zed/README.md:45-48`. Zed's 5 secondary `languages/*/config.toml` are correct today but gated by nothing.

**Fix shape:** (a) extend `rust/xtask/src/editor_extensions.rs`'s render-target list to cover Zed's secondary configs, the Sublime per-dialect syntaxes, VS Code `activationEvents`, and `@generated:`-marked blocks in the Helix/Emacs/INSTALL docs; (b) delete the two dead VS Code switches in favour of the generated map; (c) add `irules`/`expect` to `TCL_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` (or document why not, like `tclspec`); (d) route `f5-cli`'s lists through the catalogue; (e) consider a `filenames` field on `DialectProfile` so `bigip.conf`/`presentation` routing has one owner; (f) decide whether the server's shebang tier should know `wish`.

issues.title: tclvm: command-mutation visibility gaps in fold gating — proc/eval unit boundaries and AssignExpr lowering
issues.body:
Follow-up from PR #1647 (#1585), which gated builtin folds and inline emission on the unit's command bindings via a per-unit scan (the static stand-in for C Tcl's INST_START_CMD epoch re-dispatch). Two visibility gaps were documented there and deliberately not fixed, per the release scope rule (vm/codegen-side, no .tclspec loading/execution impact):

1. Unit boundaries. The VM compiles each proc body and each eval'ed script as its own unit, so a `rename` in the enclosing file is invisible to the inner unit's scan. The top-level repro from #1585 is fixed; the same call inside a proc body still folds.

2. Lowering bypass. `set x [expr {...}]` is lowered to AssignExpr before codegen, so `rename expr` does not de-optimise that shape.

Both need mutation-visibility to cross a boundary the current per-unit scan cannot see — closer to a real epoch/invalidation mechanism than a wider text scan. Refs: #1585, #1647, and C Tcl's INST_START_CMD handling in tclExecute.c.

Triage: post-release per the standing rule.

issues.title: analyser: lift the two remaining abstention limits in clay's factory-prefix walk
issues.body:
Tracking issue from #1571 / PR #1652, which fixed two of the four abstention layers in `::clay::dialect::create`'s dominating prefix (bounded-iteration loop semantics; unreadable dormant body words) and documented the remaining two as genuine limits:

1. A conditional `return` inside `::clay::PROC` selected by the live command table — distinguishing early NORMAL completion from abnormal completion in the fall-through proof.
2. `eval $ninja` — the fall-through proof carries no interprocedural argument binding, so a script value supplied by the caller is unprovable.

The corpus-gated clay test now pins what IS proved and records this boundary in prose, deliberately not asserting the absence of a `::clay::class` factory — so lifting either limit reads as an improvement, not a test failure.

Both need a redesign of the abstaining fall-through analysis (interprocedural argument binding; completion-kind distinction). Refs: #1571, #1652, and the F4 lane's synthetic-reduction bisection methodology recorded in the PR body.

Triage: post-release — analyser redesign with the release-relevant test already honest.

issues.title: analyser: a metaclass proved only by the post-pass cannot classify a creation call in its own file
issues.body:
Found by lane F5v2 while fixing #1653 (PR #1659); verified identical before and after that branch's changes, so pre-existing and filed separately.

A metaclass whose identity is only proved by the post-pass (the parameterised-class observation join) cannot classify a creation call in its own file: the walk that classifies creation heads runs before the join settles, so a class created via that metaclass in the same document (`::T::W` in the reproducer) goes unrecorded — no factory, no members, no completion.

Fix direction: either a second classification pass over creation calls after the observation join settles, or deferring head classification for heads whose metaclass status is still open (the same deferred-verdict shape the arity work in #1642 used for floors).

Triage: pre-release — analyser correctness in the compiler front-end, same family as #1653/#1656.

issues.title: TclOO method references miss list/namespace-code callback prefixes in CommandPrefix slots
issues.body:
## Problem

#1701 covers a TclOO method callback constructed with [list [self] method] when the containing argument is a registry-declared Body. The same effective callback is still missed when it is supplied through a CommandPrefix slot, including the common namespace-code wrapper forms:

    after 0 [list [self] tick]
    fileevent $sock readable [namespace code [list my read]]
    socket -server [namespace code [list my connect]] $port
    trace add variable v write [namespace code [list [self] changed]]

This is a method-target extraction gap, not a generic callback gap. Ordinary proc heads and [namespace code [list Proc]] are already covered by #978 and the #1075 implementation (audit #923 idx 92).

## Corpus evidence

- tcllib 2.0 modules/virtchannel_base/cat.tcl lines 72 and 127: after $delay [namespace code [list my Post $c]].
- tcllib 2.0 modules/httpd/httpd.tcl lines 1011 and 1014: socket -server [namespace code [list my connect]]; line 1016: [namespace code {my CheckTimeout}].
- Tk audit #923 idx 92 and idx 93 in docs/design/issue-923-differential-audit/data/06-main-audit-results-COMPLETE-105of105.json.
- https://wiki.tcl-lang.org/page/callback
- https://wiki.tcl-lang.org/page/TclOO%3A%2Bcallback%2Bwith%2Binterface%2Bclass

## Acceptance criteria

- Find References, Rename, Code Lens, and Call Hierarchy agree for statically recoverable TclOO callback targets.
- Recognition is driven by registry facts: Body, CommandPrefix, BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX, and WRAPS_COMMAND_PREFIX, without command-name branches in LSP consumers.
- [self] method preserves external object-command/public-visibility semantics; my method preserves current-object/private-dispatch semantics.
- Dynamic receivers or method names, inert list data, and list values outside callback positions abstain without invented references or W123 diagnostics.
- Add Tcl 8.6 and Tcl 9.0 oracle-backed tests, including at least one tcllib-shaped fixture.

## Explicit exclusions and linkage

- #1701 is the Body-role regression being extended here; do not duplicate its exact bind-only fix.
- #978 is the existing CommandPrefix call-site substrate.
- #1075 fixed namespace-code/list wrapping for literal proc callbacks (audit #923 idx 92).
- #1322 and #1050 cover direct [self] and registry-driven my/next/nextto dispatch, respectively.
- Stored callback values and cross-file inherited-provider attribution are separate follow-ups and are intentionally not included here.

issues.title: Track one-hop stored TclOO callback prefixes through local constants
issues.body:
## Problem

After direct callback-prefix recognition is fixed, a separate bounded gap remains when the callback prefix is first stored in a local constant:

    set cb [list [self] tick]
    bind .w <Button-1> $cb

    set cb [namespace code [list my Post]]
    after 0 $cb

The callback value is statically recoverable in the simplest same-scope cases, but the current navigation model does not carry this command-prefix value into the later callback slot. This must remain conservative: dynamic command-prefix values are common and must not be guessed.

## Corpus evidence

- Tk audit #923 idx 93 in docs/design/issue-923-differential-audit/data/06-main-audit-results-COMPLETE-105of105.json records megawidget.tcl: set callback [list my $method {*}$args]; trace add ... [namespace code $callback]. It correctly treats the parameter-derived method as dynamic and abstains; that is the negative boundary for this issue.
- tcllib 2.0 modules/virtchannel_base/cat.tcl lines 72 and 127 show the direct non-stored namespace-code/list callback shape that motivates the preceding issue.
- Tcl Wiki callback guidance documents list-built object-method callbacks: https://wiki.tcl-lang.org/page/callback

## Acceptance criteria

- Find References, Rename, Code Lens, and Call Hierarchy include a stored callback only when the value is a single unambiguous same-scope constant built from a statically known callback target.
- Cover at least list [self] method, list my method, and namespace code list forms flowing through after, bind, trace, fileevent, or an equivalent registry-declared callback slot.
- Dynamic reassignment, parameter-derived method names, {*} expansion, command substitutions, cross-frame storage, and ambiguous merges abstain without invented references, W123 diagnostics, or unsafe rename edits.
- Use the same registry-driven callback-slot and command-prefix facts as #1703; do not add command-name branches to consumers.
- Add negative tests for the Tk megawidget-style set callback/list my $method/{*}$args shape.

## Explicit exclusions and linkage

- #1701 and #1703 cover direct callback-prefix extraction; this issue is only the bounded local value-flow extension.
- #978 and #1075 cover ordinary proc command-prefix callbacks, including namespace code list Proc.
- #994 and #1099 cover object-type/instance flow and cross-document object handoff; this issue does not attempt general object inference.
- Fully dynamic callback strings and interprocedural parameter constant propagation remain intentional abstentions.

issues.title: Cross-file inherited TclOO callback references preserve effective provider and visibility
issues.body:
## Problem

Once a TclOO callback target is extracted from a list/namespace-code prefix, the workspace layer must attribute it to the effective method provider across files. A callback in an inheriting class can reach a base method, while an override or an unexported method must not be attributed to that base declaration.

Minimal cross-file shape:

base.tcl:
    oo::class create Base {
        method callback {} { return base }
    }

child.tcl:
    oo::class create Child {
        superclass Base
        method setup {} {
            bind .w <Button-1> [list [self] callback]
        }
    }

The callback occurrence is in child.tcl, but its effective provider may be Base or a later override depending on the TclOO MRO, mixins, and visibility state. The same question must be answered consistently by references, rename, code lens, and call hierarchy.

## Corpus evidence

- tcllib 2.0 modules/httpd/httpd.tcl lines 1011 and 1014 use namespace-code/list my callbacks in a substantial TclOO class hierarchy.
- tcllib 2.0 modules/virtchannel_base/cat.tcl lines 72 and 127 register a method callback from inside a TclOO method.
- TclOO self documentation defines the object receiver and method context semantics: https://core.tcl-lang.org/tcloo/wiki?name=Doc%3A+self
- Existing cross-file TclOO tests in rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/tcloo_navigation.rs cover ordinary inherited and pure-consumer dispatch, but not callback-prefix target attribution.

## Acceptance criteria

- With Base and Child in separate workspace documents, Find References, Rename, Code Lens, and Call Hierarchy include the callback in the correct effective provider family.
- A Child callback that inherits Base.callback is attributed to Base.callback; a Child override is attributed only to the override family.
- Mixin and superclass MRO ordering is respected, including a provider in a third document.
- Cross-file export/unexport/private visibility is respected: external [self] callbacks must not resolve to an unexported method, while an internal my callback may reach private methods according to TclOO semantics.
- Same-named classes in unrelated namespaces/documents remain isolated.
- Pure-consumer documents are included only when the receiver/class identity is proven; dynamic object handles and callback strings abstain.
- References, rename, lens counts/click targets, and call hierarchy use the same resolved site set.
- Add Tcl 8.6/9.0 oracle-backed end-to-end tests for provider, override, visibility, MRO, and unrelated-class negative cases.

## Explicit exclusions and linkage

- #1701 is the original Body-role bind regression; #1703 covers direct callback-prefix extraction; #1704 covers only local stored callback value flow.
- #991 and #993 already cover ordinary cross-file method/lens/rename dispatch; #1099 covers ordinary object handoff across documents. This issue adds no new general $obj method or bare class-dispatch model.
- #1322 and #1050 cover direct [self] and registry-driven my/next/nextto dispatch; this issue concerns workspace attribution after a callback target has been extracted.
- Dynamic receiver inference and interprocedural callback-parameter constant propagation remain out of scope.

issues.title: Registry callback coverage: add a drift gate for command-prefix metadata and callback diagnostics
issues.body:
## Problem

The registry is the semantic source of truth for deferred Tcl callbacks, but there is no focused inventory or drift gate proving that every callback-bearing command/option is represented as an `ArgRole::CommandPrefix`, `command_prefixes`, or a deliberate script/body role with the correct appended-argument contract.

This is a registry-coverage/audit issue, not a TclOO target-extraction issue. #1703 covers list/namespace-code TclOO method targets once a CommandPrefix slot is already found. #978 covered the generic analyser edge for a declared CommandPrefix. #1473 is a broad cross-surface tracking issue and does not provide this callback-specific inventory/gate.

A stale report specifically called out `fcopy -command` versus `chan copy -command`. On the current `rust` head both are already declared as `OptionValue::command_prefix_n("callback", AppendedArity::AtLeast(1))` (see `rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/fcopy.rs` and `chan_.rs`), so that pair is a useful regression control, not a new missing-metadata bug. The same question should be answered systematically for Tk, Expect, Tcllib, and iRules surfaces.

## Evidence / audit seeds

- Tcl `fcopy -command callback` and `chan copy -command callback` both invoke the callback later with a count and, on failure, an error argument.
- Existing metadata already covers representative Tk prefixes (`-command`, `-xscrollcommand`, `-yscrollcommand`), Expect `exit -onexit`, Tcllib callback options, and dynamic layouts such as `interp bgerror`, `selection handle`, and `regsub -command`.
- F5 iRulesLX `ILX::call`/`ILX::notify` are remote-method calls, not Tcl CommandPrefix callbacks; they are intentionally out of this issue and are tracked separately by the proposed ILX navigation issue.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Build a machine-readable inventory (or equivalent registry test) of every documented callback-bearing command/option/subcommand in the supported Tcl 8.4–9.1, Tk, Expect, Tcllib, and supported dialect registries. Each row records its kind (CommandPrefix, Body/script, remote method, or intentional dynamic/unknown), source link, dialect/version floor, and appended-argument contract where applicable.
2. For every inventory row, prove that the registry declaration is consumed by the relevant reference/definition, rename/reference-count, call-graph, semantic-token/body, and callback-arity diagnostic paths. A callback that cannot be statically resolved must be explicitly classified as dynamic/unknown rather than silently omitted.
3. Add positive and negative tests for option-bearing and positional forms, including `fcopy -command` and `chan copy -command` as parity controls, Tk widget command-prefix options, Tcllib callbacks, and at least one version/dialect-gated callback. Verify exact callback arity where Tcl documents it and preserve conservative behavior for unknown arity.
4. Make the inventory/drift test fail when a callback-bearing registry row is changed to a plain value/flag or when a documented callback surface has no classification, without duplicating per-command logic in compiler/LSP consumers.
5. Document how new callback surfaces are added and link the inventory to the command-spec documentation.

## Explicit exclusions

- TclOO method extraction through `[list my ...]` or `namespace code` (see #1703).
- One-hop stored callback constants (#1704) and cross-file inherited/effective visibility (#1705).
- The separate iRulesLX remote JavaScript method symbol model.
- Re-implementing the generic CommandPrefix analyser edge from #978.

issues.title: iRulesLX: navigate literal ILX::call/notify methods to ILXServer.addMethod definitions
issues.body:
## Problem

The registry knows `ILX::init`, `ILX::call`, and `ILX::notify` as iRules commands, but the `METHOD` word is currently just an untyped argument. In real iRulesLX code that word is the RPC method name exported by a Node.js extension via `ILXServer.addMethod(name, callback)`. Go-to-definition, hover, and find-references therefore cannot connect an iRule call to the JavaScript handler.

This is a cross-language symbol-model issue, not a TclOO callback-prefix issue (#1703), a generic CommandPrefix issue (#978), or a request to infer arbitrary dynamic Tcl values.

## Evidence

- F5 documents `ILX::call HANDLE ?-timeout ms? ?--? METHOD ?args ...?` and `ILX::notify HANDLE METHOD (ARGS)*` as invoking a specified Node.js method:
  - https://clouddocs.f5.com/cli/tmsh-reference/v16/modules/ilx/ilx_plugin.html
  - https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules-lx/ILXServer.html
- The F5 API documents the JavaScript declaration as `ilx.addMethod("method name", function(req, res) { ... })`; request parameters are supplied by the Tcl `ILX::call`/`ILX::notify` arguments.
- The current registry specs (`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/irules/ilx__call.rs`, `ilx__notify.rs`) expose hover and arity but no method-symbol role or cross-file target relation. No existing issue covers ILX or this Tcl↔JavaScript navigation.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Define a scoped remote-method symbol model for iRulesLX extension sources. Index the documented JavaScript registration shape `ILXServer.addMethod("literal", handler)` (including the normal `new f5.ILXServer()`/variable form) in extension entry-point files such as `index.js`. Keep method symbols scoped to their plugin/extension; do not make a method name globally unique.
2. When an iRule has a statically identifiable handle from a literal `ILX::init plugin extension` (including a documented workspace/config mapping where source layout cannot establish the association), and a literal method word, make `ILX::call` and `ILX::notify` go-to-definition and hover resolve to the matching JavaScript `addMethod` registration. Support `ILX::call`'s `-timeout` and `--` layout without treating them as the method.
3. Find-references from the JavaScript registration must include matching literal `ILX::call` and `ILX::notify` sites in associated iRule documents; references from a Tcl call must include the registration. Add end-to-end fixtures containing both the iRule and extension JavaScript.
4. Be conservative: dynamic handles, computed/variable method names, string concatenation, unknown plugin mappings, missing JavaScript sources, duplicate registrations, and default-method dispatch must abstain or report an explicitly scoped ambiguity rather than guessing a target. Do not emit an unresolved-method diagnostic unless the extension and its method table are known.
5. Preserve dialect gating: this relation is available only for iRules/iRulesLX documents and must not affect ordinary Tcl commands named `ILX::call`/unknown command text. Keep `ILX::call` and `ILX::notify` distinct in telemetry/hover (synchronous versus best-effort notification), while sharing the method target.
6. Document supported JavaScript syntax and workspace mapping, and explicitly classify unsupported registration forms (constructor method maps, dynamic `addMethod` names, `removeMethod`, `setDefaultMethod`) as abstentions until modeled.

## Explicit exclusions

- General JavaScript/TypeScript language-server implementation.
- TclOO `my`/namespace-code extraction, stored callback constants, or inherited visibility (#1703–#1705).
- Tcl CommandPrefix arity diagnostics: ILX methods receive RPC request parameters and are not Tcl command prefixes with appended Tcl words.
- Runtime BIG-IP/plugin execution or validation of remote method behavior.

issues.title: iRules: model registry-declared command-to-event emissions for cross-event reachability
issues.body:
## Problem

The registry models which iRules events permit a command through `event_requires`, and it separately lists event names/descriptions, but it does not model commands that *raise another event*. As a result, consumers that build event-rooted reachability, diagrams, or cross-event data-flow cannot follow these documented transitions without growing command-name tables.

Concrete seeds:

- `TCP::notify request` can raise `USER_REQUEST`; `TCP::notify response` can raise `USER_RESPONSE`; `eom` only marks a message boundary. F5 documents both the event-emission use and the message-boundary use, so this must be represented as a conditional/possible emission rather than an unconditional call edge: https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/TCP__notify.html
- `NAME::lookup <name>` continues asynchronously and eventually raises `NAME_RESOLVED`, where `NAME::response` retrieves the result: https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/NAME__lookup.html
- The registry already contains the target events (`USER_REQUEST`, `USER_RESPONSE`, `NAME_RESOLVED`) in `event_descriptions.rs`/generated event facts, but `tcp__notify.rs` and `name__lookup.rs` have no typed emission descriptor.
- No existing issue in the tracker covers command-to-event emission; #1473 is broad centralisation tracking, not this semantic relation.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Add a registry-owned, typed command-to-event emission descriptor, separate from `event_requires` (which answers whether a command is legal *inside* the current event). The descriptor must support literal subcommand/argument selectors, target event names, and whether the emission is definite, possible/conditional, asynchronous, or non-emitting for that form.
2. Seed the descriptor with the documented cases:
   - `TCP::notify request` → possible `USER_REQUEST`;
   - `TCP::notify response` → possible `USER_RESPONSE`;
   - `TCP::notify eom` → no user-event emission;
   - `NAME::lookup` with a valid target → asynchronous `NAME_RESOLVED`.
   Validate target names against the registry event table and preserve version/deprecation/dialect facts.
3. Feed the descriptor into the event-rooted executable/reachability model and the iRules diagram/reference consumers (or one shared event-edge owner) so a command in an event can create a typed edge to the emitted event and its handler/procedure closure. Do not add command-name matches in each consumer. If existing data-collection/cross-event edges can share the same descriptor, unify them rather than creating a second table.
4. Add end-to-end tests proving:
   - a literal `TCP::notify request` in a reachable event can reach a `when USER_REQUEST` handler;
   - `response` reaches `USER_RESPONSE`;
   - `eom` does not reach either user event;
   - `NAME::lookup` can reach `NAME_RESOLVED` and a helper called from that handler;
   - dynamic/computed subcommands and unknown command aliases produce no guessed event edge.
5. Preserve the important conditional semantics: do not claim that `TCP::notify request/response` always emits a user event when an mblb message-boundary context may consume it; expose/retain the edge as possible unless the surrounding model proves the event mode. Likewise, asynchronous lookup edges must not be treated as same-frame fall-through.
6. Document the descriptor contract and require new event-emitting commands to declare it in the registry, with a drift test that rejects target event names absent from the event registry.

## Explicit exclusions

- TclOO callback-prefix extraction and stored/inherited method navigation (#1703–#1705).
- iRulesLX remote JavaScript method navigation (#1707).
- Replacing `event_requires` or the existing event legality checks.
- Inferring events from arbitrary script text or dynamic command aliases.

issues.title: Post-release: adversarial audit and normalization of command semantics
issues.body:
## Goal

After the current release, perform an evidence-led, adversarial review of every behavioural fact in `CommandSpec` and its resolved semantic projections. The model must distinguish **verified absence** from **not yet known**, eliminate overlapping sources of truth, and make consumers use one central derived query for each semantic question.

`PURE` is the motivating example: purity is calculable from a complete effect footprint and should not remain an independently authored trait that can disagree with `side_effects` / `world_effects`. The same review must look for equivalent overlap or ambiguity across traits, effects, taint, callbacks, state transitions, result stability, representation effects, argument roles, scope, lifecycle, and related descriptors.

## Evidence scope

Audit against primary implementation and real usage, not existing registry comments:

- Tcl 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, 9.0, and a pinned Tcl 9.1 tag/commit source, tests, and manuals.
- Tk source, tests, manuals, demos, and the Tk-heavy repositories catalogued in `docs/CORPUS.md`.
- Tcllib source, tests, manuals, and catalogued Tcllib consumers.
- The full #1181 corpus and any newly discovered sources. Record new sources and their licence/provenance in `docs/CORPUS.md`; do not commit downloaded corpus trees.
- Run small differential experiments on the supported interpreters where source inspection does not prove observable behaviour. Retain the script, exact interpreter build/version, platform/build configuration, output, and oracle.
- For iRules, iApps, tmsh, EDA, Expect extensions, and other vendor surfaces without adequate primary evidence, record `Unknown` explicitly rather than guessing. Promote an unknown only when evidence is captured.

For each audited command/form/subcommand/option, retain concise evidence: source file/function or manual/test reference, versions/dialects checked, experiment/oracle when used, and the resulting semantic facts.

## Semantic model requirements

1. Separate known facts from their **knowledge/completeness**. Every semantic domain whose omission currently means absence must carry at least `Unknown` (no reliable fact or closed boundary), `Partial` (one or more evidence-backed may-facts plus an unknown residual), or `Complete` (the domain is closed and omitted facts are proven absent). This is mandatory per domain, not an aggregate command flag. Domains include world/representation effects, reads and writes, taint, callbacks/re-entrancy, state transitions, completion/control flow, result stability/volatility, scope/lifecycle, and argument role/layout. An unverified guess is not `Partial`: retain it separately as a hypothesis or leave the domain `Unknown` until evidence exists. An empty complete domain means “verified absent”; an empty partial/unknown domain does not. Derive an optional summary only after resolving domains: all closed is `Complete`; some verified facts with any open residual is `Partial`; no verified facts with an open boundary is `Unknown`.
2. Version both facts and completeness. A command/domain may be `Complete` for Tcl 9.0 while remaining `Unknown` for Tcl 8.4, or change when an option, callback path, platform implementation, or state transition is introduced. Resolve independent Tcl, Tk, package, vendor/product, platform, and build-feature axes across dialect, subcommand/form, option-selected shape, and source-aware call. A package-require floor is not an installed version: facts attached to a floor must hold for every compatible version. Shared implementation evidence may justify an explicit range; evidence from one release must never silently fill another cell. An unresolved target version/profile conservatively joins every possible supported cell and cannot inherit the newest/default row.
3. Define and test exact composition for command → subcommand → form → literal/option-selected shape → version/dialect/platform layer → external SpecTcl pack. Extension unions known may-facts but retains any inherited or added unknown residual. Replacement discards an inherited unknown only with explicit closed evidence for that exact invocation shape. A join over possible runtime forms is complete only when every candidate is complete; dynamic or expanded selectors preserve the union and unknown residual. External packs need schema/versioned provenance, authority, precedence, and trust rules so they cannot accidentally declare a built-in/vendor unknown complete.
4. Provide one central utility/query for each derived decision. Examples include `effects.pure()`, `effects.requires_barrier()`, taint-source/sink/sanitizer queries, callback/re-entrancy queries, termination/control-flow queries, and mutation/read/write queries. Each query must take or inherit the resolved dialect/release/package floor. Consumers must not reconstruct these answers from raw slices or combinations of flags.
5. Define derived predicates precisely before migration. Side-effect-free, referentially transparent, non-throwing, result-stable, reorderable, DCE-safe, CSE-safe, and const-foldable are different answers: reads of mutable world state, volatility, callbacks/traces, non-normal completion, and representation effects must participate where relevant. Remove `Traits::PURE` after all purity consumers use the central effect query. Audit `SubCommand::pure`, `PURE_EVALUATION`, `CSE_CANDIDATE`, user-procedure/stub purity and every other authored shortcut; remove/derive each or document its distinct irreducible contract. Prevent reintroduction with a gate.
6. Preserve conservative soundness. Semantic footprints describe possible (may) facts unless explicitly modelled otherwise; do not confuse epistemic lower bounds with must-effects. Unknown or partial residuals are not pure, CSE-safe, reorderable, or evidence that callback/taint/transition behavior is absent. Evidence-backed facts on a partial footprint remain useful positive may-facts while absence queries remain widened.
7. Ensure aliases and source-aware resolved invocations carry the same final semantics as their canonical command without per-command branches in compiler/analyser/LSP consumers. Resolve a partially applied alias after injecting its prefix arguments because it may select a subcommand/form/option shape; preserve `interp alias` interpreter/frame context.

## Consumer migration

Inventory and migrate every consumer, including at least:

- lowering, CFG/SSA/effect SSA/world-state SSA, optimiser/GVN/CSE/DCE, const folding, inlining, codegen, VM/WASM backing, BPF and dialect checks;
- diagnostics, taint propagation, side-effect rendering, hover, semantic tokens, completion, references/call hierarchy, preview and AI tooling;
- SpecTcl loader/emitter/catalogue, CommandSpeci/Spec Studio editor, generated reference pages, `?` help, examples, validation, round trips, and external packs.

Each consumer should call the resolved central query and have adversarial tests for `Unknown`, verified-empty, form refinement, dialect/version/platform refinement, alias prefix injection, external-pack layering, ambiguous abbreviations/overlapping forms, invalid invocations, and dynamic/expanded source abstention. Make authored semantic fields private to the resolver where practical; any raw-access allow-list must be small, explicit, and machine checked rather than relying only on text grep.

## Spec Studio and documentation

- Expose `Unknown` explicitly and make verified-empty visually distinct.
- Document authored versus derived properties and show the central derivation in the `?` reference and code samples.
- Trait example diagrams must put the trait badge only on the command occurrence that owns the trait. Context and consequence arrows may explain other lines, but must not label those lines as carrying the trait.
- Do not show `PURE` as an authorable trait once purity is derived. Show why a verified-empty effect footprint is pure and why an unknown footprint is not.
- Audit all examples for causal clarity, arrow order, and factual correspondence to the selected property.

## Generated audit and drift gates

Generate a checked coverage matrix and version/dialect-aware semantic inventory covering commands, subcommands, forms, options, widget/image instance methods, platform variants, and external packs. The denominator is the full pinned upstream Tcl/Tk/Tcllib surface, including missing registry entries—not merely whatever is already registered. At minimum report:

- evidence state and provenance per dialect/release/package floor;
- effect footprint, per-domain completeness, and whether it is unknown, partial, verified-empty, or known non-empty;
- derived purity/barrier/mutation classifications;
- taint sources, sinks, sanitizers, and callback-supplied taint inputs;
- callback kind, timing, execution context/re-entrancy, and appended arity;
- state transitions, control-flow completion, result stability, and representation effects;
- remaining unknowns grouped by dialect/package and consumer exposure.
- a disposition for every authored trait/descriptor: derived and removed, retained as irreducible with rationale, or still unresolved. Zero entries may remain unreviewed.

Add drift gates that fail when a new registry surface silently receives an implicit empty fact, when an authored trait duplicates a derived property, when generated Studio/reference documentation drifts, or when a consumer bypasses the central query with a raw-field reconstruction.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every pinned upstream Tcl/Tk/Tcllib command, subcommand, form, option, widget/image instance method, and platform-dependent surface has reviewed evidence and mandatory per-domain completeness (`Unknown`, `Partial`, or `Complete`); no implicit “empty means unknown” remains.
- Vendor/dialect gaps are explicitly unknown and visible in the generated inventory.
- `Traits::PURE` is removed; all former consumers use `effects.pure()` (or the final central name) and tests distinguish unknown from verified-empty.
- `SubCommand::pure`, `PURE_EVALUATION`, `CSE_CANDIDATE`, procedure/stub purity, and every other authored semantic descriptor have a generated disposition; overlaps are removed or documented as genuinely distinct and irreducible with one source of truth.
- SpecTcl, CommandSpeci/Spec Studio, generated docs, `?` help, examples, preview, and AI tooling round-trip and explain the model completely.
- Corpus sources discovered during the work are added to `docs/CORPUS.md`, with no downloaded corpus committed.
- Goldens cover unknown target version (`open`: 9.0 complete, 8.4 unknown, unresolved not 9.0), a new semantic domain defaulting every existing row to `Unknown`, external-pack extension/replacement, partial aliases, dynamic/expanded forms, ambiguous/invalid invocations, and platform-dependent behaviour.
- Targeted tests, generated drift gates, `make rust-check`, and `make prep-pr` pass. Performance is measured on a named workload and baseline with an agreed regression threshold recorded in the PR.

Related: #1181 (corpus), #1703-#1706 (callback/indexing work), #1711 (Tk/CommandSpec/Spec Studio groundwork).

labels.name: spec-studio
labels.description: Spec Studio UI, generation, and editor integrations

issues.title: Post-release semantic-facts audit: explicit completeness, versioning, and derived purity
issues.body:
## Problem

The registry's semantic facts have grown across side effects, traits, taints,
completion behaviour, and related descriptors, but there is no source-backed
audit proving that they are complete, non-overlapping, correctly versioned, or
consistently consumed.

In particular:

- an unannotated command can look indistinguishable from a command audited and
  found to be side-effect free;
- a guessed effect may be incomplete, which differs from both fully unknown and
  fully audited;
- facts can vary by Tcl/Tk version or dialect;
- `PURE` duplicates information calculable from side effects and can drift;
- Tcl/Tk/tcllib facts need upstream-source and executable-oracle evidence,
  while EDA, iRules, iApps, and other external dialects must remain explicitly
  unknown where evidence is unavailable.

## Scope

Perform a post-release audit across the registry, compiler, analyser, LSP, Spec
Studio, SpecTcl, generated documentation, and examples. Encode a clear
completeness model distinguishing at least:

1. entirely unknown;
2. partially known or based on an incomplete/guessed effect set; and
3. fully audited for the applicable version/dialect window.

The status must be version- and dialect-specific: a command may be fully known
for Tcl 9.0 while Tcl 8.4 or an external dialect remains unknown.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every unaudited command has an explicit unknown semantic status rather than
  silently appearing fully known or pure.
- Guessed/incomplete effect sets are distinguishable from entirely unknown and
  fully audited sets.
- Knowledge carries applicable package-version and dialect windows.
- Tcl, Tk, and tcllib commands are audited against upstream source and
  executable experiments across supported releases.
- EDA, iRules, iApps, and other external surfaces are conservatively unknown
  unless independently evidenced.
- Add central semantic queries, including `SideEffects::pure()` (or its final
  equivalent), and migrate every consumer from the `PURE` trait.
- Remove `PURE` as a redundant semantic authority once consumers and generated
  surfaces use the central query.
- Audit traits, side effects, taints, completion facts, and related descriptors
  for overlap, contradiction, and unclear ownership.
- Add drift gates so new registry rows cannot omit the required
  unknown/partial/full classification or regress to an ambiguous default.
- Update CommandSpec documentation, Spec Studio help, generated references,
  DSL examples, Tcl stubs, Rust projections, and code samples.

## Related work

#1711 added substantial Tk semantic infrastructure, version-aware lifecycle
handling, and Spec Studio plumbing. It does not complete this source-backed
audit, completeness model, or `PURE` migration.

issues.title: tclvm: `array get` / element access drops every element when the array NAME contains an unmatched `(`
issues.body:
Found in passing while fixing the #1602 / #1578 / #1616 variable-name cluster (PR #1728). Left unfixed there deliberately — the fix is a `VarStore` contract change, which is larger than that cluster.

## Problem

An array whose **name** contains an unmatched `(` loses every element on `array get`:

```tcl
array set {z(b} {a 1}
array get   {z(b}    ;# tclvm: {}      tclsh 8.6.16 / 9.0.4: a 1
array names {z(b}    ;# tclvm: a       (already correct)
array size  {z(b}    ;# tclvm: 1       (already correct)
```

Oracle, byte-identical on tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4:

```
array get {z(b} = 'a 1'  names='a' size=1
```

`array names` and `array size` are already right, so this is specifically the element-*value* path.

## Cause

`VarStore::get_elem` recomposes the qualified cell name with `format!("{name}({key})")` and re-parses it. For `name = "z(b"` and `key = "a"` that composes `z(b(a)`, which the parser splits at the **first** `(` — so the lookup asks for array `z` element `b(a` and finds nothing.

Any array whose name legitimately contains `(` is affected; the round-trip through a composed string is not injective.

## Suggested direction

Frame-aware element accessors on the `VarStore` contract that carry `(name, key)` as a pair, rather than recomposing a qualified string and re-splitting it. That removes the ambiguity at the source instead of adding another parse special case — PR #1728 established the same principle on the store side (`split_element_ref` as the single shared owner for deciding whether a word *is* an element reference).

## Acceptance criteria

- `array get` on an array whose name contains `(`, `)`, or both returns the same pairs as tclsh 8.4–9.1.
- `array names` / `array size` / `array unset` / element read and write stay correct for such names (regression cover — `names`/`size` are correct today and must not regress).
- Negative boundary preserved: a word that really *is* an element reference (`arr(k)`) still resolves as one, and `set r(\$i) 2` still keys on the literal `$i` (PR #1728's vectors).
- Oracle-backed tests at 8.6 and 9.0, release-invariant ones spot-checked at 8.4/8.5/9.1, in the style of `rust/tcl-vm/tests/variable_name_resolution_e2e.rs`.

issues.title: iRulesLX navigation is desktop-only: every ILX tier abstains for a non-`file:` URI, so the relation is inert on vscode.dev / github.dev
issues.body:
Split out of the #1707 review round (PR #1733), where Codex flagged that the browser entry point does not register the JavaScript reference provider. It is right that it does not — but the registration is not the gap, and adding it would advertise support that does not exist.

**Defect:** the whole iRulesLX remote-method relation is **filesystem-path** shaped. `extensions/<name>/` is matched on path components, the entry point is resolved through `package.json`'s `main`, and the caller search lists directories. So every server tier starts by turning the request's URI into a path, and a URI that is not `file:` has none:

| tier | `rust/tcl-lsp-server/src/lib.rs` |
|---|---|
| `ilx_references_command` | `let path = uri.to_file_path()?` |
| `ilx_references` | `let path = uri.to_file_path()?` |
| `ilx_definition` | `let path = uri.to_file_path()?` |
| hover | `if let Some(path) = uri.to_file_path()` |

On the web hosts documents are `vscode-vfs:` (and friends), `to_file_path` returns `None`, and all four abstain. This is **not** specific to the JavaScript end added in #1733 — it has been true of the definition and hover tiers since #1730 landed, so go-to-definition and hover on an `ILX::call` method word have never worked on vscode.dev or github.dev either. Nothing in the `test-ext-web` suite covers the relation, which is why it went unnoticed.

**Scope of a fix.** Not a client-side registration. The relation needs URI-shaped discovery throughout:

1. **Extension lookup** — `locate_extension` / `extension_of_entry` walk `Path` components for `extensions/<name>/` and the workspace directory. These want a URI-segment equivalent.
2. **Entry-point resolution** — `entry_file` reads `package.json` and stats `index.js`; both go through `IlxFiles`, which is already an abstraction (`SourceStore` + `OpenDocuments`), so this may only need the store to answer for virtual URIs.
3. **Directory listing** — `rule_files` / `collect_tcl_sources` call `SourceStore::read_dir`. Whether the wasm server's store can list a synced virtual workspace is the open question, and probably decides how much of this is reachable at all.
4. **Client** — register `registerIlxReferenceProvider` in `editors/vscode/src/extensionBrowser.ts` and drop the `scheme !== "file"` guard in `ilxReferences.ts` once the server can answer.

Worth settling first whether the wasm server's source store can enumerate directories in a synced workspace (`editors/vscode/src/webWorkspaceSync.ts`); if it cannot, the caller search has no basis on the web and only the *definition* direction (JS entry point from a Tcl call) is reachable, which would be a smaller and still useful scope.

**Documented meanwhile** in `docs/design/iruleslx-remote-methods.md` ("Desktop only, and why") and on `registerIlxReferenceProvider`, so the omission reads as deliberate rather than forgotten.

issues.title: tclvm: Tcltest driver bypasses Tcl 9 init.tcl and installs a hand-picked startup subset
issues.body:
## Problem

The bytecode-VM side of the Tcltest parity runner does not exercise the same Tcl 9 startup path as the C oracle.

`rust/tcl-vm/examples/run_test.rs` explicitly says the VM has no full `init.tcl` path. It directly sources `$TCL_LIBRARY/tcltest/tcltest.tcl`, imports `::tcltest::*`, and separately calls `Vm::init_auto_load()`, which installs a focused hand-maintained subset of the startup machinery. By contrast, the reference `tclsh` has already run `Tcl_Init` and the tree-walk runtime's `run_script --init` sources the real library `init.tcl`.

This makes a C/VM count match weaker than it looks: an `init.tcl`, package, unknown/autoload, or startup-global divergence can be bypassed on the VM side instead of exposed by the upstream suite.

## Required fix

- Add a bytecode-VM library-initialization entry point that sources the selected release's real `$TCL_LIBRARY/init.tcl` through the normal compiler/evaluator path.
- Make the Tcltest driver call that entry point, then use normal `package require tcltest`; do not source `tcltest.tcl` directly or install a second hand-picked startup implementation.
- Keep startup ownership shared as deeply as the two Rust engines' different object/storage models permit: release globals, platform/bootstrap facts, package seeds, and host paths must continue to come from their existing central owners.
- Make the `cargo xtask tcltest-sweep` VM and C sides use the same exact Tcl 9.0.4 source tree and library.
- Keep backend-specific exclusions in the existing constraint overlay, limited to non-semantic host/platform and internal-representation probes. Do not skip ordinary language-semantic failures.

## Acceptance evidence

- A focused driver test proves Tcl 9.0.4 `init.tcl` ran (not merely that autoload happens to work).
- The real Tcl 9.0.4 `package require tcltest` succeeds through package discovery.
- At least one focused upstream `.test` stem runs through the new path and still emits a parseable Tcltest summary.
- A mutation that bypasses or breaks `init.tcl` makes the driver test fail.

Found during the all-open-`tclvm` conformance programme while centralizing its Tcl 9.0.4 oracle.

issues.title: tclvm: relative-qualified upvar targets resolve in the callee namespace instead of the target frame
issues.body:
Found by the post-merge audit of PR #1742. The new shared upvar-link path resolves a relatively qualified target with the current callee namespace even when the requested target level belongs to a caller in another namespace.

Example shape: `::B::inner` executes `upvar 1 rel::x y` while called by `::A::outer`. Tcl 9.0.4 links `y` to `::A::rel::x`; tclvm can report a missing namespace or link to `::B::rel::x`. Both the parent-namespace check and final target lookup currently use the callee context.

Required fix:

- derive the namespace context from the designated target frame/level before resolving a relative-qualified target
- use that context consistently for namespace existence, scalar/element lookup, and link installation
- keep the resolution rule in the shared variable/frame owner rather than adding an `upvar`-name special case
- add exact Tcl 9.0.4 regressions covering distinct caller/callee namespaces and scalar/array targets

Review evidence: https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/pull/1742#discussion_r3898158771

issues.title: TclVM namespace reparse and child hash state survive live mutation
issues.body:
## Tcl 9.0.4 oracle gaps

Two state-retention gaps were found during review of #1747 after it merged:

- An ensemble `-unknown` handler that reconfigures the same ensemble and returns an empty list must reparse against the live configuration, not the dispatch-time snapshot. A callback-installed `-map {nope ::target}` must dispatch `nope` immediately.
- `namespace children` must retain the namespace child table's Tcl string-hash resize and bucket-chain history after child deletion. Tcl hash tables do not shrink on entry removal, so reconstructing from only the surviving children changes observable enumeration order.

## Required implementation

- Refresh the live ensemble configuration before the single reparse in both TclVM engines.
- Centralize Tcl string-hash insertion, resize, deletion, and enumeration state in the shared namespace owner and have both engines retain it per namespace.
- Pin both behaviors to exact Tcl 9.0.4 oracle vectors in the native VM and `runtime/rust`.

Found in automated review comments on #1747.

issues.title: Retain deleted namespace command tables until the last active namespace frame exits
issues.body:
## Tcl 9.0.4 oracle

An active frame retains the deleted namespace token and its private command table until that last activation exits. The namespace is unlinked from public name lookup immediately, so absolute introspection sees no commands, but relative command resolution from the retained frame still reaches the old table:

```tcl
set answer [namespace eval N {
    proc q {} {return Q}
    proc p {} {
        namespace delete ::N
        set code [catch {q} message]
        list [namespace exists ::N] [info commands ::N::p] \
             [info commands ::N::q] $code $message [namespace current]
    }
    p
}]
list $answer [namespace exists ::N] [info commands ::N::*]
```

Tcl 9.0.4 returns:

```text
{0 {} {} 0 Q ::N} 0 {}
```

This is the `activationCount > ...` branch in `Tcl_DeleteNamespace` (`generic/tclNamesp.c`): mark `NS_DYING`, unlink the parent/name edge, retain contents for active frames, and invoke deletion again from `Tcl_PopCallFrame` after the final activation exits.

## Current divergence

Both native `tcl-vm` and `runtime/rust` unlink **and eagerly clear** the namespace command table inside the `namespace delete` command. They now retain enough token identity for `namespace current` and public liveness checks, but a relative `q` cannot keep resolving through that old token.

## Required design

- Put activation/deferred-teardown state on the shared namespace-token owner, not command-name special cases.
- Unlink public namespace/name edges immediately; `namespace exists ::N` and absolute `info commands ::N::*` stay empty.
- Retain the old token's private command/variable/child state while any proc or namespace-eval frame owns it.
- Resolve relative commands from the retained frame token during that interval.
- Run fixed-point command/import/trace/ensemble/variable/child cleanup when the last activation pops.
- A same-named recreated namespace must receive a distinct token and command table; it must not revive or absorb the retained dead token.
- Add exact Tcl 9.0.4 regressions for both engines, covering proc and namespace-eval activations plus same-name recreation.

Found during the final namespace lifecycle audit for #1749.

issues.title: Preserve Tcl command-table hash order during namespace teardown
issues.body:
## Tcl 9.0.4 oracle

Namespace command teardown copies `nsPtr->cmdTable` in `Tcl_FirstHashEntry` order before deleting each token. Delete traces make that persistent `TCL_STRING_KEYS` order observable:

```tcl
set log {}
proc rec {old new op} {lappend ::log [namespace tail $old]}
namespace eval N {}
foreach n {one two three four five six seven eight nine ten} {
    proc ::N::$n {} {}
    trace add command ::N::$n delete rec
}
namespace delete ::N
set log
```

Tcl 9.0.4 returns:

```text
six four three eight seven nine five two one ten
```

Deletion and reinsertion history, including table growth without shrink, changes this order just as it does for `namespace children`.

## Current divergence

- Native `tcl-vm` stores commands in a Rust `HashMap` and builds namespace teardown frontiers from its randomized iteration.
- `runtime/rust` stores namespace commands in a `BTreeMap`, so teardown is lexical.
- #1749 centralizes the same hash-table lifecycle for namespace child tables and adds the separate ordered intrusive-list owner for namespace-owned ensembles, but ordinary per-namespace command tables still have no Tcl hash-order owner.

## Required design

- Reuse/generalize the shared `TclStringHashOrder` implementation for every namespace command table.
- Route every real/imported binding insert, replacement, rename, hide/expose, forget, and deletion through that table owner so capacity and bucket-chain history survive mutations.
- Enumerate fixed-point namespace teardown snapshots in the retained Tcl hash order in both engines.
- Preserve separate command-token and import-ref lifecycle ordering; command-table order selects source tokens but does not replace the existing depth-first import retirement.
- Add exact Tcl 9.0.4 native/runtime regressions for growth, deletion, reinsertion, trace-created commands, and same-named replacements.

Found during final review of #1749.

issues.title: Store native tclvm command and namespace sidecar state by token during deferred recreation
issues.body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #1751. The native `tcl-vm` currently stores namespace commands, variables, traces/import identities, paths, exports, unknown handlers, and child state primarily under flat canonical FQN strings. Activation-delayed deletion can retain the old token for relative lookup, but a live namespace recreated with the same spelling must coexist with that old private table. A single `::N::q` / `::N::v` key cannot represent both incarnations.

The Rust/WASM runtime already has per-`NsId` namespace arena tables and does not have this structural collision.

## Exact Tcl 9.0.4 oracle

```tcl
set answer [namespace eval N {
    variable v OLD
    proc q {} {return OLDQ}
    proc p {} {
        namespace delete ::N
        namespace eval ::N {variable v NEW; proc q {} {return NEWQ}}
        variable v
        list [q] [::N::q] $v [set v OLD2] [set ::N::v] \
             [info commands q] [info commands ::N::q] \
             [namespace current] [namespace exists {}] [namespace exists ::N]
    }
    p
}]
list $answer [set ::N::v] [::N::q]
```

Expected with Tcl 9.0.4:

```tcl
{OLDQ NEWQ OLD OLD2 NEW q ::N::q ::N 0 1} NEW NEWQ
```

## Required owner refactor

- Store command and namespace-variable tables by stable namespace token (`NsId`) plus simple name; keep public FQN lookup as a separate live-name index.
- Key command generations, command/execution traces, imports, builtin/TclOO identities, and active sidecars by stable binding identity rather than FQN spelling.
- Put child/path/export/unknown lifecycle state on the namespace token as well.
- Preserve a proc command token's defining `NsId` through invocation and rename.
- Absolute lookup must reach the recreated live token while relative lookup from an old active frame reaches the retained dying token.
- Final teardown must delete only the old token tables and must not disturb the new same-spelled namespace.

Do not use synthetic Tcl-visible names as storage keys: Tcl names can contain arbitrary data and sidecar rendering/identity would remain ambiguous.

## Additional coverage

Cover pre-delete `variable` links, command/variable teardown traces, imports, a recreated child subtree, and suspended coroutine activations alongside the exact oracle above.

issues.title: Retain compiled descendant command tokens across activation-delayed parent namespace deletion
issues.body:
## Tcl 9.0.4 oracle

```tcl
set answer [namespace eval ::N {
    namespace eval C {proc q {} {return OLDQ}}
    proc p {} {
        namespace delete ::N
        namespace eval ::N::C {proc q {} {return NEWQ}}
        list [C::q] [::N::C::q]
    }
    p
}]
list $answer [::N::C::q]
```

Tcl 9.0.4 returns:

```tcl
{OLDQ OLDQ} NEWQ
```

The tokenized namespace-table work for #1751/#1752/#1753 makes the relative `C::q` call reach the retained old child table, but tcl-vm and runtime/rust currently produce `{OLDQ NEWQ} NEWQ`: the literal absolute `::N::C::q` call is re-resolved through the recreated FQN.

## Required ownership

Fix this in the shared compiler/runtime command-reference cache and stable binding-token owner. A precompiled literal command reference must retain the old descendant command token through activation-delayed namespace teardown, while a later compilation/dynamic lookup sees the recreated command. Do not special-case `namespace delete`, descendant names, or this proc at an invocation site.

Add exact native and runtime regressions against Tcl 9.0.4. Coordinate with #1648 command-mutation binding identities and #1751/#1753 namespace incarnation tokens so there is one stable command-reference model.

issues.title: Make Tcl oracle setup reject stale 9.0 patchlevels
issues.body:
## Problem

`scripts/dev/ensure-test-deps.sh` treats the Tcl reference toolchain as ready when versioned executable names merely exist. On a host where `/usr/bin/tclsh9.0` is Tcl 9.0.3, the early return succeeds even though the repository pins Tcl 9.0.4. Differential/oracle tests that resolve `tclsh9.0` therefore run against a stale patchlevel, while `tcl-test-support` correctly records the actual binary patchlevel.

Observed locally on 2026-09-01:

```text
$ tclsh9.0 <<'EOF'
puts [info patchlevel]
EOF
9.0.3
```

The retained/source gold tree is Tcl 9.0.4.

## Required behavior

- Centralize the pinned reference patchlevels in the test-tool layer.
- Have `ensure-test-deps` validate exact patchlevels, not just executable presence, before its early return.
- Build/install or wrap the pinned `tmp/tcl9.0.4` interpreter when `tclsh9.0` is present but stale.
- Keep `tcl-test-support` as the runtime oracle resolver/provenance owner and make setup agree with it.
- Add a shell-level regression for the stale-present case without depending on the host installation.
- Preserve Tcl 8.4/8.5/8.6/9.1 release-aware resolution.

This was found while enforcing Tcl 9.0.4 as the gold standard for the open `tclvm` conformance work and SpecTcl 1.x/2.0 execution gates.

issues.title: Make SpecTcl compatibility a non-vacuous Tcl 9.0.4 PR gate
issues.body:
## Problem

The ordinary `rust-tests` workspace run exercises the internal SpecTcl execution/equivalence suites, but `pack_is_real_tcl` silently returns success when no Tcl interpreter is present. The `rust-tests` job currently installs Rust and nextest only, so this real-interpreter part of the compatibility contract can pass vacuously.

## Required contract

- Add one central Make/tool entry point for the SpecTcl compatibility lane.
- Run every shipped 1.x legacy pack through both internal TclVM loader paths.
- Upgrade legacy packs to 2.0 and compare the resulting registry exhaustively.
- Exercise the live pack-source hook path.
- Source every shipped pack with an exact Tcl 9.0.4 interpreter; a missing or stale interpreter must fail rather than skip in this gate.
- Invoke the entry point from PR CI for relevant Rust/tooling changes, while keeping local ordinary tests usable on machines without Tcl.
- Reuse the release-aware reference-toolchain owner rather than embedding another patchlevel or source URL.

This was found while auditing the `tclvm` repair PRs and belongs with the #1757 exact-oracle/toolchain work.

issues.title: Key standalone-runtime command traces by command token across namespace recreation
Give TclOO classes and objects stable identity across deferred namespace deletion
issues.body:
## Problem

Both engines key TclOO backing state by the display fully-qualified name instead of a stable class/object or command-generation identity. Activation-delayed namespace deletion plus same-name recreation therefore crosses incarnations:

- native `tcl-vm` retains the old object command but resolves it through the newly recreated object's FQN-keyed state, so the old object invokes the new method;
- `runtime/rust` destroys TclOO state eagerly when namespace deletion is requested, before the active namespace frame can finish, so the retained old object command disappears.

## Tcl 9.0.4 oracle

```tcl
set r [namespace eval N {
    oo::class create C {method m {} {return OLD}}
    C create o
    proc p {} {
        namespace delete ::N
        namespace eval ::N {
            oo::class create C {method m {} {return NEW}}
            C create o
        }
        set a [catch {o m} am]
        set b [catch {::N::o m} bm]
        list $a $am $b $bm [info commands o] [info commands ::N::o]
    }
    p
}]
set c [catch {::N::o m} cm]
list $r $c $cm
```

Tcl 9.0.4 returns `{0 OLD 0 NEW o ::N::o} 0 NEW`. Native VM returns OLD-as-NEW; standalone runtime loses the old `o`.

## Required contract

- Mint stable TclOO class/object IDs, or reuse the exact stable command generation as the OO registry key.
- Carry that identity inside the native and standalone runtime command variants; keep the FQN as mutable/display metadata only.
- Defer TclOO namespace cleanup until the exact old namespace/command generation is finalized.
- Same-name recreation must not overwrite or destroy retained old backing state.
- Add exact Tcl 9.0.4, native VM, and standalone runtime tests covering simultaneous old/new calls and final old-only teardown.

Found during independent review of the #1751/#1752/#1753 namespace-lifecycle group. This is distinct from command-trace sidecar collision #1763 and must integrate with #1754 command-binding generation logic.

issues.title: wasm codegen: analysis-tier `puts` fast path re-parses compatibility text, so `puts "$p$q"` reads a variable named `p}${q`
issues.body:
Found by the native-lowering review (`docs/design/compiler/wasm-native-lowering-plan.md` §2.2) while linking `samples/wasm/` against the real runtime.

## Repro

```tcl
set p 1; set q 2
puts "$p $q"
puts end
```

Compiled with `SemanticOptimisationPassId::LegacyAnalysisSpecialisation` enabled (`emit_wasm --analysis`) and run against `tcl_runtime.wasm`: prints nothing, not even `end`. Default tier and tclsh print `1 2` / `end`.

## Cause

`try_emit_direct_operation` (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/wasm/backend.rs`, `ChannelWrite` arm) admits the single-argument `puts` fast path when `whole_var_reference(&args[0])` succeeds.
