issues.title: A `::`-qualified global written by a nested RMW is missing from the proc's global-write summary: `puts $hits` folds to the stale value
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
set hits 0
proc bump {} {
    set y [incr ::hits]
    return $y
}
bump
puts $hits
```

tclsh 9.0.4 / 8.6.18 print `1`. `tcl opt FILE --profile full` emits

```tcl
proc bump {} {
    set y [incr ::hits]
    return $y
}
bump
puts 0
```

which prints `0` — the call to `bump` is not seen to write `::hits`, so `set hits 0` is the single reaching definition at `puts $hits` and O102 forwards its literal. The `set hits 0` store is also reported `O109 Eliminate dead store` in the same run.

The braced spelling reproduces identically:

```tcl
proc bump {} { set y [expr {[incr ::hits] + 1}]; return $y }
```

Both spellings agreed before and after #2141 / #2050, which is how this was found rather than introduced.

## What is expected

No O102 and no O109. `bump`'s summary must name `::hits`: the proc writes a global, so a caller's later read of it is not reached by the pre-call store.

## Cause (as far as measured)

`GlobalWriteInfo` for a proc comes from `own_body_global_writes`, whose nested half is `variable_write_effects_from_commands` over the statement's embedded substitutions. That projection *does* return `::hits` for `[incr ::hits]` — the name is recovered. It is `collect_write_targets` that then declines to publish it:

```rust
if !renamed_aliases.targets.contains_key(target)
    && !renamed_aliases.opaque_locals.contains(target)
    && state.get(target).is_some_and(|f| f.writes_outer_scope())
{
    info.names.insert(target.to_owned());
}
```

`state` holds the body's `global` / `variable` / `upvar` declarations, and `bump` makes none — it writes the global by qualifying the name, not by declaring it. A `::`-qualified target is outer-scope by spelling alone and needs no declaration to be one.

A direct `incr ::hits` written as a whole statement may take a different path; the nested-substitution route is the one measured here.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/cfg_builder/global_write_info.rs` — `collect_write_targets`, and `collect_global_frame_effects` beside it.

## Related

- #2050, #2141 (the nested read-modify-write read/write pair — same programs, different layer)

issues.title: O103 folds a pure-proc call without the `expr`-trust gate O110 consults: a shadowed `expr` is evaluated as the builtin
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
namespace eval ::n {}
proc ::n::expr {s} { return "SHADOW:$s" }
proc ::n::f {r} { return [expr {$r ** 2}] }
puts [::n::f 3]
```

tclsh 9.0.4 prints `SHADOW:$r ** 2` — inside `::n`, the unqualified `expr` resolves to `::n::expr`, which returns its argument's source text with a prefix.

`tcl opt FILE --profile full` emits

```tcl
namespace eval ::n {}
proc ::n::expr {s} { return "SHADOW:$s" }
proc ::n::f {r} { return [expr {$r ** 2}] }
puts 9
```

with the single rewrite `O103 Fold pure-proc call to '::n::f' to its constant return`. The optimised program prints `9`.

## Why this is a separate defect from #2159

#2159 fixed O110's half of exactly this: `::n::f`'s **body** is correctly left alone — `return [expr {$r ** 2}]` is not rewritten to `$r * $r`, because the module-wide `expr`-trust gate sees the qualified shadow. The gate works.

O103 does not consult it. It folds the *call* by evaluating the body, and that evaluation treats `expr` as the builtin, so it computes `3 ** 2 = 9`. The body is left honest and the call is folded dishonestly, in the same run.

Reproduces identically at `a7bd7b7` (the merge of #2211) and on the current head, so it predates and is untouched by the nested-read-modify-write work — found while probing the `expr`-trust gate for #2141/#2050.

## What is expected

No O103. `::n::f` is not a pure proc whose return can be evaluated statically, because the `expr` its body calls is not the one the folder would use.

More generally: whatever decides a proc is const-foldable must ask the same question O101/O110/O115/O129 ask — is every command the body calls the one the registry describes?

## Where

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/` — the O103 pure-proc-call fold and its purity/foldability predicate.
- The gate O110 consults is `ModuleCommandMutations` / `trusts("expr")`, reached through `ModuleCommandBindings`; see `builtin_shadowed_by_qualified_definition` in `rust/tcl-compiler/src/command_binding.rs` (added for #2159).

## Related

- #2159 (the same shadow, O110's half — fixed)
- #2218 (a dynamic head in a proc body does not switch the gate off either)

issues.title: A dynamic command head inside a proc body does not switch the module-wide `expr`-trust gate off
issues.body:
## What happens

`samples/optimiser/README.md` states the rule the `expr`-trust gate implements:

> O115 (like O101 and O129) is gated on `expr` being provably untouched across the whole module. A command head the analysis cannot resolve could `rename` `expr`, so an unresolvable head anywhere turns the gate off for the entire file.

A dynamic head inside a procedure body is exactly such a head, and it does not turn the gate off:

```tcl
proc double_expr {x} {
    return [expr {[expr {$x * 2}]}]
}
proc g {cmd} { $cmd }
```

`tcl opt FILE --profile readability` reports `O115 Remove redundant nested expr` and rewrites `double_expr`. `$cmd` can hold `rename ::expr ::realexpr`, which is the case the gate exists for.

The two spellings that *do* switch it off, for contrast — both correctly reported as no-O115:

```tcl
proc setup {} { rename ::expr ::realexpr }
proc install {} { proc ::expr {args} { return SHADOW } }
```

So the gate is reached through a procedure's own unit for a *statically named* threat, but a dynamic head in the same position contributes nothing.

## Measured

| file (plus `double_expr`) | `a7bd7b7` | current head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proc g {cmd} { $cmd }` | O115 fires | O115 fires |
| `rename ::expr` in a proc body | — | not reported |
| `proc ::expr` in a proc body | — | not reported |

Unchanged across the nested-read-modify-write work, so this is pre-existing rather than a regression. It surfaced because #2141's fix stopped a *self-recursive* call being misread as an unresolvable head, which had been switching the gate off in `samples/optimiser/input.tcl` for the wrong reason and masking this row — the README's table asserted this case was "not reported", and it never was.

## What is expected

Either the gate turns off for a dynamic head in a proc body, or the README's stated rule narrows to describe what is actually implemented. The first is the conservative reading and matches the rule as written.

## Where

- Whatever feeds `ModuleCommandMutations` / the `trusts("expr")` query from a procedure body — `rust/tcl-compiler/src/command_binding.rs`, and the opacity signals `ModuleCommandBindings` collects.
- The README table this contradicts: `samples/optimiser/README.md`, § *O115 and the `factorial` stanza* (updated in the same change that found this, so it now records the row honestly rather than asserting the old claim).

## Related

- #2217 (O103 ignores the same gate entirely)
- #2159 (a qualified shadow of `expr` — fixed)

issues.title: A relative builtin spelling (`tcl::dict::set d k v`) is unknown to the registry, so its store is deleted as unread
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
set d {a 1}
tcl::dict::set d k v
puts $d
```

Observed on branch `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42` at e6765dba, `tcl opt --profile full`: the head `tcl::dict::set` resolves to no registry command (only the `::tcl::dict::set` and `dict set` spellings are known), so the invocation has no `VarWrite` role and no `READS_BEFORE_WRITE` trait, O109 deletes `set d {a 1}` as unread, and the optimised program prints `k v`; tclsh 8.5.19 through 9.1b0 print `a 1 k v`.

The fully qualified `::tcl::dict::set` and the plain `dict set` are handled (the keyed updates carry `READS_BEFORE_WRITE` since cd2a7fab).

## What is expected

A relative qualified name resolves the way Tcl resolves it at the global scope: `tcl::dict::set` is `::tcl::dict::set`. The registry lookup (`CommandRegistry`'s name resolution and `ResolvedInvocation`) should canonicalise a relative qualified spelling before matching, so every consumer — the analyser, lowering, the value transfers, the editor's hover and completion — sees the one command.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-registry/src/` (the lookup that maps a spelling to a `CommandSpec`; `resolved_invocation.rs`).
- Witness: the program above under `tcl opt --profile full`, against every tclsh on `PATH`.

issues.title: Compiled `incr x {$n}` raises `can't read "$n"` where tclsh raises `expected integer but got "$n"`
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
proc p {} { set n 3; set x 1; incr x {$n}; return $x }
puts [catch {p} m]
puts $m
```

tclsh 8.4.20 through 9.1b0 print `1` and `expected integer but got "$n"`: a braced amount is the literal text `$n`, which is not an integer. The compiled program (observed on branch `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42` at e6765dba) raises `can't read "$n": no such variable` instead: the lowering treats the braced amount word as a variable reference and reads it before the integer check.

## What is expected

A braced word reaches `incr` as literal text, and the runtime's integer conversion produces the same error text as tclsh. The analysis side already declines the fold with `WrongRepresentation` (the `amount_braced` flag landed in cd2a7fab); the compiled code path needs the same distinction.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering/hooks/incr.rs` (the amount word's token kind) and the codegen for the typed `Incr`.
- `rust/tcl-vm/` for the error text on the integer conversion.

issues.title: tclvm: preserve safe scalar facts across source binding and registry effect projection
issues.body:
Taking this regression group before merging PR #2196. Deep CI on head49ff9148 loses previously valid constant-folding facts across unrelated global writes/traces, existence queries, class-variable contexts, and iRules word-operator conditions.

Representative failing tests: `o101_global_write_across_call_guard`, `o101_module_wide_variable_trace_guard`, `an_existence_query_is_neither_a_read_before_set_nor_a_write`, `a_namespace_alias_is_not_a_caller_frame_alias`, `an_unrelated_class_keeps_propagation_despite_a_classvar_helper_elsewhere`, `irules_word_operators_fold_through_sccp`, and the dialect_threading/CLI iRules counterparts. Native coverage regression #2236 may share lost proof inputs.

Evidence: https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/actions/runs/35832385220

Investigate the interaction of SourceBindingTimeline, source-level bindings and registry handler barrier projection. Preserve opacity where Tcl can genuinely mutate a caller frame, while retaining proven-safe registry calls and unrelated-variable facts. No command-name special cases, test weakening or blind fixture regeneration. A stronger read-only planner and focused implementation agent are tracing the common cause.

issues.title: tclvm: invalidate seeded procedure parameters across registry handler effects
issues.body:
Taking fresh Codex P1 feedback on PR #2196 head49ff9148 before merge: https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/pull/2196#discussion_r4080144047

A procedure parameter seeded by uniform literal callers remains non-escaping after the marker guard in var_escape/cfg_propagation/walker.rs, while SCCP preserves version-0 parameter seeds across Barrier. Thus `proc p {x} { missing_command; if {$x == 5} {...} }; p 5` can retain ConstantBranch(true), although real Tcl's autoloaded missing_command can mutate x through upvar 1.

The forward-only SSA clobber fix being developed alongside #2236/#2237 must cover seeded parameters/version-0 inputs as well as assigned locals. Preserve pre-barrier values for earlier uses and invalidate later reads, without fabricating executable calls/escape evidence. Add C Tcl 9-pinned regression and retained-safe control; final gates and Codex re-review required.

issues.title: The W210 `dict with` harvest's same-block literal fallback reads through an intervening `dict unset`
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
set d {a 1}
dict unset d a
dict with d {puts $a}
```

tclsh 8.5.19 through 9.1b0 raise `can't read "a": no such variable`: `dict with` binds only the keys the dictionary holds when it runs, and `a` was removed. Observed on branch `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42` at 3c6714b4 (and on `rust` before the lane's work): the analyser binds `a` from the literal `{a 1}` and reports no W210 on `puts $a`. The W210 harvest's same-block literal fallback reads the dictionary's last literal `set` in the block and never sees the `dict unset` between them; the lattice that knows the version the statement reads is widened by the `dict with` barrier, so the fallback is what answers.

## What is expected

The keys `dict with` binds are the keys of the dictionary's value *as it reaches the statement*: a lattice fact, or nothing. A literal fallback that skips intervening writes is not sound. Under the value-transfers contracts the structural plan for `dict with` (`docs/design/compiler/value-transfers.md` § Storage-writing commands, the `dict with` structural plan in slice 5 of the migration plan) takes the reaching value from the lattice and binds no key when the value is unknown; the existence rung (slice 8) is where the fallback retires.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/dataflow.rs` (the W210 harvest's `dict with` handling and its literal fallback).
- Witness: the program above under `tcl diag`, expecting W210 on `$a`, against every tclsh on `PATH`.

issues.title: `::tcl::dict::with` draws W002 and W211 under `tcl8.6` where `dict with` draws neither
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
set d {a 1}
::tcl::dict::with d {puts $a}
```

Observed on branch `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42` at 3c6714b4 with `tcl diag --dialect tcl8.6`: W002 ("disabled in the active dialect profile") on the head and W211 on `d`. The same program spelled `dict with d {puts $a}` draws neither. tclsh 8.6.18 runs both spellings identically (`::tcl::dict::with` is the ensemble's implementation command).

## Cause

The analyser reads the qualified spelling itself rather than resolving it to the `dict with` subcommand the registry knows: the availability check does not find the qualified name in the profile and the `dict with` handler (which reads the dictionary and binds its keys) does not run, so `d` looks unread.

## What is expected

The qualified spelling of an ensemble subcommand resolves to the same `ResolvedInvocation` as the ensemble form (the same defect family as #2233 for `tcl::dict::set`): one command, one availability answer, one handler. The resolution belongs in the registry's name resolution so every consumer sees it.

## Where

- `rust/tcl-registry/src/` (name resolution for `::tcl::dict::*` spellings) and `rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/` (the availability check and the `dict with` handler's dispatch).
- Related: #2233.

issues.title: `make rust-check` never runs the dialect-drift gate: `xtask-dialect-drift` sits after the `##` help comment on the `xtask-check` line, and 8 sites on `rust` fail it
issues.body:
## What happens

`make rust-check` (and therefore the PR gate it mirrors) passes on `rust`, while `cargo xtask dialect-drift` run directly reports eight sites:

```
dialect-drift: 8 site(s) give a document a second grammar. A document's grammar is resolved once at the ingress (dialect-profile-model.md §2.5) and threaded; a re-read of document text takes it from the nearest context. If the text is genuinely not the document's Tcl (a DSL, a manifest, a fixed literal), mark the line `// dialect-drift-ok: <reason>`:
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/codegen/control_flow.rs:236: let names = tcl_syntax::list::split_list(&args[variable_list_index].0).ok()?;
      -> splits document text under a fixed list grammar; go through tcl_syntax::word_rules::WordValueRules
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/command_binding.rs:2349: let Ok(elements) = tcl_syntax::list::split_list(lambda) else {
      -> splits document text under a fixed list grammar; go through tcl_syntax::word_rules::WordValueRules
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/compile_service.rs:125: config: LexerConfig::default(),
      -> re-lexes under the default grammar; take the config from the context (State::lexer_config / LexerConfig::for_profile / from_grammar)
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/lowering_hooks.rs:786: extract_single_expr_arg_with_config(text, aliases, "::", registry, None, LexerConfig::default())
      -> re-lexes under the default grammar; take the config from the context (State::lexer_config / LexerConfig::for_profile / from_grammar)
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/var_refs.rs:196: Self::with_config(options, LexerConfig::default())
      -> re-lexes under the default grammar; take the config from the context (State::lexer_config / LexerConfig::for_profile / from_grammar)
  rust/tcl-compiler/src/var_refs.rs:219: Self::with_config_and_cache_size(options, LexerConfig::default(), cache_size)
      -> re-lexes under the default grammar; take the config from the context (State::lexer_config / LexerConfig::for_profile / from_grammar)
  rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/refactor/extract_proc.rs:616: let Ok(names) = tcl_syntax::list::split_list(word) else {
      -> splits document text under a fixed list grammar; go through tcl_syntax::word_rules::WordValueRules
  rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/refactor/inline_proc.rs:472: let Ok(names) = tcl_syntax::list::split_list(word) else {
      -> splits document text under a fixed list grammar; go through tcl_syntax::word_rules::WordValueRules
```

(Observed at `9906d6af` on `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42`, which reports a ninth site of its own that the branch is fixing; `git blame` puts the eight above on `rust`: six from 59a855ae (#1754), one each from 62e39593 and 11267172.)

## Why

`Makefile` line 872 declares the prerequisites of `xtask-check` on one line and ends it with a `##` help comment:

```make
xtask-check: … xtask-c-api-ownership ## Rust-side check gates (docs index coverage + generated-table/catalog drift) xtask-dialect-drift
```

Make treats everything after `#` as a comment, so `xtask-dialect-drift` is part of the help text, not a prerequisite. The `xtask-dialect-drift` target itself (line 991) is correct and runs the gate when invoked by name; nothing invokes it. The word landed in that position in 922568ab (`fix(ci): preserve cargo smoke execution contracts`), so the gate has never run under `make rust-check` since it was added, and the eight sites accumulated unnoticed.

## Reproduction

```
grep -c 'xtask-dialect-drift' <(make -n xtask-check 2>/dev/null)   # 0
cargo xtask dialect-drift; echo exit=$?                             # 8 sites, exit=1
make rust-check; echo exit=$?                                       # exit=0
```

## Proposed fix

1. Move `xtask-dialect-drift` before the `##` on the `xtask-check` line (or onto its own `xtask-check: xtask-dialect-drift` line), and add a `check-*` self-test that parses the `xtask-check` prerequisite list with `make -n`/`make -p` and asserts every `xtask-*` target defined in the Makefile is reachable from `xtask-check`, so a comment cannot swallow a gate again.
2. Bring the eight sites under the rule before wiring the gate in, or the PR gate goes red on `rust`: the four `LexerConfig::default()` sites take the config from their context (`State::lexer_config` / `LexerConfig::for_profile` / `from_grammar`); the four `split_list` sites go through `tcl_syntax::word_rules::WordValueRules`, or carry a `// dialect-drift-ok: <reason>` waiver where the text is genuinely not the document's Tcl (the `lambda` body in `command_binding.rs` and the variable lists in the refactors are document text, so they need the real fix).

issues.title: hover.rs keeps a dead, test-only hover path that recognises `format`/`scan`/`regexp`/`regsub`/`clock` by whitespace-token spelling under a standing `#[allow(dead_code)]`
issues.body:
## What

`rust/tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs` carries a hover fallback that production no longer calls, kept alive only by its unit tests:

- `#[cfg(test)] #[allow(dead_code)] fn format_string_hover` (line 836–837), dead since `fbbc8b94` (2026-09-05) moved hover onto the registry-driven path;
- its helpers `sprintf_format_string_at_position` (1683; `if tokens[0] != "format" && tokens[0] != "scan"` at 1689), `binary_format_context_at_position` (2102), `#[allow(dead_code)] fn regex_pattern_at_position` (2716–2723; `matches!(tokens[0], "regexp" | "regsub")`), `clock_format_string_at_position` (2826), and a further `#[allow(dead_code)]` at 2463.

`grep -rn 'regex_pattern_at_position\|format_string_hover(' rust/tcl-lsp-core/src` finds no caller outside their definitions and the `#[cfg(test)]` module (tests at 4847–5236 exercise the helpers directly).

## Why it matters

- They split the source on whitespace and recognise commands by the spelling of `tokens[0]`, the pattern the value-transfer design retires everywhere else (a `::regexp` or `namespace import`ed spelling, a `{*}` prefix or a continuation line all defeat it); anyone reading hover.rs for how hover finds a format string is led to the wrong path.
- `#[allow(dead_code)]` is a standing waiver in a crate that otherwise builds under pedantic clippy with no allows; the gate cannot tell a new dead function from these.
- The registry-axes lint (`cargo xtask registry-axes`) skips them only because they sit past the file's first `#[cfg(test)]` item, which is the same scanning gap as the value-transfers lint's (`rust/xtask/src/value_transfers.rs` breaks at the first `#[cfg(test)]` line, function-level or not).

## Proposed fix

Delete `format_string_hover`, `regex_pattern_at_position` and the helpers with no production caller, and move any test that still pins wanted behaviour onto the production entry points (`hover` over a document with the registry) inside the `tests` module. Drop the `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes. If a helper is still wanted as a test utility, move it into the `tests` module rather than keeping it at module level behind `#[cfg(test)]`.

issues.title: `tcl_lexer::word_parts::decompose` scans an array index under the caller's substitution flags, where `Tcl_ParseVarName` always scans it with every kind
issues.body:
## What happens

`rust/tcl-lexer/src/word_parts.rs`'s `decompose` takes the `subst`-style flags (`-nobackslashes` / `-nocommands` / `-novariables`, line 143) and applies them to the whole word, including the components of an array index it recurses into (`VarRef::index: Option<Vec<WordPart>>`, lines 224–231). C Tcl's `Tcl_ParseVarName` (tclParse.c) scans the index of `$name(index)` with every substitution kind enabled regardless of the caller's flags: `subst -nocommands {$a([b])}` still runs `b` for the index, and only top-level `[…]` is left as text.

So under `-nocommands` the `[b]` in `$a([b])` comes back from `decompose` as literal text, while every release evaluates it as a command substitution:

```
% set b k; set a(k) v
% subst -nocommands {$a([b])}
v
```

(tclsh 8.4–9.1 all print `v`; `decompose` under the same flags yields a variable reference whose index is the text `[b]`, that is `a([b])`, an element that does not exist.)

## Where it bites

Every consumer that hands `decompose` a restricted flag set and then reads `VarRef::index`: the template-word plan (`rust/tcl-registry/src/value_transfer/template.rs`) rescans each index itself today to work around this (recorded as "found and left" in the value-transfers lane doc at VT5.8), the W101/W303 scans, and `tcl-vm`'s `subst` where it uses the decomposed form rather than the raw index span (`VarRefRaw::index`, lines 234–242, is the shape the VM's own index substitution needs and is unaffected).

## Proposed fix

Recurse into the index with `Flags::ALL` whatever the caller passed, matching `Tcl_ParseVarName`; keep the caller's flags for the top-level components only. Add a unit test in `word_parts.rs` for `$a([b])` and `$a($i)` under each restricted flag set, and a `tcl-vm` differential for `subst -nocommands {$a([b])}` and `subst -novariables {$a($i)}` against the oracle (`/root/.local/bin/tclsh8.4`…`9.1`). The template plan's own index rescan can then go.

issues.title: `namespace upvar`'s `otherVar` word carries no `ArgRole`, so every role-driven consumer is blind to the word that names the aliased cell
issues.body:
## What

`rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs` (the `upvar` sub-command, about lines 1196–1199) declares `NamespaceName` at position 0 and a strided `VarWrite` on each `myVar`, and nothing on each `otherVar`. The word that names the cell being aliased has no role, so every consumer that walks roles rather than spellings never sees it:

- semantic tokens and hover on `$v` in `namespace upvar ::mypkg $v local` classify it as a plain read, not a cell-naming word;
- SSA def/use records no use of `v` there;
- the rename safety tier's hazard scan (`rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/rename_safety.rs` about 723–800 walks `VarWrite`/`VarRead` only) does not see the word, and a rename of `::mypkg::version` is refused only because the workspace alias index records the computed cell separately (`WorkspaceVariableAlias`, `workspace_index.rs` about 634–641), which is a second mechanism doing the role's job.

## Reproduction

Two documents in one workspace:

```tcl
# a.tcl
namespace eval ::mypkg { variable version 1 }
puts $::mypkg::version
```

```tcl
# b.tcl
proc p {v} { namespace upvar ::mypkg $v local; return $local }
```

Rename `::mypkg::version` from `a.tcl`: no role-driven consumer reports `$v` in `b.tcl` as a hazard; only the alias index's ambiguous-cell record does (and that record depends on the analyser keeping the `::mypkg::$v` marker). `tcl symbols` / semantic tokens over `b.tcl` show `v` as an ordinary read.

## Why it is pre-existing

The role table has never had an `otherVar` entry (`git log -S'strided(VarWrite' -- rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs`); the consumer-contracts lane's step 2 (which retired the `NamespaceUpvar` analyser hook onto the state-transition resolver) neither added nor removed one, and `upvar`'s `otherVar` has the same gap.

## Proposed fix

Add a role for a word that names a variable cell without reading its value (a `VarCell`-shaped role, or reuse whichever role the design page assigns to `upvar`'s `otherVar`), declare it on `namespace upvar`'s and `upvar`'s `otherVar` positions (strided, alternating with the `VarWrite` locals), and have the alias index and the rename hazard scan read the role rather than the substitution marker. Pin with a semantic-token test over `namespace upvar ::mypkg $v local` and a rename-safety test where the hazard is found through the role alone.

issues.title: O126 deletes a store to the empty variable name `{}` when its only read is by name: `set {} 5; puts [set {}]` stops printing
issues.body:
## Summary

The SSA records `set {} 5` as a def of the empty variable name `""`, but it records no use for a by-name read of that name (`[set {}]`). The store therefore looks unused, and O126 deletes it. The rewritten program then fails with `can't read "": no such variable`.

`tcl opt --profile full` on `rust` (reproduced at 290f08d on the #2256 branch, whose changes do not reach this path):

| program | tclsh 8.6.18 | optimised | optimised under tclsh |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proc p {} {set {} 5; puts [set {}]}; p` | `5` | `proc p {} {; puts [set {}]}` | `can't read "": no such variable` |
| `proc p {} {set {} 5; puts "[set {}]"}; p` | `5` | `proc p {} {; puts "[set {}]"}` | `can't read "": no such variable` |
| `proc p {} {set {} 5; puts "${} [set {}]"}; p` | `5 5` | `proc p {} {; puts "5 [set {}]"}` | `can't read "": no such variable` |

The first two involve no other optimisation: O126 alone fires. In the third, O100 inlines `${}` (the `rust` scanner already did this), which leaves `[set {}]` as the only read. Codex found the third shape reviewing #2256.

## Where

`tcl explore --json` on the first program: statement 0 is `assign-const` with `defs: {"": {version 1, const(5)}}`, and statement 1 (`call puts [set {}]`) has `uses: {}`.

`ssa.rs` (the `for name in reads` loop that fills `found.by_name`, about line 1835) skips an empty name with `if name.is_empty() { continue; }`. Removing that skip alone does not restore the use, so the empty name is also lost earlier: either the nested substitution's name-role extraction never yields it, or `""` also stands for "no static name" there. A fix needs to tell the literal empty name (`{}` or `""` in a name role) apart from an unresolved one, and treat an unresolved name conservatively.

## Expected

A by-name read of `""` is a use of `""`, like any other name, and the store stays. Or, where the empty name cannot be modelled, a def of `""` is never reported dead.

issues.title: An `uplevel 0 {…}` body records no reads or writes, so O126 and O109 delete stores the body reads
issues.body:
## What happens

The SSA records nothing for the body of `uplevel 0 {…}` (an `UpFrame` at level 0, which runs the script in the current frame), so the dead-store passes see a store with no later use and remove it, and the rewritten program prints something else.

```tcl
proc p {} { set x 1; uplevel 0 {puts $x}; set x 2; return $x }
p
```

`tcl opt` (tcl8.6 profile) removes `set x 1` (O109, overwritten before read); tclsh 8.6.18 prints `1` then returns `2`, the rewritten program raises `can't read "x": no such variable` inside the `uplevel`.

```tcl
proc q {} { set x 1; uplevel 0 {info exists x} }
q
```

`set x 1` goes to O126 (unused variable); the original returns `1`, the rewrite `0`.

## Where

`uplevel 0` lowers to an `UpFrame` statement whose body is a script word; the script-body harvest that materialises reads and writes for `catch`/`if`/`foreach` bodies does not run over an `UpFrame` body, and the `UpFrame` itself only turns every place `MayBound` in the existence domain (value-transfers slice 8, `rust/tcl-compiler/src/sccp.rs`), which does not stop O126/O109 (they read SSA uses). Found during value-transfers slice 8 (VT8.5, `docs/design/lanes/value-transfers.md` row VT8.5 "Found and left"); the lane does not own `uplevel` bodies (the registry's `UpFrame` semantics and the frame-effect query are the consumer-contracts lane's, its step 2 `frame_effect`).

## Proposed fix

Lower an `uplevel` whose level word resolves to the current frame (`0`, or `#N` naming the current level) with its body walked as an ordinary nested script in the same frame, so its reads and writes reach the SSA (uses of the versions live at the `uplevel`, definitions after it); any other level keeps today's barrier. Witness: the two programs above print identically before and after `tcl opt` under tclsh 8.4–9.1, and `set x 1; uplevel 0 {puts $x}` draws no W211/O126.

issues.title: A nested `[unset x]` is recorded as a read but not as a kill, so O102 folds a later `$x` to the value the `unset` destroyed
issues.body:
## What happens

Value-transfers slice 8 (D167) records a nested `[unset x]` — in an argument, a value word, a condition or a `return` word — as an existence read of the version it observes (which correctly keeps the store it observes for O108/O109), but gives it no kill definition. A read of `x` after the statement therefore still sees the version the `unset` destroyed:

```tcl
proc p {} { set x 1; puts [unset x]; puts $x }
p
```

tclsh 8.4–9.1 print an empty line and then raise `can't read "x": no such variable`; `tcl opt` rewrites the second `puts $x` to `puts 1` (O102/O100), so the rewritten program prints `1` and exits 0.

The statement form `unset x` gets its kill definition (W213 and the existence rung read it); only the nested form is missing it.

## Where

`rust/tcl-compiler/src/ir_helpers.rs` (`variable_read_effects_from_commands` records the `DESTROYS_VARIABLE` target as a read) and the lowering that materialises a nested command's writes as a synthetic statement (the `LocalWrites`/`StatefulNested` path) — the unbind outcome (`ExistenceOutcome::Unbind`) of a nested command is not turned into a definition the way a nested `[incr x]`'s write is. Recorded as "Found and left" in `docs/design/lanes/value-transfers.md` (row VT8.5, D167); slice 9 (`LocalWrites`) admits nested *writes* in expressions and would be the natural place for the nested *unbind* too, but its item text does not name it.

## Proposed fix

When the lowering materialises a nested command whose transfer is an `Unbind` of a place, emit the same kill definition the statement form gets (the existence rung then reads `Unbound` after it, and W210 reports the later `$x` instead of O102 folding it). Witness: the program above prints the same before and after `tcl opt` (and both raise), `set x 1; puts [unset x]; puts $x` draws W210 on the second read.

issues.title: KCS feature note for the MCP server omits `spectcl_check` and `spectcl_expand` and has no gate tying its tool table to the tool catalogue
issues.body:
## What

`docs/kcs/features/kcs-feature-mcp-server.md` lists the MCP server's tools as one table row per tool, but `spectcl_check` and `spectcl_expand` (the pack-authoring tools in `rust/tcl-mcp/src/spectcl.rs`) have no row, and nothing enumerates a tool's arguments, so a new argument (the consumer-contracts lane's step 3 just added `tier`, `trust` and a `provenance` verdict to `spectcl_check`) changes nothing in the note.

`grep -n 'spectcl_check\|spectcl_expand' docs/kcs/features/kcs-feature-mcp-server.md` → no match; `grep -c '^| \`' docs/kcs/features/kcs-feature-mcp-server.md` → 25 rows against the `ToolDef` catalogue in `rust/tcl-mcp/src/tools.rs`.

`cargo xtask gen-ai-diagnostics --check` generates `ai/shared/diagnostics.json` from `DiagCode` only; no generator or drift check derives the note's table (or any doc) from the `ToolDef` catalogue, so the two drift silently.

## Proposed fix

Generate the tool table (name, one-line purpose, argument names with their enum values where the catalogue has them) from `ToolDef` into the note between markers, checked by the same `--check` mechanism the other generated catalogues use (`xtask gen-ai-diagnostics` or a sibling), and add the missing rows for `spectcl_check` (with `tier`, `trust`, and the `provenance` output) and `spectcl_expand`.

issues.title: W211 reports an array element as never used when a computed-key `info exists` observes it
issues.body:
## What happens

```tcl
proc p {k} { set a(x) 1; if {[info exists a($k)]} {puts yes} else {puts no} }
p x
```

`tcl diag` reports W211 "Variable 'a(x)' is set but never used"; tclsh prints `yes`, so the store is observed.

## Why

The registry's read projection names the array `a` for the computed-key existence read (`[info exists a($k)]`), and W211 counts uses per element: the element `a(x)` gets no use because the read names the whole array with an unknown key. O109 does not delete the store only because `dynamic_names.reads` disables it for a computed key (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/optimiser/elimination.rs` about line 572), so the diagnostic and the optimiser disagree about the same fact.

Found by the slice 8 review of the value-transfers lane (`rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/diagnostics/dataflow.rs`, the W211 harvest); likely pre-existing.

## Proposed fix

W211 treats a whole-array existence read (or any whole-array read: `array get a`, `array names a`, `[info exists a($k)]` with a computed key) as a use of every element of `a` that is bound at that point, the same rule O109 already applies through `dynamic_names.reads`. Witness: the program above draws no W211; `set a(x) 1; if {[info exists a(y)]} {…}` still draws it.

issues.title: tclvm: `interp alias` with a qualified alias name does not create the namespace, and the two-argument describe form is missing
issues.body:
## What happens

Two divergences from tclsh 8.4 through 9.1 in the VM's `interp alias`:

1. A qualified alias name whose namespace does not exist yet:

   ```tcl
   interp alias {} ::vendor::unpack {} lindex
   puts [namespace exists ::vendor]
   puts [::vendor::unpack {a b c} 1]
   ```

   Every tclsh prints `1` then `b` (the alias creation creates `::vendor`); the VM raises on the alias creation (or leaves the namespace absent so the qualified call fails to resolve).

2. The describe form `interp alias {} name` (two arguments after the sub-command) returns the target command and its prefix arguments in every tclsh:

   ```tcl
   interp alias {} ::vendor::unpack {} lindex
   puts [interp alias {} ::vendor::unpack]     ;# lindex
   ```

   The VM has no arm for it and reports a wrong-number-of-arguments error.

## Where

`rust/tcl-vm` (the `interp` builtin's `alias` arm). Found by the consumer-contracts lane while writing the rung-1 VM witness for `alias_of` (step 4, CC4.3/CC4.4), which had to create the namespace explicitly to proceed (recorded there as D4.14).

## Proposed fix

Create the qualified name's namespace on alias creation the way `proc ::a::b {} {}` does (Tcl's `Tcl_CreateAlias` goes through `Tcl_CreateObjCommand`, which creates intermediate namespaces), and add the describe form returning `{target prefix…}` with the `{}` interpreter paths handled as tclsh does. Differential witness under `/root/.local/bin/tclsh8.4`…`9.1` for both programs.

issues.title: An unscoped pack `-override` loses to a scoped shipped spec in every profile-aware lookup (`best_visible` prefers scoped specs)
issues.body:
## What happens

A pack command declared `command NAME -override` with no `dialects` row (unscoped) is meant to shadow the shipped command of that name. In every profile-aware lookup, however, `CommandRegistry`'s `best_visible` selection prefers a spec scoped to the active profile over an unscoped one, so the shipped spec — which carries a `dialects` scope — keeps winning and the override never answers.

Reproduction (a workspace pack):

```
command lindex -override
  arg list {kind: any}
  arg index {kind: int}
  evaluate -implementation vendor.lindex.v1
```

`tcl explore --dialect tcl8.6 --show registry lindex` (or any consumer resolving `lindex` under a profile) still reports the shipped spec; the override is reported only under a profile-less lookup. Adding a `dialects tcl8.6` row to the pack command makes it win, which is the workaround the consumer-contracts lane's rung-1 VM witness had to use (step 4, recorded there as D4.21).

## Where

`rust/tcl-registry/src/registry.rs` (`best_visible` / the visibility ordering used by `get_in_dialect` and `invocation`); the `-override` contract in `docs/design/registry/spec-packs.md` says an override shadows the shipped spec within the pack's tiers, and says nothing about needing a `dialects` row. This predates the consumer-contracts lane and is broader than codegen (hover, diagnostics and the optimiser all resolve through the same lookup).

## Proposed fix

Order candidates by provenance first (a pack override at an admitted tier beats the shipped spec) and by scope specificity second, or treat an unscoped `-override` as scoped to every profile the pack loads under. Pin with a registry test: an unscoped `-override` of `lindex` is what `get_in_dialect("lindex", tcl8.6)` returns, and a scoped one still is.

issues.title: tclvm: interp exists and issafe ignore nested interpreter paths
issues.body:
Found while validating safe-child inheritance (#2195) in the alias/package-autoload chunk. Taking this with #2193/#2269/#2195; use the existing shared interpreter-path resolver rather than direct-child lookup.

```tcl
interp create a
a eval {interp create -safe b}
puts [interp exists {a b}]
puts [catch {interp issafe {a b}} msg]
puts $msg
```

C Tcl 9.0.4 prints:
```
1
0
1
```

Bytecode VM on merged rust c2860edc (real init.tcl/tcltest.tcl) prints:
```
0
1
could not find interpreter "a b"
```

The child exists and can be evaluated through its parent; these two queries use direct-child-only helpers while resolve_interp_path already supports list paths. Preserve missing-path behavior, empty/current interpreter paths, safe/trusted controls and nested safe-child regressions. This is portable Tcl semantics; no test exclusions.

issues.title: tclvm: child interpreter commands lack alias and aliases subcommands
issues.body:
Found in original Tcl 9.0.4 interp.test (interp-7.1–7.6) while validating #2193/#2269. The parent `interp alias` API and child command alias API are separate entry points.

```tcl
interp create child
puts [child alias foo list]
puts [child aliases]
puts [child eval {foo x y}]
```

C Tcl 9.0.4 prints `foo`, `foo`, then `x y`. Merged rust c2860edc bytecode VM reports `bad option "alias"` / `bad option "aliases"`; its child-command option table omits both. Root reproduced each missing option using catch with real upstream init.tcl/tcltest.tcl.

Reuse the existing interpreter-arena alias/token/lifecycle owners and the pending #2269 alias introspection work. Cover create, describe, list, deletion, target prefix arguments, rename/token lifecycle, and nested child paths against C9. Do not duplicate alias state or add semantic skips. Related older architecture tracker #936 is closed; this is the remaining child-command API surface.

issues.title: tclvm: interp create treats a multi-component interpreter path as a literal child name
issues.body:
Found in the real Tcl 9.0.4 interp.test creation cases while validating alias and nested-path queries. The old arena/path architecture issue #936 is closed; #2273 fixes exists/issafe lookup only. Creation still needs correct path placement.

```tcl
interp create a
puts [interp create {a x2}]
puts [list [interp children a]]
puts [interp exists {a x2}]
```

C Tcl 9.0.4 prints:
```
a x2
x2
1
```

Merged rust c2860edc VM prints:
```
a x2
{}
1
```

The VM creates a direct child literally named `a x2`, rather than child `x2` beneath `a`; the old direct-child-only exists implementation masks the placement error. The shared list-path resolver used by the #2273 fix exposes it. This also blocks later nested alias/eval/delete cases in interp.test.

Resolve all parent path elements and create the final element under that parent through the existing lifecycle owner. Preserve one-element names containing spaces (proper Tcl list quoting), returned path spelling, missing-parent/duplicate errors, effective safety, child startup and rollback. Add original upstream creation cases and direct C9 regressions. No semantic exclusions.
